Tibet is also sometimes given this name.
At what age did the Holy Prophet Muhammad (SAW) lose his mother, Hazrat Aminah?
Hazrat Aminah died at Abwa while returning from Madinah, when the Prophet (SAW) was about 6 years old.
His grandfather Abdul Muttalib then looked after him until he died when the Prophet was 8.
What is the official capital of Indonesia?
Jakarta is Indonesia's legal capital. A new capital, Nusantara in East Kalimantan, was planned by a 2022 law, but Jakarta stays the capital until a formal transfer decree is issued.
Nusantara is now planned only as a political capital (target 2028), so candidates who wrote Nusantara in 2022 were anticipating a move that has not formally happened.
Which planet has the largest number of moons?
Saturn has the most confirmed moons of any planet, about 293 as of 2026. Jupiter is second with about 115.
Saturn's count was 83 in 2022 and rose sharply after new discoveries, so older answers differ.
How many wajibat of Namaz are there according to the Hanafi school?
The Hanafi school counts 14 wajibat of Namaz, such as reciting Surah Fatiha and a further surah.
The fard acts of Namaz are 13 in number.
What was the real (original) name of Titu Mir?
Titu Mir, the Bengali leader of the Barasat uprising, was born as Mir Nisar Ali.
He was killed in 1831 by British forces at his bamboo fort in Narkelbaria.
How many articles does the 1973 Constitution of Pakistan have?
The 1973 Constitution, Pakistan's third constitution, contains 280 articles.
It has 12 parts and 7 schedules and was enforced on 14 August 1973.
Rough is to smooth as crude is to what?
Rough and smooth are opposites, so the opposite of crude (unrefined) is polished (refined).
Crude oil is oil that has not yet been refined.
In which year was FATA merged into Khyber Pakhtunkhwa?
The 25th Constitutional Amendment was passed in May 2018 and merged FATA into Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, which was completed after the President signed it.
Candidates often confuse this with 2021, but the merger law was passed in 2018.
How old was the Holy Prophet (PBUH) when his grandfather Abdul Muttalib died?
The Prophet (PBUH) lost his mother at 6 and his grandfather Abdul Muttalib at about 8 years of age. His uncle Abu Talib then took care of him.
Abdul Muttalib was the chief of Quraish and the one who cared for him after his mother Amina died.
In which Hijri year did the Holy Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) perform his Hajj (the Farewell Hajj)?
The Prophet (PBUH) performed his only Hajj in 10 AH, and delivered the Last Sermon at Arafat during it.
Some sources mention that Hajj was made obligatory in 9 AH, and the Prophet passed away in 11 AH.
Which country is the largest gold producer in the world?
China has led world gold mine production for many years, with about 380 tonnes a year, ahead of Russia and Australia.
Candidates in 2022 also gave China, and it is still first in 2025 estimates.
What is the antonym of abhor?
To abhor means to hate strongly, so its opposite is to love or admire.
Loathe and detest are synonyms of abhor.
Aleem Dar is a famous umpire of which game?
Aleem Dar, from Lahore, is a famous Pakistani cricket umpire who stood in over 100 Test matches and won the ICC Umpire of the Year award three times in a row (2009-2011).
He served on the ICC Elite Panel of Umpires for many years.
Which bridge in Turkey connects Asia and Europe over the Bosphorus Strait?
The Bosphorus Bridge in Istanbul spans the Bosphorus Strait and joins the European and Asian sides of the city.
It was renamed 15 July Martyrs Bridge in 2016, and Istanbul has other Bosphorus bridges too.
Who is the President of China as of October 2026?
Xi Jinping has been President of China since 2013 and also leads the Communist Party.
The head of government, the Premier, is Li Qiang, so the office of PM is not held by Xi.
What is the height of the Diamer Bhasha Dam?
The Diamer Bhasha Dam on the Indus is 272 metres high, per WAPDA.
It is a roller-compacted concrete dam and one of the tallest of its kind in the world.
On which date did Muhammad Ali Bogra present the Bogra Formula?
Muhammad Ali Bogra presented his constitutional formula on 7 October 1953.
The formula was never implemented because the Constituent Assembly was dissolved in 1954.
What is the relation between Hazrat Musa (AS) and Hazrat Haroon (AS)?
Hazrat Haroon (AS) was the elder brother of Hazrat Musa (AS) and was also a prophet.
Musa (AS) asked Allah to make Haroon (AS) his helper, as mentioned in the Quran.
Which surah is called the heart of the Quran?
A hadith describes Surah Yaseen as the heart of the Quran.
Surah Yaseen is the 36th surah and has 83 verses.
According to Islamic tradition, who first built the Kaaba?

Islamic tradition says the Kaaba was first built by Hazrat Adam (AS), and later rebuilt by Hazrat Ibrahim (AS) with his son Ismail (AS). Many candidates and sources give this answer for the first building.
Sources differ, and some Pakistani textbooks credit Ibrahim and Ismail (AS) with building it, but they rebuilt it on its old foundations.
Which country is called the Land of the Rising Sun?
Japan is called the Land of the Rising Sun; its name Nippon means origin of the sun.
Vienna is the capital of which country?
Vienna is the capital and largest city of Austria on the Danube River.
Budapest, the capital of Hungary, is also on the Danube.
In which surah of the Quran is the name Ahmad (for the Holy Prophet PBUH) mentioned?
The name Ahmad appears in Surah As-Saff (61:6), where Hazrat Isa (AS) gives the good news of a messenger named Ahmad coming after him.
The name Muhammad is mentioned four times in the Quran, in Al-Imran, Al-Ahzab, Muhammad and Al-Fath.
How many articles did the 1956 Constitution of Pakistan have?
The 1956 Constitution, Pakistan's first constitution, had 234 articles.
It was enforced on 23 March 1956 and abrogated in October 1958.
Which is the last completely revealed surah of the Holy Quran?
Surah An-Nasr is regarded as the last complete surah to be revealed.
Sources differ about the last verse revealed, with Al-Baqarah verse 281 or Al-Maidah verse 3 often mentioned.
Which was the first ghazwa (expedition led personally by the Holy Prophet SAW) of Islam?
The first ghazwa, in Safar 2 AH, was Abwa, also called Waddan, in which the Prophet (SAW) himself went out but no fighting occurred.
The first major battle of Islam was Badr in Ramadan 2 AH.
What is the capital of South Korea?
Seoul is the capital and largest city of South Korea.
Pyongyang is the capital of North Korea.
Malaysia has a king instead of a president. Who is the head of state (Yang di-Pertuan Agong) of Malaysia in 2026?
Malaysia is a constitutional monarchy with no president. Sultan Ibrahim of Johor has been the 17th Agong since 31 January 2024.
His predecessor was Sultan Abdullah of Pahang, who was Agong from 2019 to 2024.
According to the 2023 census, about what percentage of Pakistan's population is Muslim?
The 2023 census recorded Muslims at about 96.35 percent of the population of Pakistan.
The 2017 census figure was 96.47 percent, and candidates often quote 97 percent.
About how many times is the command of Namaz (Salah) mentioned in the Holy Quran, according to common textbooks?
Salah and its related commands are repeated about 700 times in the Quran, showing its great importance.
Sources differ on the exact count, but 700 is the figure given in most Pakistani textbooks.
Which letter comes next in the series: B, E, J, Q, ?
The positions are 2, 5, 10, 17. The gaps are 3, 5, 7, so the next gap is 9 and 17 + 9 = 26, which is Z.
The positions are one more than the squares 1, 4, 9, 16, and 25 + 1 = 26.
What is the approximate total length of railway track in Pakistan?
Pakistan Railways reports about 11,881 track kilometres, counting all tracks including double-track sections.
The route length is shorter, about 7,791 km, which is why sources differ.
Who was the first civilian Chief Martial Law Administrator of Pakistan?
On 20 December 1971 Zulfiqar Ali Bhutto took over as President and became the first civilian Chief Martial Law Administrator after Yahya Khan stepped down.
Martial law was lifted in Pakistan in 1972 and the 1973 Constitution was adopted under Bhutto.
Amsterdam is the capital of which country?
Amsterdam is the constitutional capital of the Netherlands. The government sits in The Hague.
Brussels is the capital of Belgium.
Lima is the capital of which country?
Lima is the capital and largest city of Peru. It lies on the Pacific coast.
Santiago is the capital of Chile.
In which country are the headquarters of the Economic Cooperation Organization (ECO) located?
The ECO secretariat is in Tehran, the capital of Iran.
Pakistan, Iran and Turkey were the founding members of ECO.
In which year was the Al-Khalid main battle tank inducted into the Pakistan Army?
The Al-Khalid (MBT-2000), developed by Pakistan with Chinese cooperation, entered service with the Pakistan Army in 2001.
An upgraded Al-Khalid-I was first handed over to the Armoured Corps in July 2020.
Who is the Prime Minister of Israel?
Benjamin Netanyahu has been Prime Minister of Israel since December 2022 and was still in office in October 2026.
Naftali Bennett (2021-2022) was PM when candidates wrote in 2022, and Israel's next general election is scheduled for 27 October 2026.
What is the capital of the Netherlands?
Amsterdam is the constitutional capital of the Netherlands. The government and parliament sit in The Hague.
The International Court of Justice is located in The Hague.
In which year was Bengal partitioned by the British?
Lord Curzon partitioned Bengal in 1905 into East Bengal and Assam and the rest of Bengal.
In which constitution was the bicameral (two-house) legislature introduced in Pakistan?
The 1973 Constitution created a bicameral Parliament of the National Assembly and the Senate.
The Senate was first formed in 1973 and the 1956 and 1962 constitutions had one house.
In which year did Pakistan win the IBSF World Snooker Championship for the first time?
Muhammad Yousuf won the world amateur snooker title for Pakistan in 1994.
Muhammad Sajid won the world amateur title in 2006, Pakistan's second.
Who was the father of Hazrat Yousuf (AS)?
Hazrat Yousuf (AS) was the son of Hazrat Yaqub (AS), who was the son of Hazrat Ishaq (AS).
Hazrat Yaqub (AS) is also known as Israel.
Which one is different from the others: Circle, Square, Triangle, Angle?
Circle, square and triangle are closed geometric figures, while an angle is not a closed figure.
An angle is formed by two rays meeting at a common point.
Which country hosted the Olympic Games that were held in 2021 (the Tokyo Olympics, postponed from 2020)?
The Games named Tokyo 2020 were postponed because of COVID-19 and held in Tokyo, Japan, in July and August 2021.
The next Summer Olympics after Tokyo were held in Paris, France, in 2024.
What is the antonym of intimate (adjective)?
Intimate means close and familiar, so the opposite is distant.
Close, familiar and dear are synonyms of intimate.
Who is the President of Sri Lanka (as of October 2026)?
Anura Kumara Dissanayake won the September 2024 presidential election and took office as President.
Gotabaya Rajapaksa was President until 2022 and Ranil Wickremesinghe until 2024.
Between which two countries does the Line of Control (LOC) lie?
The Line of Control is the de facto military border dividing Indian-administered and Pakistan-administered Kashmir.
It was established by the Simla Agreement of 1972.
In which year was the North-West Frontier Province (NWFP) renamed as Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KPK)?
The 18th Amendment, passed in April 2010, renamed NWFP as Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. Some candidates recall 2008, but that is not correct.
Before the renaming, the province was called NWFP from the British period.
Who recited verses of the Quran in the court of King Najashi of Abyssinia?
Hazrat Jafar (RA) led the Muslim migrants to Abyssinia and recited the opening verses of Surah Maryam before Najashi. The king was moved and refused to hand the Muslims over to Quraish.
Hazrat Jafar (RA) is also known as Jafar Tayyar and was martyred at the Battle of Mutah.
Which was the second major battle (ghazwa) fought between the Muslims and the Quraish of Makkah, after the Battle of Badr?
The Battle of Badr in 2 AH was the first major battle of Islam and the Battle of Uhud in 3 AH was the second.
The Battle of Uhud was fought near Mount Uhud, close to Madinah, in Shawwal 3 AH.
On what date did the Australian cricketer Shane Warne die?
Shane Warne died of a suspected heart attack in Koh Samui, Thailand, on 4 March 2022 at the age of 52.
Warne took 708 wickets in Test cricket, a record for a leg-spinner.
The Shimla Agreement between Pakistan and India was signed after which war?
After the 1971 war and the separation of East Pakistan, Pakistan and India met at Shimla in 1972 and signed the agreement.
The 1966 Tashkent Declaration was signed after the 1965 war.
Vehicle is to wheel as sound is to what?
A vehicle moves by means of wheels, and sound travels by means of waves.
Sound needs a medium such as air, water or a solid to travel as waves.
In which country was the FIFA World Cup 2022 held?
The 2022 FIFA World Cup was hosted by Qatar from November to December 2022.
Argentina won the tournament, beating France in the final on penalties.
Which city is known as the City of Gold?
Johannesburg in South Africa is called the City of Gold because it grew after gold was discovered in the Witwatersrand in 1886.
South Africa has long been one of the largest gold producers in the world, though sources differ on later rankings.
Which plant is commonly named as the fastest growing plant (tree) in the world?
Some bamboo species can grow almost one metre in a single day, which is why bamboo is commonly named the fastest growing plant.
Bamboo is technically a grass, and the Paulownia is often called the fastest growing true tree, so sources differ.
About what percentage of Antarctica is covered by ice?
About 98 percent of Antarctica is covered by an ice sheet, and only about 2 percent is bare rock. Some sources give 97.6 or 99 percent.
The ice sheet is on average about 2 km thick.
On which date is the International Day to Combat Islamophobia observed?
The UN General Assembly proclaimed 15 March as International Day to Combat Islamophobia in 2022, on a resolution moved by Pakistan on behalf of the OIC.
15 March was chosen as the anniversary of the 2019 Christchurch mosque attacks.
Which companion (Sahabi) of the Holy Prophet (PBUH) is mentioned by name in the Quran?
Only Hazrat Zaid bin Haritha (RA) is named in the Quran, in Surah Al-Ahzab, verse 37. Other great companions are referred to without their names.
Abu Bakr (RA) is referred to as Sani-ithnain (second of the two) in Surah At-Tawbah.
Who is the Pakistani Nobel Prize winner in Physics, and how many Pakistanis have won a Nobel Prize in Physics?
Dr. Abdus Salam shared the 1979 Nobel Prize in Physics for work on the electroweak theory. He is the only Pakistani to win a Nobel in Physics.
Pakistan's other Nobel laureate is Malala Yousafzai (Peace, 2014).
The Khyber Pass connects Peshawar with which city of Afghanistan?
The Khyber Pass links Peshawar (Pakistan) with Kabul through the Torkham border crossing and Jalalabad.
The pass lies in the Safed Koh range.
What is the population of Pakistan according to the 2023 census?
The 2023 digital census recorded Pakistan's population as about 241.49 million.
The 2017 census had recorded about 207.7 million, and candidates in 2022 used estimates of about 220 million.
Who is the President of the United States?
Donald Trump is the 47th President of the USA, in office since January 2025.
Joe Biden, named by candidates in 2022, was president from 2021 to 2025.
Which was the first private television channel of Pakistan?
Shalimar Television Network, which began in 1990 as People's Television Network, was the first channel to break the monopoly of state-run PTV. It is the answer most textbooks give.
Sources differ on the word private: ARY Digital (2001) and Indus TV (2000) are often called the first fully independent channels.
Who was the first poet of the Punjabi language?
Hazrat Baba Fariduddin Ganjshakar (1188-1266) is regarded as the first poet of Punjabi, and his verses appear in the Guru Granth Sahib.
A quadratic equation is an equation of which degree?
The highest power of the variable in a quadratic equation is 2, so it is a second degree equation.
The general form is ax squared plus bx plus c equals 0, where a is not 0.
Hazrat Sara (RA), the wife of Hazrat Ibrahim (AS), was the mother of which prophet?
Hazrat Sara was the wife of Hazrat Ibrahim (AS) and gave birth to Hazrat Ishaq (AS) in her old age.
Hazrat Ismail (AS) was the son of Hazrat Hajra (RA), and Hazrat Yaqub (AS) was the son of Hazrat Ishaq (AS).
In which year was SUPARCO, the Pakistan Space and Upper Atmosphere Research Commission, established?
SUPARCO was formally established on 16 September 1961 by an executive order, with Dr Abdus Salam as its first chairman.
Some sources trace a precursor committee to 1961 as well; candidate answers such as 1955 and 1959 are incorrect.
If 1 man writes 5 papers in 5 minutes, how long will 1 man take to write 1 paper?
5 papers take 5 minutes, so 1 paper takes 5 / 5 = 1 minute.
A rate of 1 paper per minute means that 60 papers would take an hour.
According to the 1956 Constitution, what was the minimum age to become President of Pakistan?
The 1956 Constitution required the President to be a Muslim of not less than 40 years of age.
Some candidates remembered 45, but 40 is the age given in the Constitution of 1956.
If the 4th day of a month is Friday, what day will the 19th be?
From the 4th to the 19th is 15 days. 15 days is 2 full weeks plus 1 day(s), so the day is 1 day(s) after Friday, which is Saturday.
Dates that are 7 days apart always fall on the same weekday, so only the remainder after dividing the gap by 7 matters.
If the 4th day of a month is Tuesday, what day will the 26th be?
From the 4th to the 26th is 22 days. 22 days is 3 full weeks plus 1 day(s), so the day is 1 day(s) after Tuesday, which is Wednesday.
Dates that are 7 days apart always fall on the same weekday, so only the remainder after dividing the gap by 7 matters.
What is the antonym of sublime?
Sublime means of very high excellence or beauty, so its opposite is ridiculous or lowly.
Magnificent, grand and noble are close in meaning to sublime.
On which side of Pakistan does the Arabian Sea lie?
Pakistan's coastline of about 1,046 km runs along the Arabian Sea in the south, in Sindh and Balochistan.
Iran and Afghanistan lie to the west, China to the north-east and India to the east.
In which province and city is the BRT (Zu Peshawar) transport system located?
The BRT Zu Peshawar is a bus rapid transit system of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. It serves the city of Peshawar.
Lahore has the Orange Line Metro Train and Metro Bus, which are different projects.
Which country is the current men's Hockey World Cup champion (2026 edition)?
Germany beat Spain 1-0 in the final on 30 August 2026 in Wavre, Belgium, to retain the title.
Belgium won the 2018 World Cup, and Germany won in 2023; Pakistan has four titles, the same as Germany.
In how many years was the revelation of the Holy Quran completed?
The Quran was revealed gradually to the Prophet (PBUH) over about 23 years, from the first revelation in Hira until shortly before his death.
About 13 years of this period were in Makkah and about 10 years in Madinah.
Which of the following countries lies in both Europe and Asia?
Turkey is divided by the Bosphorus strait, with a small part in Europe and most of its land in Asia.
Istanbul is the major city that lies on both continents.
What is the derivative of sin x with respect to x?
The standard derivative of sin x is cos x.
The derivative of cos x is -sin x.
In which year was the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor (CPEC) agreement signed and launched?
CPEC was launched in April 2015 when Chinese President Xi Jinping visited Pakistan and agreements worth about 46 billion dollars were signed.
A preliminary MoU on the corridor had been signed in 2013 during the visit of Premier Li Keqiang, which is why some sources give 2013.
Who is the current President of India?
Droupadi Murmu took oath as the 15th President of India on 25 July 2022.
Her predecessor Ram Nath Kovind, the answer given in 2022, served from 2017 to 2022.
Which country hosted the extraordinary session of the OIC Council of Foreign Ministers on the Afghan crisis in December 2021?
Pakistan hosted the 17th Extraordinary Session of the OIC Council of Foreign Ministers in Islamabad on 19 December 2021 to discuss the Afghan humanitarian crisis.
The 47th regular CFM was held in Niamey, Niger, in November 2020.
Who is the Prime Minister of Israel (as of October 2026, before the 27 October election)?
Benjamin Netanyahu has led Israel's government since December 2022, and he is campaigning for the election due on 27 October 2026.
Candidates in 2022 wrote Naftali Bennett, who was PM from June 2021 to June 2022, followed by Yair Lapid.
Which country has the largest number of lakes in the world?
Canada has the most lakes in the world, with several hundred thousand, more than the rest of the world combined by most estimates.
Finland is known as the land of a thousand lakes but has far fewer lakes than Canada.
Which is the longest river lying entirely within Afghanistan?
The Helmand River, about 1,150 km long, is the longest river that flows wholly in Afghanistan.
The Amu Darya forms part of the northern border with Central Asia, so it is not counted as entirely Afghan; some sources differ.
How many Madni surahs are there in the Holy Quran according to the common Pakistani textbook count?
The Quran has 114 surahs, of which 86 are Makki and 28 are Madni.
Madni surahs were revealed after the Hijrat to Madina.
What is the third letter of the word MANAGEMENT?
The letters in order are M, A, N, A, G, E, M, E, N, T. The third letter is N.
Whose motto is Faith, Unity, Discipline?
Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah gave the motto Faith, Unity, Discipline (Iman, Ittehad, Tanzeem) to the nation.
It is the national motto of Pakistan.
Hazrat Muaz bin Jabal (RA) was appointed governor of which place by the Holy Prophet (PBUH)?
The Holy Prophet (PBUH) sent Hazrat Muaz bin Jabal (RA) to Yemen as governor and teacher.
He was known as the most knowledgeable Companion about halal and haram.
Which letter comes next in the series: L, M, N, ?
The letters are in alphabetical order, so O follows N.
L, M, N, O are the 12th to 15th letters of the alphabet.
On which date was the Pakistan-China border agreement signed?
Pakistan and China signed the border agreement in Beijing on 2 March 1963, fixing the boundary between Gilgit-Baltistan and Xinjiang.
Pakistan and China established diplomatic relations on 21 May 1951.
Who is the chairman of the Pakistan Peoples Party (PPP)?
Bilawal Bhutto Zardari has been PPP chairman since 2007 and was re-elected in April 2025.
Asif Ali Zardari is the co-chairperson of the party.
What is the boundary line between Pakistani Punjab and Indian Punjab called?
The Radcliffe Line was drawn by Sir Cyril Radcliffe in 1947 to divide Punjab and Bengal between Pakistan and India.
The Radcliffe Award was announced on 17 August 1947.
Who started the Reshmi Rumal (Silk Letters) Movement?

The Reshmi Rumal Tehreek was organised by Maulana Ubaidullah Sindhi together with Shaikh-ul-Hind Maulana Mahmud Hasan of Deoband. Secret messages were written on silk cloth to seek help against British rule.
The plot was discovered in 1916 and Maulana Mahmud Hasan was imprisoned in Malta.
The Suez Canal separates Africa from which continent?
The Suez Canal in Egypt separates the African mainland from the Sinai Peninsula, which is part of Asia. It also joins the Mediterranean Sea to the Red Sea.
What is the last letter of the meaningful word formed by arranging the letters UTYEAB?
The letters UTYEAB can be arranged to form the word BEAUTY, whose last letter is Y.
The word BEAUTY is made of six letters, three of which (E, A, U) are vowels.
Who abrogated the 1962 constitution of Pakistan?
President Ayub Khan resigned in March 1969 and handed power to army chief General Yahya Khan, who abrogated the constitution.
Who is the President of the United States in October 2026?
Donald Trump won the 2024 election and was sworn in as the 47th President on 20 January 2025.
Joe Biden was President from January 2021 to January 2025, which is the answer candidates gave in 2022; the USA has a President and no Prime Minister.
What is the antonym of applaud?
To applaud is to show approval or praise, so its opposite is to criticize or condemn.
Praise, cheer and admire are synonyms of applaud.
Bashar al-Assad was the president of which country?
Bashar al-Assad ruled Syria from 2000 until his government fell in December 2024.
He succeeded his father Hafez al-Assad, who ruled Syria from 1971 to 2000.
Who was the first woman Governor of the State Bank of Pakistan?
Shamshad Akhtar became the first woman Governor of the State Bank of Pakistan in 2005.
She later served as Caretaker Finance Minister in 2023.
Who was the first Governor of the State Bank of Pakistan?
Zahid Hussain was the first Governor of the State Bank of Pakistan, appointed in 1948.
The bank was inaugurated by Quaid-e-Azam on 1 July 1948.
What was the code name of Pakistan's first nuclear tests conducted on 28 May 1998?
Pakistan's first set of nuclear tests in the Chagai Hills on 28 May 1998 was code-named Chagai-I.
The second test on 30 May 1998 was code-named Chagai-II, and 28 May is observed as Youm-e-Takbeer.
On which date was the Lahore Declaration signed by the prime ministers of Pakistan and India?
Nawaz Sharif and Atal Bihari Vajpayee signed the Lahore Declaration on 21 February 1999 during Vajpayee's bus visit to Lahore.
Months later the Kargil conflict broke out in 1999.
One degree of angle is equal to how many minutes?
One degree is divided into 60 minutes, and one minute into 60 seconds.
Demise means death or end, so its opposite is birth or beginning.
Death, end and collapse are all synonyms of demise.
Which desert is located in Sindh?
The Thar Desert, also called the Great Indian Desert, is in the Tharparkar region of Sindh and is the largest desert of Sindh.
Thar is also home to the largest coal reserves of Pakistan.
Who is the President of Israel?
Isaac Herzog was elected the 11th President of Israel in June 2021 and is still in office.
His predecessor was Reuven Rivlin, and the presidency is largely ceremonial.
Which were the national languages of Pakistan under the 1956 Constitution?
The 1956 Constitution declared Urdu and Bengali as the state languages of Pakistan. English was to continue as an official language for a period.
The 1962 Constitution kept Urdu and Bengali, and the 1973 Constitution made Urdu the only national language.
LOC stands for Line of Control, the ceasefire line in Kashmir between India and Pakistan.
It began as the 1949 Ceasefire Line and was renamed after the 1972 Simla Agreement.
How many members does SAARC have?
SAARC has eight members: Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Maldives, Nepal, Pakistan and Sri Lanka. Afghanistan joined as the eighth member in 2007.
SAARC began in 1985 with seven founding members, and its secretariat is in Kathmandu.
In which city is Mughalpura (famous for its railway workshops) located?
Mughalpura is an area of Lahore and is known for its large railway workshops and station.
Lahore Junction is the main railway station of the city.
Which Sahabi narrated the largest number of Ahadith?
Hazrat Abu Huraira (RA) narrated about 5,374 Ahadith, the highest number among the Companions.
He is known as Abu Huraira, meaning father of the kitten.
NASA, the space agency, belongs to which country?
NASA stands for the National Aeronautics and Space Administration, a United States government agency.
NASA was founded in 1958 and landed the first humans on the Moon in 1969.
On which date did the partition of Bengal take effect?
The partition of Bengal came into effect on 16 October 1905.
Muslims celebrated it, while Hindus observed the day as a day of mourning.
Which planet is nearest to the Sun?
Mercury orbits closest to the Sun, at about 58 million km.
Mercury is also the smallest planet of the solar system.
Which city lies on the border of Punjab and Sindh?
Mithankot, in Rajanpur district, lies at the southern tip of Punjab near the Sindh border.
Mithankot is close to where the Panjnad river joins the Indus.
What is a quarter of 1/3 of 120?
1/3 of 120 is 40. A quarter of 40 is 40 divided by 4, which equals 10.
A quarter of 1/3 is 1/12, so the answer is 120 divided by 12.
Who is the Prime Minister of Russia?
Mikhail Mishustin has been Prime Minister of Russia since January 2020, and he remains in office as of October 2026.
His predecessor as Prime Minister was Dmitry Medvedev.
In which year was the South East Asia Treaty Organization (SEATO) formed through the Manila Pact?
SEATO was formed by the Manila Pact signed on 8 September 1954 in Manila, Philippines.
Pakistan joined SEATO in 1954 and the organisation was dissolved in 1977.
How many senses do human beings have according to the traditional classification?
The five senses are sight, hearing, smell, taste and touch.
Modern science recognises additional senses such as balance and body position awareness.
Tamed means made gentle and under control, so its opposite is wild or untamed.
Domesticated is a synonym of tamed.
After which event did Hazrat Khalid bin Waleed (RA) accept Islam?
Khalid bin Waleed (RA), who fought against Muslims at Uhud, accepted Islam after the Treaty of Hudaibiya in 7 AH.
He is known as Saifullah, the Sword of Allah.
The White House in Washington, D.C. is the official residence and workplace of whom?
The President of the United States
The Chief Justice of the US
The White House is the official residence and main workplace of the President of the United States.
The official residence of the US Vice President is the Naval Observatory, not the White House.
In a class of 1500 students, 1200 are boys. What percentage of the students are girls?
The percentage of boys in this class is 80%, and the two percentages always add up to 100%.
Out of 1500 students, 1300 are present. What percentage of the students are absent (to two decimal places)?
The percentage present is 86.67%, which together with 13.33% makes 100%.
Which is the third largest city of Pakistan by population?
By population Karachi is first, Lahore second and Faisalabad third, in both the 2017 and 2023 censuses.
What is the apex court of Pakistan called?
The Supreme Court of Pakistan is the highest court of the country and its final court of appeal.
The Supreme Court sits in Islamabad.
What is the antonym of autonomy?
Autonomy means self-rule, so its opposite is dependence, being controlled by others.
Synonyms of autonomy include independence and self-government.
Point out the odd one out: Wheat, Hay, Rice, Barley.
Wheat, rice and barley are food grains (cereals) eaten by people, while hay is dried grass kept as fodder for animals.
Wheat and rice are the two major food crops of Pakistan.
Who benefited from the Partition of Bengal in 1905?
The partition created a Muslim-majority province of East Bengal and Assam with Dhaka as its capital, which helped Muslims in education and jobs.
Hindus opposed it strongly and it was annulled in 1911.
The Bus Rapid Transit (BRT) project, Zu Peshawar, was built by which government?
The Peshawar BRT was started in 2017 by the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa provincial government under Chief Minister Pervez Khattak. It runs in Peshawar, the provincial capital.
The Peshawar BRT was formally inaugurated on 13 August 2020 and has a corridor of about 27.5 km.
What is the capital of China?
Beijing is the capital of the People's Republic of China.
Shanghai is China's largest city, but not its capital.
What is the value of cot 90 degrees?
Tan 90 is undefined because cos 90 is 0.
In which year was the Sui gas field in Balochistan discovered?
Natural gas was discovered at Sui in Balochistan in 1952 and supply started in 1955.
Sui is the largest natural gas field of Pakistan by output historically.
On what date did Operation Radd-ul-Fasaad start?
The Pakistan Army launched Operation Radd-ul-Fasaad on 22 February 2017 against terrorism after a wave of attacks. It was a nationwide operation.
Operation Zarb-e-Azb in 2014 was an earlier operation in North Waziristan.
In which year did the Urdu-Hindi controversy begin?
The Urdu-Hindi controversy began in 1867 at Banaras (Varanasi), when Hindus demanded Hindi in Devanagari script replace Urdu.
The controversy led Sir Syed Ahmad Khan to conclude Hindus and Muslims could not progress together.
How many sugar mills did Pakistan have at the time of independence in 1947?
Most colonial-era sugar mills lay on the Indian side of the border, and Pakistan inherited only two.
The first new sugar mill after independence was set up at Tando Muhammad Khan in Sindh in 1961.
Habba Khatoon was a famous poetess of which language?
Habba Khatoon was a 16th century Kashmiri poetess, known as the Nightingale of Kashmir.
She was the wife of Yusuf Shah Chak, the last independent Muslim ruler of Kashmir.
Lat, Manat and Uzza were what?
Lat, Manat and Uzza were the three chief idols worshipped by the pagan Arabs before Islam.
The Quran mentions them in Surah An-Najm.
Which is the latest confirmed fighter jet inducted by the Pakistan Air Force?
The Chinese-made J-10C multirole fighter was inducted by the PAF in March 2022 and is the latest confirmed fighter type.
Reports about the Chinese J-35 stealth fighter for Pakistan remain unconfirmed.
What was the old name of Makkah?
Makkah was also called Bakkah, a name mentioned in Surah Al-Imran.
Madina was earlier known as Yathrib.
In which city of Pakistan was the first Metro Bus service inaugurated?
The Metro Bus Service was inaugurated in Lahore in February 2013. It runs between Gajju Matta and Shahdara.
Rawalpindi-Islamabad followed in 2015 and Multan in 2017.
What is the multiplicative inverse of 0.01?
Which army operation launched in February 2017 is a nationwide counter-terrorism operation of the Pakistan Army?
Operation Radd-ul-Fasaad was launched in February 2017 to eliminate the remaining threat of terrorism across the country.
Operation Azm-e-Istehkam was announced in 2024 as a further counter-terrorism campaign.
Who was the first Pakistani woman to take 100 wickets in One Day Internationals?
Sana Mir reached 100 ODI wickets in February 2017 during the Women's World Cup Qualifier against Bangladesh in Colombo.
Sana Mir was inducted into the ICC Hall of Fame and finished with about 150 ODI wickets.
Which elements are found in the first period of the periodic table?
The first period has only one shell, which can hold two electrons, so it contains just hydrogen (H) and helium (He).
The second period begins with lithium and ends with neon.
In which year was the film Jinnah released?
The biographical film Jinnah, starring Christopher Lee as Jinnah, was released in 1998. It was directed by Jamil Dehlavi.
The film's screenplay was written by Akbar Ahmed and Jamil Dehlavi.
By what other name is the Pakistan Resolution known?
The Pakistan Resolution of 1940 was passed at Lahore, so it is also called the Lahore Resolution. It demanded independent states for the Muslims of India.
The Allahabad Address of 1930 by Allama Iqbal first outlined the idea of a Muslim state.
Which country developed the Sinovac COVID-19 vaccine (CoronaVac)?
Sinovac Biotech is a Chinese company in Beijing that developed the CoronaVac vaccine.
Pakistan used Sinovac, Sinopharm and CanSinoBIO (all Chinese) vaccines widely in its COVID-19 campaign.
Stagnant means not flowing or moving, as in stagnant water. Its opposite is flowing.
Stagnant can also describe an economy that is not growing.
In football, what did BPL originally stand for in the English league?
The English top division was sponsored by Barclays from 2001 to 2016 and was called the Barclays Premier League (BPL). Today it is simply the Premier League.
BPL also stands for the Bangladesh Premier League in cricket.
Which title of Hazrat Muhammad (PBUH) is mentioned in the Quran as a mercy for all the worlds?
The Quran in Surah Al-Anbiya says that the Prophet was sent as a mercy for all the worlds, hence the title Rahmatul lil Alameen.
Other Quranic titles include Khatam-un-Nabiyyin and Siraj-e-Munir.
What does the word venerate mean?
To venerate is to regard someone or something with deep respect and reverence. Its synonyms are revere and honour.
The adjective venerable describes a person worthy of great respect, often because of age or wisdom.
Who was the Viceroy of India at the time of the Partition of Bengal in 1905?
Lord Curzon was Viceroy from 1899 to 1905 and announced the partition of Bengal in 1905.
The partition was annulled in 1911 under Lord Hardinge.
Which of the following vitamins is NOT water soluble?
Vitamins A, D, E and K are fat soluble and do not dissolve in water. The B vitamins and vitamin C are water soluble.
Fat soluble vitamins can be stored in the body, while water soluble ones are mostly excreted.
A man walks 20 km in 1 hour and 40 minutes. How much time will he take to cover 1 km?
1 hour 40 minutes = 100 minutes. Time for 1 km = 100 / 20 = 5 minutes.
His speed is 20 km in 100 minutes, which is 12 km per hour.
Where is Pakistan's largest railway workshop, the Mughalpura Workshop, located?
The Mughalpura Railway Workshop is in Lahore and is the largest railway workshop in Pakistan.
It was established in 1913 and repairs and builds railway coaches and wagons.
Which battle of the Muslims, fought in 3 AH, is counted as the second major battle after Badr?
The major battles in order are Badr (2 AH), Uhud (3 AH) and Khandaq (5 AH), so Uhud is the second.
Sources differ: early chronologies also list small expeditions such as Abwa and Buwat before Badr.
Who abrogated the 1956 constitution of Pakistan?
President Iskander Mirza abrogated the 1956 constitution on 7 October 1958 and imposed martial law.
Ayub Khan, the army chief, removed Iskander Mirza only 20 days later.
How many votes in the 342-member National Assembly are needed to pass a no-confidence motion against the Prime Minister?
A no-confidence resolution needs a majority of the total membership of the House. Half of 342 is 171, so 172 votes are needed.
Article 95 of the Constitution deals with the vote of no confidence against the Prime Minister.
What is cos(90 degrees - x) equal to?
By the complementary angle identity, cos(90 - x) = sin x.
In which province of Pakistan is the Reko Diq mine project located?
Reko Diq is a large copper and gold deposit in Chagai district in the west of Balochistan.
Reko Diq is one of the largest undeveloped copper-gold deposits in the world.
In a village the population in 2000 was 4600 and it doubles every five years. What was the population in 1995?
Going back five years halves the population: 4600 / 2 = 2300.
Population in 2005 would be 9200 at the same rate.
In which year was the ECO (Economic Cooperation Organization) formed in its present form?
ECO was re-established in 1985 by Pakistan, Iran and Turkey as the successor of RCD.
Six Central Asian states and Afghanistan joined in 1992.
FATF is the Financial Action Task Force, an international body that sets standards against money laundering and terror financing.
Pakistan was placed on the FATF grey list in June 2018 and removed in October 2022.
What is the closest meaning of the word 'forestall'?
To forestall means to prevent something from happening by taking action ahead of time.
Forestall is often confused with forest but has no connection with trees.
Which country occupies the Golan Heights?
Israel captured the Golan Heights from Syria in the Six-Day War of 1967. It has held the area since then.
The Golan Heights overlook the Sea of Galilee and the Jordan valley.
Who was the first Hafiz of the Holy Quran?
The Quran was revealed to the Holy Prophet (PBUH), who memorised it first, so he is called the first Hafiz.
Among the Companions, Hazrat Ali, Ubayy bin Kab and Zaid bin Thabit were also famous Huffaz.
Which country hosted the FIFA Football World Cup in 2022?
The 2022 FIFA World Cup was held in Qatar from 20 November to 18 December 2022. It was the first World Cup held in an Arab and Muslim country.
Argentina won the 2022 final against France on penalties.
Which layer of the Earth is the hottest?
Temperature rises with depth, and the inner core is the hottest part of the Earth, at about 5000 to 6000 degrees Celsius. The crust is the coolest solid layer.
The inner core is solid because of the enormous pressure, even though it is so hot.
Who is the angel in charge of Jahannam (Hell), often called its keeper?
Malik is the angel appointed as the keeper (Daroga) of Jahannam, and he is mentioned in Surah Az-Zukhruf.
Ridwan is the angel who is the keeper of Jannah.
How many times did Jansher Khan win the World Open squash title?
Jansher Khan won the World Open squash championship eight times between 1987 and 1996.
He also won the British Open six times, while Jahangir Khan won the World Open six times.
Who was the king (Najashi) of Habsha (Abyssinia) who gave shelter to the Muslim migrants?
The Christian king of Abyssinia, known by the title Najashi (Negus), was Ashama ibn Abjar. He protected the early Muslims who migrated there.
Abraha was the Abyssinian governor of Yemen who marched against the Kaaba in the Year of the Elephant.
KRL stands for Khan Research Laboratories, named after Dr Abdul Qadeer Khan. It is located at Kahuta.
It was originally set up in 1976 as the Engineering Research Laboratories and renamed in 1981.
What is the legislature of Pakistan called?
Pakistan's federal legislature is the Majlis-e-Shura (Parliament), made up of the President, the National Assembly and the Senate.
India's lower house is called the Lok Sabha.
In which region of Pakistan is the Neelum Valley and the Neelum River located?
The Neelum Valley and the Neelum River lie in Azad Jammu and Kashmir.
The river flows through Muzaffarabad and joins the Jhelum, and its capital valley town is Athmuqam.
Ali is 5 years old and his sister is three times his age. How old will his sister be when Ali is 10 years old?
The sister is 15 years old when Ali is 5, so she is 10 years older than him. When Ali is 10, she is 10 + 10 = 20 years old.
The age difference between two people always stays the same.
In which city is Ayub National Park located?
Ayub National Park is a large public park on Murree Road in Rawalpindi, named after President Ayub Khan.
It has a lake, a zoo-like area and recreation facilities for families.
Who developed the first successful inactivated (injectable) polio vaccine?
Jonas Salk developed the first effective inactivated polio vaccine, which was announced as safe and effective in 1955.
Albert Sabin later developed the oral polio vaccine, which is the one used in drops in Pakistan.
What is the meaning of the word prescribe?
To recommend or order as a remedy or rule
To prescribe means to advise or order something, such as a medicine or a rule. Its synonyms include recommend, advise and ordain.
A doctor writes a prescription to prescribe medicine.
Jabal-e-Rehmat (Mount of Mercy) is located near which city?
Jabal-e-Rehmat is a hill on the plain of Arafat, about 20 km southeast of Makkah in Saudi Arabia. Pilgrims stand at Arafat on 9 Dhul Hijjah.
The Prophet (PBUH) delivered his Farewell Sermon near this area in 10 AH.
In which year was the Rowlatt Act passed?
The Rowlatt Act was passed by the Imperial Legislative Council in March 1919. It allowed arrest and detention without trial.
The Act was named after Justice Sidney Rowlatt, and it led to the Jallianwala Bagh massacre in April 1919.
A law allowing arrest and detention without trial
The Rowlatt Act of 1919 gave the British government power to imprison suspects without trial and to limit press freedom. Indians called it the Black Act.
Gandhi launched a nationwide protest against it.
Which prophet is known for suffering patiently from a long skin disease?
Hazrat Ayyub (AS) bore a long illness, said to be a skin disease, with great patience and is the model of sabr (patience).
The Quran mentions his prayer in Surah Al-Anbiya and Surah Sad.
In which year was the valley of Kashmir sold to Gulab Singh Dogra under the Treaty of Amritsar?
After the First Anglo-Sikh War the British signed the Treaty of Amritsar on 16 March 1846 and sold Kashmir to Gulab Singh.
The price was 75 lakh Nanak Shahi rupees.
How many sons did the Holy Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) have?
He had three sons, Qasim, Abdullah (also called Tayyab and Tahir) and Ibrahim, and all of them died in infancy.
Ibrahim was the son of Hazrat Maria Qibtiyya and the others were sons of Hazrat Khadija.
What field does SUPARCO deal with?
SUPARCO is Pakistan's national space agency, responsible for space science, satellites and upper atmosphere research.
Pakistan launched its first satellite, Badr-1, in 1990.
Zabeehullah (the one offered in sacrifice) is the title of which prophet?
Hazrat Ismail (AS) was the son Hazrat Ibrahim (AS) was ready to sacrifice, so he is called Zabeehullah.
The sacrifice on Eid-ul-Azha commemorates this event.
Which is the biggest trade currency in the world?
The US dollar is the most widely used currency in international trade and reserves.
The euro ranks second in global trade and reserves.
If a helicopter travels 320 km using 50 gallons, how many gallons will it need to travel 700 km?
Gallons per km is 50 divided by 320. For 700 km: 700 times 50 divided by 320 equals 109.375 gallons.
This is a direct proportion problem.
What did the British call the War of 1857 that Muslims and Hindus of the subcontinent called the War of Independence?
The British described the uprising of 1857 as a mutiny of their Indian soldiers (sepoys), calling it the Sepoy Mutiny or Indian Mutiny.
Indian and Pakistani historians call it the War of Independence; the last Mughal emperor Bahadur Shah Zafar was exiled to Rangoon afterwards.
Which President introduced the 1962 Constitution of Pakistan?
Field Marshal Ayub Khan was President and enforced the 1962 Constitution on 8 June 1962, framed by a commission headed by Justice Shahabuddin.
It introduced a presidential system with the President elected through Basic Democrats.
If the 2nd day of a month is Monday, what day will the 20th be?
From the 2nd to the 20th is 18 days. 18 days is 2 full weeks plus 4 day(s), so the day is 4 day(s) after Monday, which is Friday.
Dates that are 7 days apart always fall on the same weekday, so only the remainder after dividing the gap by 7 matters.
For how many days was the 1965 Pakistan-India war fought?
The war began in early September 1965 and the ceasefire came on 23 September 1965, a total of 17 days. It is remembered as the 17-day war.
Pakistan celebrates 6 September as Defence Day in memory of the 1965 war.
Who is generally listed as the first Governor-General of India (of Bengal, 1774)?
Warren Hastings became Governor-General of Bengal in 1774 and is commonly called the first Governor-General of India in textbooks.
Sources differ: Lord William Bentinck was the first Governor-General of all India in 1833, and Lord Mountbatten was the first of independent India.
Which is counted as the third major Ghazwa of the Holy Prophet (PBUH), after Badr and Uhud?
The major battles in order are Badr, Uhud and Khandaq (Ahzab), fought in 5 AH. The Muslims dug a trench on the advice of Salman Farsi.
Sources differ: early chronologies also list small expeditions such as Abwa and Buwat before Badr.
Which prophet was sent to the nation (Qaum) of Aad?
Allah sent Hazrat Hud (AS) to guide the people of Aad, who lived in Al-Ahqaf in southern Arabia.
Hazrat Salih (AS) was sent to the nation of Thamud.
Who acts as the President of Pakistan in the absence of the President?
Under Article 49 of the constitution, the Chairman of the Senate acts as President when the office is vacant or the President is absent.
If the Chairman is unavailable, the Speaker of the National Assembly acts as President.
What is the antonym (opposite) of ADVERSITY?
Adversity means hardship or misfortune, so its opposite is prosperity, meaning good fortune and success.
The plural form adversities is used for repeated difficulties.
Which word is closest in meaning to ADVERSITY?
Adversity means a state of serious difficulty or misfortune. Hardship is the nearest synonym.
The proverb says that adversity is the test of true friends.
Ahmed Ghulam Ali Chagla is famous for composing what?
The tune of the national anthem of Pakistan
The words of the national anthem of Pakistan
The design of the flag of Pakistan
Ahmed Ghulam Ali Chagla (1902-1953) was a Pakistani musician who composed the music of the national anthem of Pakistan.
The words of the anthem were written by Hafeez Jalandhari.
Which is the national airline of Pakistan?
Pakistan International Airlines (PIA) is the national flag carrier of Pakistan, established in 1955.
PIA operated its first flight in 1955 and is headquartered in Karachi.
Syed-ul-Ansar was the title of which Sahabi?
Hazrat Saad bin Muadh (RA), chief of the Aws tribe of Madina, was given the title Syed-ul-Ansar.
Sources may differ on the title holder, but most Pakistani textbooks give Hazrat Saad bin Muadh (RA).
In which year was the national anthem of Pakistan officially approved and adopted?
The national anthem was officially approved by the government of Pakistan in August 1954.
Its tune was composed by Ahmed G. Chagla in 1949 and the words were written by Hafeez Jalandhari.
Which animal was with the Ashab-e-Kahf (Companions of the Cave)?
The Quran in Surah Al-Kahf mentions that their dog lay at the entrance of the cave with outstretched paws.
The dog is traditionally named Qitmir.
Which is the highest civil award of Pakistan?
Nishan-e-Pakistan is the highest civil decoration of Pakistan, given for exceptional public service.
Hilal-e-Imtiaz and Sitara-e-Imtiaz are lower civil awards.
Against whom did the Muslims fight the Battle of Badr?
The Battle of Badr in 2 AH was fought between the Muslims and the Quraish of Makkah.
It was the first major battle of Islam.
What is the antonym of the word biased?
Biased means unfairly favouring one side, so its opposite is impartial.
Unbiased and neutral are other opposites.
What is the border line between Pakistan and India (drawn in 1947) called?
The Radcliffe Line was drawn by the Boundary Commission headed by Sir Cyril Radcliffe at the partition of India in 1947.
The Durand Line is the Pakistan-Afghanistan border and the McMahon Line is the India-China boundary.
In a bus of 24 people, 2/3 are male. What percentage are female?
Males are 2/3 of 24 = 16, so females are 24 - 16 = 8. Percentage = 8/24 x 100 = 33.33 percent.
Females are 1/3 of the bus because the two fractions add up to 1.
How many times did Jahangir Khan win the World Open squash championship?
Jahangir Khan won the World Open six times, the last in 1988.
He also won the British Open ten times in a row from 1982 to 1991.
Which prophet was blessed with a son in his old age?
Hazrat Ibrahim (AS) was granted Hazrat Ismail (AS) and later Hazrat Ishaq (AS) in his old age.
Hazrat Zakariya (AS) was also given a son, Hazrat Yahya (AS), in old age.
The circumference of a circle of radius r is equal to
Circumference = 2 x pi x r, which is the same as pi x diameter.
The area of a circle is pi r squared.
What are two circles called that have three points in common?
Three non-collinear points determine exactly one circle. If two circles share three points, they must be the same circle, so they coincide.
Two different circles can meet in at most two points.
What are sets that have no common element called?
Sets with no element in common have an empty intersection, and such sets are called disjoint sets.
Sets that have the same number of elements are called equivalent sets.
Who composed the music of the national anthem of Pakistan?
The tune of the anthem was composed by Ahmed Ghulamali Chagla, while the words were written by Hafeez Jalandhari.
The anthem was officially adopted in 1954.
Who was the first Pakistani woman cricketer to take 100 wickets in One Day Internationals?
Sana Mir reached 100 ODI wickets in February 2017, the first Pakistani woman to do so. She finished as Pakistan's highest wicket-taker in women's ODIs with about 150 wickets.
Sana Mir was inducted into the ICC Hall of Fame as Pakistan's first woman.
Which crop is grown on the largest area in Pakistan?
Wheat is the staple food and covers the largest cropped area, about 9 million hectares.
Cotton is the major cash crop of Pakistan, but it is grown on a smaller area than wheat.
At what age did Dr Abdul Qadeer Khan die?
Dr A. Q. Khan died on 10 October 2021. He was born in 1936, so he was 85.
Most sources give his birth date as 1 April 1936, though some give 1935.
What is a decimal called in which the digits repeat again and again?
A decimal in which a digit or block of digits repeats endlessly, like 0.333..., is called a recurring (repeating) decimal.
Every recurring decimal can be written as a fraction of two integers, so it is a rational number.
In which year did Quaid-e-Azam declare in Dhaka that Urdu would be the state language of Pakistan?
On 21 March 1948 at Dhaka, Quaid-e-Azam declared that Urdu alone would be the state language of Pakistan.
Urdu was formally made the national language in the 1973 Constitution, so some sources give a different answer.
A square matrix whose determinant is zero is called what?
A square matrix with determinant equal to zero has no inverse and is called a singular matrix.
A matrix with a non-zero determinant is called non-singular and has an inverse.
Where did the Holy Prophet (SAW) deliver the Last Sermon (Khutba Hujjat ul Wida)?
The Last Sermon was delivered in the valley of Uranah at the plain of Arafat during the Farewell Pilgrimage.
It was delivered on 9 Dhul Hijjah.
On whose advice does the President of Pakistan dissolve the National Assembly under the Constitution as it stands today?
Under Article 58 the President dissolves the National Assembly only on the advice of the Prime Minister.
Before the 18th Amendment of 2010 the President could also dissolve it on his own discretion under Article 58(2)(b).
A train's speed is double that of a car, and the car travels 30 km in 1 hour. How far will the train travel in 30 minutes?
Car speed is 30 km/h, so train speed is 2 x 30 = 60 km/h. In 30 minutes the train covers 60 x 0.5 = 30 km.
Distance equals speed multiplied by time.
What is the term (duration) of the National Assembly of Pakistan?
The National Assembly has a term of five years from its first sitting unless dissolved earlier.
A Senator has a term of six years.
How many doors (gates) does Jannah (Paradise) have according to hadith?
Authentic hadith state that Paradise has eight gates, one of them being Ar-Rayyan for those who fast.
For how many years is the President of Pakistan elected?
Under the 1973 Constitution the President holds office for a term of five years.
The President is elected by an electoral college of the Senate, National Assembly and provincial assemblies.
What is the main source of electricity generation in Pakistan today?
Recent data for 2025 show hydel power as the largest single source, around 39 percent in some months. RLNG and nuclear follow.
In earlier decades thermal (oil and gas) plants produced most of Pakistan's electricity.
How many articles are there in the English language?
The English articles are a, an and the. A and an are indefinite and the is definite.
Candidates often wrongly say 2, forgetting that a and an are separate forms.
A train travels twice as fast as a car. If the car covers 30 km in 60 minutes, in what time will the train cover 30 km?
The car's speed is 30 km per hour, so the train's speed is 60 km per hour. The train covers 30 km in 30 / 60 hour = 30 minutes.
Which is the fastest land (terrestrial) animal?
The cheetah is the fastest land animal and can run at about 100 to 110 km per hour in short bursts.
The peregrine falcon is the fastest bird in a dive.
How many agencies were there in the Federally Administered Tribal Areas (FATA)?
FATA had seven agencies: Bajaur, Mohmand, Khyber, Orakzai, Kurram, North Waziristan and South Waziristan.
There were also frontier regions (FRs) attached to FATA.
In which year was the Bogra Formula presented?
Prime Minister Muhammad Ali Bogra presented the formula in 1953 to solve the constitutional deadlock.
It was announced in the Constituent Assembly in October 1953.
A constitutional proposal for a two-house legislature with parity between East and West Pakistan
A plan to make Urdu the only national language
It proposed a bicameral legislature, with equal representation of the provinces in the upper house and representation by population in the lower house.
It was named after Prime Minister Muhammad Ali Bogra.
In which galaxy does the Earth lie?
Our solar system and the Earth lie in the Milky Way galaxy, a barred spiral galaxy.
The nearest large galaxy to the Milky Way is Andromeda.
The ancient region of Gandhara lay mainly between which two modern cities?
Gandhara covered the Peshawar valley and the Potohar plateau around Taxila, roughly from Peshawar to Rawalpindi in north-west Pakistan.
Sources differ on exact limits, but Taxila and Peshawar are its best-known centres.
What is the name of the keeper (gatekeeper) of Hell (Jahannam)?
The angel Malik is named in the Quran (Surah Az-Zukhruf) as the keeper of Hell.
Ridwan is the angel in charge of Paradise.
In which country do the Golan Heights lie?
The Golan Heights is a rocky plateau in south-western Syria. Most of it has been occupied by Israel since 1967.
Israel annexed the Golan Heights in 1981, but this is not recognised by most of the world.
Who sold the Kashmir valley to Gulab Singh in 1846?
By the Treaty of Amritsar (1846) the British East India Company sold Kashmir to Gulab Singh for 7.5 million rupees.
Gulab Singh became the first Dogra Maharaja of Jammu and Kashmir.
If Hamza is three times as old as Ali, what will be the age of Hamza when Ali is 7 years old?
Hamza's age is 3 times Ali's age, so 3 x 7 = 21 years.
Age problems are solved by first writing the ratio between the ages.
Who is the author of the book The Conquest of Happiness?
The Conquest of Happiness (1930) was written by the British philosopher Bertrand Russell.
Russell won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1950.
For how many years did the Quraish of Makkah boycott Banu Hashim?
The Quraish imposed a social and economic boycott on Banu Hashim for about three years in the valley of Shib Abi Talib.
The boycott took place from the 7th to the 10th year of prophethood.
What is the new name of the Kashmir Highway in Islamabad?
In August 2020 Pakistan renamed Islamabad's Kashmir Highway as Srinagar Highway in solidarity with Kashmiris.
The renaming was done on the first anniversary of India's revocation of Article 370 in 2019.
Where was the ICC Men's T20 World Cup of 2021 played?
The 2021 T20 World Cup, officially hosted by the BCCI of India, was moved because of COVID-19 and played in the UAE and Oman in October and November 2021.
Australia won the 2021 final against New Zealand in Dubai.
What does the adjective intimate mean?
Intimate describes a very close, familiar relationship or a detailed, deep knowledge of something.
Intimate can also be a verb meaning to hint at something indirectly, pronounced differently.
How many gates does Jannah (Paradise) have?
According to authentic hadith, Jannah has eight gates, one of which is Ar-Rayyan for those who fast.
Jahannam, by contrast, has seven gates.
Who wrote the famous biography 'Jinnah of Pakistan'?
Stanley Wolpert, an American historian, wrote 'Jinnah of Pakistan' in 1984.
Fatima Jinnah wrote 'My Brother' and Hector Bolitho wrote 'Jinnah: Creator of Pakistan'.
Which one is different from the others: Karachi, Lahore, Balochistan, Rawalpindi?
Karachi, Lahore and Rawalpindi are cities, while Balochistan is a province.
Balochistan is the largest province of Pakistan by area.
What is the capital of North Korea?
Pyongyang is the capital and largest city of North Korea.
Seoul is the capital of South Korea.
Which language is the lingua franca (common link language) of Pakistan?
Urdu is understood across all provinces and links people of different mother tongues. It is also the national language.
Punjabi is the most widely spoken mother tongue in Pakistan.
Which letter comes after G in the English alphabet?
The order is F, G, H, I, so H follows G.
Which letter comes after the letter that is followed by M?
The letter followed by M is L, and the letter after L is M.
M is the 13th letter, exactly in the middle of the alphabet.
Which of these countries lies in two continents (Asia and Europe)?
Turkey is partly in Europe (East Thrace) and mostly in Asia (Anatolia).
Russia, Egypt and Kazakhstan are also transcontinental.
Mark Zuckerberg co-founded Facebook in 2004 and is the CEO of its parent company Meta.
Facebook was renamed as Meta Platforms in 2021.
On which date did the Holy Prophet (PBUH) arrive in Madina after the Hijrat?
After staying at Quba, the Prophet (PBUH) entered Madina on 12 Rabi-ul-Awwal, 1 AH (September 622 AD). He had left Makkah a few days earlier.
Some sources give slightly different days for the departure and arrival, but 12 Rabi-ul-Awwal is the common Pakistani textbook date.
What is the median of the data 2, 2, 3, 3, 5, 6, 7, 8, 8?
The data is already in order and has 9 values, so the median is the 5th value. The 5th value is 5.
The median is the middle value of ordered data, and for an even count it is the mean of the two middle values.
How many seats does the Provincial Assembly of the Punjab have in total?
The Punjab Assembly has 297 general seats, 66 seats for women and 8 for non-Muslims. Together this makes 371.
Punjab has the largest provincial assembly in Pakistan.
What is the midpoint of the points (3, 1) and (-3, 1)?
The midpoint formula is the average of the x values and the average of the y values.
In which Nabawi year was Namaz (the five daily prayers) made obligatory?
The five daily prayers were made obligatory on the night of Miraj, which most Pakistani textbooks place in the 10th year of prophethood.
Sources differ on the exact year of Miraj; some say the 11th or 12th Nabawi year.
In which Nabawi year did the Holy Prophet (SAW) migrate from Makkah to Madina?
The Hijrat took place in 622 CE, which was the 13th year of prophethood.
This Hijrat marks the start of the Islamic Hijri calendar.
OGRA stands for the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority, which regulates the midstream and downstream oil and gas sector of Pakistan.
OGRA was established in 2002 and has its head office in Islamabad.
In which year did Pakistan purchase Gwadar from Oman?
Pakistan bought the Gwadar enclave from the Sultan of Oman in 1958, and it was formally handed over on 8 December 1958.
Gwadar became part of Balochistan province in 1977.
Hazrat Ibrahim (AS), with the help of his son Hazrat Ismail (AS), raised the walls of the Kaaba by Allah's command. This is the answer given in most Pakistani textbooks.
Some traditions say the Kaaba was first built by Hazrat Adam (AS) or the angels, so sources differ.
Whom did the partition of Bengal of 1905 benefit most?
The new province of East Bengal and Assam had a Muslim majority, and Muslims got better chances in education, jobs and trade.
Hindu leaders opposed the partition and launched the Swadeshi movement.
Geographically, into how many main regions is Pakistan divided according to most textbooks?
Pakistan is usually divided into six regions: Northern Highlands, Western Highlands, Balochistan Plateau, Potohar Plateau and Salt Range, Indus Plain, and Deserts.
Some books group them into three or five regions, so sources differ.
Where was the Battle of Plassey fought?
The battle was fought on 23 June 1757 at Plassey in Bengal, on the bank of the Bhagirathi river.
Plassey is in present-day West Bengal, India.
Who was the Prime Minister of Pakistan when the first constitution (1956) was adopted?
Chaudhry Muhammad Ali was Prime Minister when the 1956 Constitution was passed and enforced on 23 March 1956.
Pakistan was declared an Islamic Republic under this constitution.
What was the first document in the process of making the constitution of Pakistan?
The Objective Resolution, passed by the Constituent Assembly in March 1949, laid down the guiding principles for all later constitutions of Pakistan.
It was moved by Liaquat Ali Khan and later became the preamble of the 1973 Constitution.
According to Pakistani textbooks, how many prophets were sent by Allah in total?
A well-known hadith, as taught in Pakistani textbooks, gives the number of prophets as 124,000.
Only 25 prophets are named in the Quran, and some narrations give 224,000.
Approximately how many soldiers of the Quraish army fought against the Muslims in the Battle of Badr?
The Quraish army at Badr numbered about 1000 men (some sources say about 950), against about 313 Muslims. The Muslims won despite being outnumbered.
The Quraish army at Uhud was much larger, about 3000 men.
What is the meaning of the word refute?
To refute a claim is to prove it wrong. Synonyms include disprove, rebut and counter.
Refute is sometimes wrongly used to mean simply deny.
Which country does not have a regular army?
Costa Rica abolished its army in 1948 after a civil war. It relies on police forces for security.
Dominica, Iceland and Panama are other countries without a standing army.
What does SUPARCO stand for and what is it related to?
Pakistan's space and upper atmosphere research agency
SUPARCO is the Space and Upper Atmosphere Research Commission, Pakistan's national space agency. It was founded in 1961.
Pakistan launched its first satellite Badr-1 in 1990.
Is the square root of 7 a rational or an irrational number?
7 is not a perfect square, so its square root is a non-terminating, non-repeating decimal and cannot be written as a fraction of integers. Hence it is irrational.
The square root of any prime number is irrational.
On what date was the Rowlatt Act passed in 1919?
The Imperial Legislative Council passed the Rowlatt Act on 18 March 1919.
Some sources give 21 March 1919, the date of the Viceroy's assent, so sources differ slightly.
How many member countries does SAARC have?
SAARC has 8 members: Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Maldives, Nepal, Pakistan and Sri Lanka.
Afghanistan joined as the eighth member in 2007, and SAARC began with 7 members in 1985.
How many Sahaba were martyred in the Battle of Uhud?
About 70 Muslims were martyred at Uhud, including Hazrat Hamza (RA).
Uhud took place in 3 Hijri after the archers left their post on the hill.
In which part of Punjab is the Salt Range located?
The Salt Range lies in northern Punjab, between the Jhelum River and the Indus River south of Potohar Plateau. Khewra salt mine is in the range.
Mount Sakesar is the highest peak of the Salt Range.
In which year was the Scientific Society founded by Sir Syed Ahmad Khan at Ghazipur?
Sir Syed Ahmad Khan established the Scientific Society in 1864 at Ghazipur to translate Western scientific works into Urdu.
The society later moved to Aligarh in 1866, where it published the Aligarh Institute Gazette.
In which year was Sir Syed Ahmad Khan born?
Sir Syed Ahmad Khan was born in Delhi on 17 October 1817.
He founded the M.A.O. College at Aligarh, which later became Aligarh Muslim University.
Which word is closest in meaning (a synonym) to "totally"?
Totally means entirely, which is completely.
Entirely and wholly are also synonyms.
Which word is closest in meaning (a synonym) to "tyrant"?
A tyrant is a cruel ruler with absolute power, a despot.
Tyranny is the rule of a tyrant.
What is the value of tan 90 degrees?
tan 90 = sin 90 / cos 90 = 1 / 0, and division by zero is undefined.
tan 45 degrees equals 1 and tan 0 degrees equals 0.
In which year was the name Pakistan first coined and used, in the pamphlet Now or Never?
Choudhry Rahmat Ali and his Cambridge colleagues first used the name Pakistan in the pamphlet Now or Never, published on 28 January 1933.
The Lahore Resolution demanding separate Muslim states was passed later, in March 1940.
At what age of the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) was the last revelation (wahi) revealed?
The Prophet (PBUH) received his first revelation at 40 and the last verses shortly before his death at the age of 63.
He passed away in 11 AH (632 CE).
Who signed the Indus Waters Treaty of 1960 on behalf of India, as Prime Minister of India at that time?
The treaty was signed at Karachi on 19 September 1960 by Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru for India and President Ayub Khan for Pakistan.
The World Bank was also a signatory, as it had mediated the treaty.
What is the value of sin 180 degrees?
On the unit circle, 180 degrees is the point (-1, 0), and sine is the y-coordinate, which is 0.
Also cos 180 degrees = -1 and sin 90 degrees = 1.
What is the value of cos 180 degrees?
On the unit circle, 180 degrees is the point (-1, 0), and cosine is the x-coordinate, which is -1.
cos 0 degrees = 1, cos 90 degrees = 0 and cos 180 degrees = -1.
Who abrogated the 1956 Constitution of Pakistan in October 1958?
President Iskander Mirza abrogated the 1956 Constitution on 7 October 1958, dissolved the assemblies and imposed martial law.
Iskander Mirza himself was removed by General Ayub Khan only 20 days later.
Where were the FIFA World Cup matches of 2022 played?
The 2022 FIFA World Cup was hosted by Qatar from November to December 2022. Argentina won it.
It was the first FIFA World Cup held in an Arab and Muslim-majority country.
Which country hosted the 2022 Winter Olympics?
The 2022 Winter Olympics were held in Beijing, China, in February 2022. There was no Summer Olympics in 2022.
The 2020 Summer Olympics were held in Tokyo in 2021, and the 2024 Summer Games in Paris.
Who was the third Governor-General of Pakistan?
The Governors-General were Quaid-e-Azam, Khawaja Nazimuddin, Ghulam Muhammad (1951-55) and then Iskander Mirza.
Iskander Mirza became the first President of Pakistan in 1956.
What is the meaning of abhor?
Abhor means to regard with disgust and hatred.
What is a synonym of acute?
Acute can mean sharp or intense, as in acute pain, and severe is the closest synonym.
Acute angle means an angle less than 90 degrees.
Which prophet (AS) was sent to the tyrant king Namrood (Nimrod)?
Hazrat Ibrahim (AS) invited Namrood to the worship of one Allah and debated with him. Namrood later had him thrown into a fire, which Allah made cool and safe.
Hazrat Ibrahim (AS) is called Khalil-ullah (friend of Allah).
What is the meaning of the word ADHERE?
To adhere means to stick or hold fast to something, such as a surface, a rule or a belief. Its synonyms include stick, cling and follow.
The related noun adherent means a supporter or follower of a cause.
Which companion (Sahabi) of the Holy Prophet (PBUH) was his adopted son?
Hazrat Zaid bin Haritha (RA) was freed and adopted by the Prophet (PBUH) before prophethood, and was known as Zaid bin Muhammad until adoption was abolished.
Zaid is the only companion whose name is mentioned in the Quran (Surah Al-Ahzab).
What does the Arabic word Alfeel mean?
Alfeel means elephant. Surah Al-Fil of the Quran tells of Abraha's army with elephants that tried to destroy the Kaaba in the Year of the Elephant.
The Holy Prophet (PBUH) was born in the Year of the Elephant (about 570 CE).
When was the Non-Aligned Movement (NAM) founded?
The Non-Aligned Movement was formally founded at the Belgrade Summit in September 1961 by leaders such as Tito, Nehru, Nasser, Nkrumah and Sukarno.
The movement grew out of the 1955 Bandung Conference.
Which act of worship is mentioned in the Quran together with Zakat in many verses?
The Quran repeatedly commands to establish Salat and pay Zakat together, for example in Surah Al-Baqarah.
Salat is the second and Zakat the third pillar of Islam in the usual list (after Shahada).
Amjad and Ahmad together kept 24 balls. Amjad kept three times as many as Ahmad. How many balls did Ahmad keep?
Let Ahmad keep x balls, so Amjad keeps 3x. Then x + 3x = 24, so 4x = 24 and x = 6.
Amjad therefore kept 18 balls, and 18 is three times 6.
What is the antonym of defile?
To defile means to make dirty or impure, so its opposite is to purify.
Pollute, stain and spoil are close to defile in meaning.
What is the antonym of dilate?
To dilate is to become wider or larger, so its opposite is to constrict or contract.
The pupil of the eye dilates in dim light.
What is the circling (going around) of the Kaaba during Hajj and Umrah called?
Tawaf is the act of walking seven times around the Kaaba in an anticlockwise direction.
Tawaf begins and ends at the Black Stone (Hajr-e-Aswad).
How many articles did the 1962 Constitution of Pakistan have?
The 1962 Constitution given by Ayub Khan had 250 articles.
It was suspended when martial law was imposed in 1969.
According to the 1973 Constitution, what is the term of the National Assembly and the Provincial Assemblies?
Unless dissolved earlier, the National and Provincial Assemblies serve a term of five years from their first meeting.
A Senator's term is six years, with half retiring every three years.
How old was the Holy Prophet (PBUH) when his grandfather Hazrat Abdul Muttalib passed away?
Abdul Muttalib took care of the Prophet (PBUH) after his mother died and passed away when the Prophet was 8 years old. Afterwards his uncle Abu Talib became his guardian.
The Prophet (PBUH) lost his mother Hazrat Amina at the age of 6.
What was the real name of Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA)?
His name was Abdullah bin Abi Quhafa, and he received the title Siddiq and Atiq.
Some narrations say his pre-Islamic name was Abd al-Kaba, which the Prophet (PBUH) changed to Abdullah.
Baltistan is also known as which of the following?
Baltistan, in Gilgit-Baltistan, is called Little Tibet (Tibet-e-Khurd) because of its culture and mountain landscape similar to Tibet.
Skardu is the main town of Baltistan.
Who introduced the Basic Democracies system in Pakistan?
Field Marshal Ayub Khan introduced the Basic Democracies system in 1959 as a local-government and electoral-college system.
It had 80,000 Basic Democrats, later 120,000, who elected the President under the 1962 Constitution.
Which prophet (AS) was given the ability to understand the language of birds and animals?
The Quran says that Allah taught Hazrat Sulaiman (AS) the speech of birds, and he talked with the hoopoe and the ant.
Hazrat Sulaiman (AS) also ruled over the jinn and the wind, and he was the son of Hazrat Dawood (AS).
On which date of the Islamic month was the Holy Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) born, according to the view most followed in Pakistan?
The Holy Prophet (PBUH) was born on Monday, 12 Rabi-ul-Awwal in the Year of the Elephant, which is about 570 AD in Makkah.
Some scholars and the Shia tradition give 17 Rabi-ul-Awwal, so sources differ on the exact day.
What is the antonym (opposite) of the word brilliant?
Brilliant means very bright or very intelligent, and its opposite is dull.
Synonyms of brilliant include bright, radiant and gifted.
What was the Cabinet Mission of 1946?
A British mission sent to India to discuss the transfer of power
A Muslim League mission sent to London
A Congress mission sent to the Viceroy
A United Nations mission to Kashmir
The Cabinet Mission was a delegation of three British cabinet ministers sent to India in 1946. It proposed a plan for the transfer of power and a united India with a weak centre.
The Muslim League first accepted the plan and later withdrew its acceptance.
How many players play in a game of chess?
Chess is played between two players, one with white pieces and one with black.
Each player starts with 16 pieces on a board of 64 squares.
What is the highest civilian award of Pakistan?
Nishan-e-Pakistan is the highest civil award of Pakistan.
Nishan-e-Haider is the highest military award for gallantry.
Which is the coldest inhabited place of Pakistan?
Skardu in Gilgit-Baltistan records the lowest winter temperatures among Pakistan's inhabited places; it recorded about minus 21 degrees Celsius in December 2019.
Ziarat and Gilgit are also among the coldest places in winter.
In which year AD was Makkah conquered by the Muslims?
Makkah was conquered in Ramadan 8 AH, which corresponds to January 630 AD.
The conquest was almost bloodless and the Prophet (PBUH) announced a general amnesty.
Which political party controlled the North-West Frontier Province (KPK) at the time of partition in 1947?
The Congress ministry of Dr Khan Sahib was in power in NWFP in 1947, and it was dismissed after independence.
The NWFP referendum of July 1947 decided the province would join Pakistan.
How many copies of the Quran were prepared by Hazrat Usman (RA) and sent to different regions?
Hazrat Usman (RA) had standard copies prepared from the Abu Bakr copy and sent them to major centres; most Pakistani textbooks say five copies.
Some sources say seven copies, including one kept in Madina, so sources differ.
A. R. Cornelius, a Chief Justice of Pakistan, belonged to which religion?
Justice Alvin Robert Cornelius was a Christian and served as Chief Justice of Pakistan from 1960 to 1968.
He was known for his scholarship and integrity.
What is the meaning of the word crude?
Crude means in a natural or raw state, not yet processed, or rough and lacking refinement.
Crude oil is petroleum before it is refined into petrol and diesel.
Who is the current Prime Minister of India?
Narendra Modi has been Prime Minister since 2014 and began his third consecutive term in June 2024.
He is the longest-serving Prime Minister of India after Jawaharlal Nehru and Indira Gandhi in total years.
Against whom did Nawab Siraj ud Daula fight the Battle of Plassey in 1757?
The British East India Company forces under Robert Clive defeated the Nawab of Bengal at Plassey, helped by the betrayal of Mir Jafar.
The battle marked the beginning of British rule in India.
Who was the first woman to head a democratic government in Pakistan, and the first elected woman leader of a Muslim country?
Benazir Bhutto became Prime Minister of Pakistan in December 1988, the first woman to head the government of a Muslim-majority country.
She served twice, 1988 to 1990 and 1993 to 1996.
Roughly what fraction of the Earth's land surface is covered by deserts (arid regions)?
Deserts and arid lands cover roughly one third of the Earth's land surface.
Sources differ depending on how a desert is defined.
At what age did Dr. A.Q. Khan, the Pakistani nuclear scientist, die?
Dr. Abdul Qadeer Khan was born on 1 April 1936 and died on 10 October 2021, aged 85.
He is known as the father of Pakistan's nuclear programme.
Whose words are Unity, Faith and Discipline (Ittehad, Imaan, Tanzeem)?
Quaid-e-Azam gave the nation the motto Unity, Faith, Discipline as the guiding principle of Pakistan.
The motto is written on the national emblem of Pakistan.
What type of star is our Sun?
The Sun is a G-type main-sequence star, commonly called a yellow dwarf.
In about five billion years it will become a red giant and later a white dwarf.
What is the antonym of the word 'ecstasy'?
Ecstasy means overwhelming joy, so its opposite is deep unhappiness, which is misery. Rapture, elation and delight are its synonyms.
Agony and despair are also opposites of ecstasy.
Who elects the President of Pakistan?
An electoral college of the Senate, National Assembly and provincial assemblies
