The President is elected indirectly by an electoral college made up of members of the Senate, the National Assembly and the four provincial assemblies.
Asif Ali Zardari was elected President for a second time in March 2024.
Completely is to what, as a synonym? Choose the word closest in meaning to 'entirely'.
Entirely means in every part or fully, the same as completely.
Wholly and totally are also synonyms.
BODMAS gives division priority over addition.
What is the closest meaning of the word excuse (as a verb)?
To excuse someone means to forgive or pardon a fault. Blame, punish and accuse have the opposite sense.
As a noun, excuse means a reason offered to justify a fault, for example a pretext.
According to Islam, fasting (Roza) protects a person from what?
The Holy Prophet (PBUH) said that fasting is a shield. It teaches self-control and keeps a person away from sins and evil deeds.
The Quran says fasting was prescribed so that you may become pious (taqwa).
What happened on 27 February 2019 when the Pakistan Air Force responded to an Indian incursion?
Pakistan shot down two Indian aircraft and captured a pilot
On 27 February 2019 the PAF shot down Indian aircraft inside Pakistani airspace and the Indian pilot Wing Commander Abhinandan was captured.
Pakistan named its response Operation Swift Retort and returned the pilot to India on 1 March 2019.
Against whom did the Muslims fight in the Ghazwa (Battle) of Badr?
Badr was the first major battle of Islam, fought in 2 AH between the Muslims and the Quraysh of Makkah.
About 313 Muslims faced an army of roughly 1000 Quraysh.
What was the name of the foster mother of the Holy Prophet (PBUH)?
Halima Sadia of the Banu Saad tribe nursed and raised the infant Prophet (PBUH) in the desert.
Thuwaiba, a freed slave of Abu Lahab, nursed him briefly before Halima.
Which is the fourth source of Islamic law (Shariah) in the usual order?
The four sources in order are the Holy Quran, the Sunnah (Hadith), Ijma (consensus of scholars) and Qiyas (analogy).
Hanafi fiqh, followed by most Pakistanis, accepts all four sources.
What is the capital of France?
Paris, on the River Seine, is the capital and largest city of France.
The Eiffel Tower is in Paris.
The Friendship Gate (Bab-e-Dosti) at Chaman is a border crossing between which two countries?
The Friendship Gate stands at Chaman in Balochistan on the Pakistan-Afghanistan border.
It is on Pakistan's western border, the Durand Line, opposite Spin Boldak in Afghanistan.
In which year of prophethood (Nabwi) was the Year of Grief (Aam-ul-Huzn)?
The Year of Grief was the 10th year of prophethood, when the Prophet (PBUH) lost his wife Hazrat Khadija (RA) and his uncle Abu Talib within a short time.
Soon after, the Prophet (PBUH) travelled to Taif.
Who is the guard (darogha) of Jahannam (Hell)?
The chief angel who guards Hell is named Malik, as mentioned in Surah Az-Zukhruf.
The keeper of Paradise is the angel Ridwan.
Habba Khatoon was a famous poet of which language?
Habba Khatoon (Zoon) was a 16th century Kashmiri poet known for her lyrical songs.
She is often called the Nightingale of Kashmir.
The Black Stone fixed in the Kaaba
A gate of the Prophet's Mosque
Hajr-e-Aswad is the Black Stone set in the eastern corner of the Kaaba.
Pilgrims try to kiss or point to it at the start of each Tawaf.
What is the HCF of 6 and 12?
6 divides 12 exactly, so the largest number dividing both is 6.
When one number divides the other, the smaller number is the HCF and the larger is the LCM.
At what age is Hazrat Isa (AS) commonly said to have been raised to the heavens?
The commonly stated age at which Hazrat Isa (AS) was raised to the heavens is 33 years.
Sources differ on the exact age, but 33 is the figure most commonly given.
What is the most important event of 10 Hijri?
The Farewell Hajj and Last Sermon of the Prophet (PBUH)
In 10 AH the Prophet (PBUH) performed his only Hajj, the Hajjatul Wida, and delivered the Last Sermon at Arafat.
The Conquest of Makkah took place in 8 AH.
Which Chinese fighter jets did Pakistan Air Force formally induct in March 2022?
The PAF commissioned its first six J-10C multirole fighters from China in March 2022.
China's stealth fighter J-35 has been reported as a possible future PAF purchase, but no delivery has been officially confirmed.
Which cricketer scored 400 not out in a single Test innings?
Brian Lara of the West Indies scored 400 not out against England at Antigua in 2004.
This remains the highest individual score in Test cricket; Lara also made 375 in 1994 and Hayden's 380 once held the record in between.
What is the integral of ln x with respect to x?
Integrating by parts with u = ln x and dv = dx gives x ln x - integral of (x times 1/x) dx = x ln x - x + C.
The derivative of ln x is 1/x.
What is the meaning of the word interim?
Interim describes something provided or done for the time between two events, that is, temporary.
An interim government rules only until a regular government is elected.
Inzamam-ul-Haq, one of Pakistan's best batsmen, played which sport for the Pakistan national team?
Inzamam-ul-Haq played Test and One Day cricket for Pakistan from 1991 to 2007 and captained the team.
He scored 8830 Test runs and 11701 ODI runs.
Hazrat Sara (AS), wife of Hazrat Ibrahim (AS), was the mother of Hazrat Ishaq (AS).
Hazrat Hajra (AS) was the mother of Hazrat Ismail (AS).
Who is regarded as the first martyr of Islam?
Hazrat Sumayyah (RA), mother of Hazrat Ammar (RA), was killed by Abu Jahl for her faith and is the first martyr of Islam.
Some sources name Harith bin Abi Hala as the first male martyr, so sources differ.
Which city was the capital of Pakistan before Islamabad?
Karachi was the first capital from 1947 until the capital moved to the new city of Islamabad in the 1960s, with Rawalpindi as interim seat.
Islamabad was planned by the Greek architect Constantinos Doxiadis.
In which year was Pakistan's first postage stamp issued?
Pakistan issued its first set of four postage stamps on 9 July 1948.
Before that, stamps of British India overprinted with the word Pakistan were used in 1947.
Which fighter jet has Pakistan produced jointly with China?
The JF-17 Thunder is a light multirole fighter built by Pakistan Aeronautical Complex, Kamra, with China's Chengdu Aircraft Corporation.
Its Chinese designation is FC-1 Xiaolong.
How many Jewish tribes lived in Madina when the Holy Prophet (SAW) migrated there?
The three main Jewish tribes of Madina were Banu Qaynuqa, Banu Nadir and Banu Quraizah.
The Charter of Madina (Misaq-e-Madina) was made with them after the Hijrah.
Which was the first princely state to accede to Pakistan?
Bahawalpur was the first princely state to accede to Pakistan, in October 1947.
Its ruler, the Nawab Sadiq Muhammad Khan Abbasi V, acceded on 5 October 1947.
Arfa Karim, the youngest Microsoft Certified Professional, belonged to which country?
Arfa Abdul Karim Randhawa was a Pakistani girl from Faisalabad who became a Microsoft Certified Professional at age 9.
She died in January 2012 at the age of 16, and Lahore has a software technology park tower named after her.
Kathmandu is the capital of which country?
Kathmandu is the capital and largest city of Nepal.
Thimphu is the capital of Bhutan.
On which river is the Khanpur Dam built?
Khanpur Dam is built on the Haro River in the Haripur district of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.
It supplies drinking water to Islamabad and Rawalpindi.
What is the LCM of 4 and 6?
Multiples of 4 are 4, 8, 12 and multiples of 6 are 6, 12. The first common multiple is 12.
LCM times HCF of two numbers equals their product (12 x 2 = 24).
What is the process by which a liquid changes into vapour (gas) called?
When a liquid gains heat and its molecules escape into the air as vapour, the change is called evaporation or vaporization.
The reverse process, vapour changing into liquid, is called condensation.
What is the antonym (opposite) of the word 'loved'?
Loved means felt strong affection for, and its opposite is hated.
Loathed and detested are other close opposites.
In which year was Mangla Dam completed?
Mangla Dam was built under the Indus Waters Treaty works and completed in 1967.
It was raised in height in the 2000s to increase storage.
Which type of medicine is used to relieve pain?
Analgesics such as paracetamol and aspirin are painkillers. They reduce pain without making the person lose consciousness.
Anaesthetics are different because they cause loss of sensation before surgery.
Which country voted against the admission of Pakistan to the United Nations in 1947?
Afghanistan was the only country that voted against Pakistan's admission to the UN in September 1947. It reversed its stand soon afterwards.
Pakistan became the 56th member of the UN on 30 September 1947.
If a helicopter needs 50 gallons of fuel to move 320 km, how many gallons are needed to cover 400 km?
Fuel per km is 50 divided by 320. For 400 km, 400 x 50 / 320 = 62.5 gallons.
This is a direct proportion question.
What was the approximate strength of the Muslim army sent against Musailma Kazzab in the Battle of Yamama?
Hazrat Khalid bin Walid (RA) led about 13,000 Muslims against the army of Musailma Kazzab at Yamama in 633 CE (11 AH).
Musailma's army is usually given as about 40,000, though sources differ on exact numbers.
In which city is Masjid-e-Nabawi located?
Masjid-e-Nabawi was built by the Holy Prophet (SAW) in Madina after the Hijrat.
It also contains the blessed grave of the Prophet (SAW).
Who was the first Commander-in-Chief of the Pakistan Navy?
Vice Admiral H. M. S. Choudri
Vice Admiral James Wilfred Jefford of the Royal Navy became the first head of the Royal Pakistan Navy in 1947.
The first Pakistani Commander-in-Chief of the Navy was Vice Admiral Muhammad Siddiq Choudri.
A person walks 7 miles towards the north, then turns left, then turns left again. In which direction is he going now?
Facing north, a left turn makes him face west. Turning left again from west makes him face south.
Two successive left turns make a total turn of 180 degrees.
In which city is the head office (secretariat) of the Economic Cooperation Organization (ECO) located?
The ECO secretariat is located in Tehran, Iran.
ECO was founded in 1985 by Pakistan, Iran and Turkey as the successor of RCD.
Which type of medicine is used to reduce pain?
Analgesics (painkillers) such as paracetamol and aspirin relieve pain. Vaccines prevent disease and antibiotics kill bacteria.
Anaesthetics are different from analgesics because they cause loss of sensation.
If 5 men write 5 pages in 5 minutes, how many pages will one man write in 5 minutes?
5 men write 5 pages in 5 minutes, so each man writes 1 page in 5 minutes.
The rate is 1 page per man per 5 minutes, or 0.2 pages per minute.
Complete the sentence: The prices of clothes are too ___.
Prices are described as high or low, so high is the correct word.
We use tall and long for height and length, not for prices.
What is the antonym of provoke?
Provoke means to make someone angry or stir them up; the opposite is to pacify or calm them.
Appease and soothe are also antonyms of provoke.
Under which treaty did Gulab Singh purchase Kashmir from the British?
By the Treaty of Amritsar (March 1846) the British sold Kashmir to Gulab Singh of Jammu for 7.5 million rupees.
This created the princely state of Jammu and Kashmir under Dogra rule.
A quarter means one fourth. 12 divided by 4 equals 3.
A quarter of 120 is 30, ten times the answer here.
Which political party launched the Quit India Movement in August 1942?
The Indian National Congress passed the Quit India resolution in Bombay in August 1942 under the leadership of Mahatma Gandhi. The Muslim League opposed the movement.
The Quit India Movement demanded an immediate end to British rule in India.
On which date was Operation Radd-ul-Fasad announced?
Operation Radd-ul-Fasad was announced on 22 February 2017 by the Pakistan Army after a wave of terrorist attacks.
Radd-ul-Fasad means elimination of discord or mischief.
A rational number can be written as p/q where p and q are integers and q is not zero. 5/7 fits this form, so it is rational.
Fractions such as 2/3 and 11/9 are rational too, while pi is irrational.
In which year was RCD changed into the Economic Cooperation Organization (ECO)?
RCD became inactive after the Iranian Revolution of 1979. It was revived and renamed the Economic Cooperation Organization (ECO) in 1985 by Pakistan, Iran and Turkey.
In 1992, ECO admitted seven more members, including Afghanistan, Azerbaijan and several Central Asian states.
To get information and knowledge about current events
Newspapers report news and information about local and world events. People read them mainly to gain knowledge and stay informed.
The first printed newspapers appeared in Europe in the early 1600s.
What is the real part of the complex number -i(4i + 6)?
-i(4i + 6) = -4i squared - 6i = 4 - 6i since i squared = -1. The real part is 4.
The imaginary part of this number is -6.
Who rebuilt the Kaaba together with his son Hazrat Ismail (AS)?
Hazrat Ibrahim (AS) and his son Hazrat Ismail (AS) raised the foundations of the Kaaba by Allah's command. This is mentioned in Surah Al-Baqarah.
Quraish later rebuilt it again when the Prophet (PBUH) was about 35 years old.
Who wrote the book Dead Reckoning: Memories of the 1971 Bangladesh War?
Dead Reckoning (2011) was written by Sarmila Bose and discusses the 1971 war and its casualty figures. It is often confused with works by authors with similar names.
Shrabani Basu wrote Victoria and Abdul, a different book.
What does the word refund mean?
Refund means to give back money that was paid, for example for a returned item. Its synonym is reimburse.
Refund can be a noun (a refund) or a verb (to refund).
What is the meaning of the word reluctant?
Reluctant means unwilling or hesitant to do something. A reluctant person does not want to act.
In which province of Pakistan is the Reko Diq (Rikodik) copper and gold mine project?
Reko Diq is in the Chagai district of Balochistan and is one of the world's largest copper and gold deposits.
The Saindak copper and gold project is also in Chagai.
Which two hadith books are called the Sahihain?
Sahihain means the two Sahih books: Sahih al-Bukhari by Imam Bukhari and Sahih Muslim by Imam Muslim.
These two are considered the most authentic books of hadith.
The differences are 3, 6, 12, which double each time, so the next difference is 24. Then 45 - 24 = 21.
A series whose differences double is a common pattern in reasoning tests.
What is the value of sin 0 degrees?
On the unit circle the angle 0 degrees points along the x-axis, so the y-coordinate (the sine) is 0. Hence sin 0 = 0.
My brother's son's sister is my what?
My brother's son is my nephew, and his sister is my brother's daughter, who is my niece.
A niece is the daughter of one's brother or sister.
The Sun is currently in which stage of a star's life?
The Sun fuses hydrogen into helium in its core, which is the main sequence stage. It has been in this stage for about 4.6 billion years.
In about 5 billion years the Sun will become a red giant.
Which is the largest railway station of Pakistan, according to most sources?
Lahore Junction is most commonly named as the largest railway station of Pakistan by area.
Sources differ on this point, and Karachi Cantonment and Rohri are also described as very large.
What is the closest meaning of 'strenuous'?
Strenuous means needing great effort or energy. Arduous has the same meaning.
The opposite of strenuous is effortless or easy.
Sukkur city is located in which province of Pakistan?
Sukkur is a city on the bank of the River Indus in the province of Sindh.
The Sukkur Barrage was completed in 1932.
Which word is closest in meaning (a synonym) to "normally"?
Normally means in the usual way, which is usually.
Which word is closest in meaning (a synonym) to "oppress"?
To oppress is to treat people harshly and unjustly, close to persecute.
Which word is closest in meaning (a synonym) to "retrieve"?
To retrieve is to get something back, which is to recover.
A retriever dog is named for fetching game.
Tayammum is done by striking the hands on clean earth or dust and wiping the face and arms.
It is allowed instead of wudu or ghusl when water is unavailable or harmful to use.
What is the antonym of the word timid?
Timid means lacking courage, so its opposite is bold.
Shy, fearful and meek are synonyms of timid.
Jami at-Tirmidhi (Tirmizi Sharif) is a book of what?
Jami at-Tirmidhi is a collection of the sayings and actions (ahadith) of the Prophet (PBUH) compiled by Imam Tirmidhi.
It is one of the six major hadith collections known as Sihah Sitta.
In which language was the Holy Quran first translated in the subcontinent (India)?
Shah Waliullah made the well-known first full translation into Persian in 1738, which is the usual textbook answer.
Sources differ, as an early Sindhi translation is also claimed; Shah Abdul Qadir later did the first Urdu translation.
Change into passive voice: Soldiers are digging trenches.
Trenches are being dug by soldiers.
Trenches have been dug by soldiers.
The present continuous active becomes am/is/are being plus the past participle in the passive.
The past continuous 'were digging' becomes 'were being dug'.
Who was the first Viceroy of India?
Lord Canning became the first Viceroy in 1858 after the Government of India Act transferred power from the East India Company to the Crown.
Warren Hastings was the first Governor-General of Bengal, and Lord William Bentinck the first Governor-General of India.
Which of the following diseases is caused by a virus?
Influenza is caused by influenza viruses. Tuberculosis and cholera are caused by bacteria and malaria by a protozoan parasite.
Antibiotics do not work against viral diseases.
Which is the highest waterfall in the world?
Angel Falls in Venezuela has a total height of about 979 metres, with an uninterrupted drop of about 807 metres, making it the highest waterfall in the world.
Angel Falls is located in Canaima National Park, Venezuela, and is named after the pilot Jimmie Angel.
Any non-zero number divided by itself equals 1, so 90/90 = 1.
Division of zero by a non-zero number gives 0, but division by zero is undefined.
If the 4th day of a month is Sunday, what day will be the 13th of that month?
The 13th is 9 days after the 4th, and 9 = 7 + 2. Sunday + 2 days = Tuesday.
A week has 7 days, so the same weekday repeats every 7 days of the month.
If the 1st day of a month is Monday, what day will be the 14th of that month?
The 14th is 13 days after the 1st, and 13 = 7 + 6. Monday + 6 days = Sunday.
A week has 7 days, so the same weekday repeats every 7 days of the month.
If the 1st day of a month is Monday, what day will be the 15th of that month?
The 15th is 14 days after the 1st, which is exactly two weeks, so it is also a Monday.
A week has 7 days, so the same weekday repeats every 7 days of the month.
Which term comes next in the series: 3z, 6y, 9x, 15w, ?
The numbers 3, 6, 9, 15 follow the rule that each is the sum of the two before it (3+6=9, 6+9=15), so the next is 9+15=24. The letters go backwards from z, y, x, w to v.
A series where each term is the sum of the previous two is called a Fibonacci-type series.
What is the square root of 1600?
40 x 40 = 1600, so the square root of 1600 is 40.
The square root of 16 is 4, so the square root of 1600 is 4 x 10 = 40.
Who announced the partition of Bengal in 1905?
Lord Curzon, the Viceroy of India, announced the partition of Bengal on 19 July 1905 and it took effect on 16 October 1905, creating a Muslim-majority eastern province.
The partition was annulled in 1911, and the All India Muslim League was formed in 1906 partly in reaction to these events.
In which year did Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah receive the title of Quaid-e-Azam (Great Leader), as most Pakistani textbooks state?
Most Pakistani textbooks say that Maulana Mazharuddin Shaheed gave the title Quaid-e-Azam to Jinnah in 1938.
Sources differ on the exact year, and some mention 1936 or other dates.
Which party formed the government in the North-West Frontier Province (now KPK) at the time of independence in 1947?
The ministry of Dr Khan Sahib, which belonged to the Indian National Congress (backed by the Khudai Khidmatgars), was in power in the province in August 1947.
The Governor dismissed the Khan Sahib ministry on 22 August 1947, and Abdul Qayyum Khan of the Muslim League then became Chief Minister.
If the 2nd day of a month is Friday, what day will the 19th be?
From the 2nd to the 19th is 17 days. 17 days is 2 full weeks plus 3 day(s), so the day is 3 day(s) after Friday, which is Monday.
Dates that are 7 days apart always fall on the same weekday, so only the remainder after dividing the gap by 7 matters.
If the 3rd day of a month is Sunday, what day will the 19th be?
From the 3rd to the 19th is 16 days. 16 days is 2 full weeks plus 2 day(s), so the day is 2 day(s) after Sunday, which is Tuesday.
Dates that are 7 days apart always fall on the same weekday, so only the remainder after dividing the gap by 7 matters.
If the 24th day of a month is Tuesday, what day will the 3rd be?
From the 3rd back to the 24th is 21 days. 21 days is 3 full weeks plus 0 day(s), so the day is 0 day(s) before Tuesday, which is Tuesday.
Dates that are 7 days apart always fall on the same weekday, so only the remainder after dividing the gap by 7 matters.
Which constitution was enforced in Pakistan in April 1972 after the separation of East Pakistan?
After 1971 a temporary Interim Constitution was adopted in April 1972, which ended martial law and ran until the permanent constitution of 1973.
The permanent Constitution of Pakistan was passed in April 1973 and enforced on 14 August 1973.
What was the official name of Pakistan under the 1973 Constitution?
Article 1 of the 1973 Constitution names the country the Islamic Republic of Pakistan.
The 1956 Constitution also used the name Islamic Republic of Pakistan, while the 1962 Constitution used Republic of Pakistan.
Under whose government was the 1973 Constitution of Pakistan framed and passed?
The 1973 Constitution was drafted by a parliamentary committee and passed by the National Assembly during the premiership of Zulfikar Ali Bhutto. It was adopted in April 1973.
Abdul Hafeez Pirzada, the law minister, played a leading role in drafting it.
Work left to right: 2 x 2 is 4, and 4 divided by 2 is 2.
Multiplication and division have equal priority and are done left to right.
In a class of 500 students, 340 are male. What percentage of the students is male?
In a school of 500 students, 340 are male. What percentage of the students is female?
Females are 500 minus 340, which is 160. Then 160 divided by 500 times 100 gives 32 percent.
Multiply first: 3x4 = 12 and 2x4 = 8 (4x2 is also 8). Then add: 12 + 8 = 20.
In arithmetic, multiplication is done before addition (BODMAS).
How many columns does a matrix of order 5x4 have?
A matrix of order m x n has m rows and n columns. For 5x4 there are 5 rows and 4 columns.
The total number of elements in a 5x4 matrix is 20.
If the 28th day of a month is Monday, what day will be the 8th day of that month?
From the 8th to the 28th is 20 days, and 20 = 2 weeks + 6 days. Going back 6 days from Monday gives Tuesday.
Going back 6 days is the same as going forward 1 day in a week cycle.
In which Hijri year was Aam-ul-Wafood (Year of Delegations)?
Delegations from many Arab tribes came to Madina to accept Islam in 9 AH, after the conquest of Makkah. This year is called Aam-ul-Wafood.
The year 9 AH is also when the Battle of Tabuk took place.
For which field is Abdur Rehman Chughtai famous?
Abdur Rehman Chughtai (1894-1975) was a famous Pakistani painter and artist known for his Mughal-influenced style.
He is also known for designing Pakistan's early postage stamps.
What is the meaning (synonym) of abolish?
To abolish a law or system means to formally put an end to it, which is to do away with it.
Annul, scrap and repeal are other synonyms of abolish.
Which Surah of the Holy Quran is named after the ant?
Surah An-Naml (Surah 27) is named after the ant that spoke to Hazrat Sulaiman (AS).
Surah Al-Ankabut is named after the spider and An-Nahl after the bee.
Who was the first among slaves to accept Islam, according to most Pakistani textbooks?
Textbooks list Abu Bakr among men, Khadija among women, Ali among children and Zaid bin Haritha among freed slaves as the first to accept Islam.
Some sources name Hazrat Bilal (RA) as the first slave to accept Islam, so sources differ.
How many acute angles are there in an acute triangle?
In an acute triangle all three angles are less than 90 degrees, so all three are acute.
A right triangle has two acute angles and an obtuse triangle has two acute angles as well.
When was the Indian Independence Act passed?
The Indian Independence Act was passed by the British Parliament in July 1947 and created the two dominions of India and Pakistan from 15 August 1947.
It received royal assent on 18 July 1947.
Which word is the antonym (opposite) of ADHERE?
Adhere means to stick to something, so its opposite is detach, meaning to separate or loosen.
Adhesive is a substance that makes things adhere to each other.
What does an adjective describe or explain?
An adjective modifies a noun or pronoun by telling its quality, quantity or kind, as in a tall boy.
An adverb, in contrast, modifies a verb, an adjective or another adverb.
What is the name of the border line between Pakistan and Afghanistan?
The Durand Line was fixed in 1893 by Sir Mortimer Durand and the Afghan ruler Amir Abdur Rahman Khan, and it forms the border between Pakistan and Afghanistan.
The Radcliffe Line separates Pakistan and India, and the McMahon Line is between India and China.
Point out the odd one out: America, Africa, Asia, Euro.
America, Africa and Asia are continents, while Euro is the currency of many European countries.
The word Europe, not Euro, is the name of the continent.
What is the (executive) capital of South Africa?
Pretoria is the administrative (executive) capital of South Africa. The country has three capitals: Pretoria, Cape Town and Bloemfontein.
Cape Town is the legislative capital and Bloemfontein is the judicial capital.
Ahmed is 3 years old and his sister is 3 times his age. How old will his sister be when Ahmed is 9?
The sister is 3 x 3 = 9 years old now. Ahmed becomes 9 after 6 years, so she will be 9 + 6 = 15 years.
The age difference between two people always stays the same (here 6 years).
Who is the current President of Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK) as of October 2026?
PML-N's Dr Najeeb Naqi was elected and sworn in as the 25th President of AJK on 24 September 2026 for a five-year term.
His predecessor Sultan Mehmood Chaudhry died on 31 January 2026, and acting presidents served until the new election.
Which letter comes first in alphabetical order in the word MANAGEMENT?
The letters of MANAGEMENT are M, A, N, A, G, E, M, E, N, T. Arranged alphabetically they begin with A, so A comes first.
Arranged fully, the word becomes A A E E G M M N N T.
After arranging the letters of the word MANAGEMENT in alphabetical order, which letter is the third from the last?
Alphabetical order of MANAGEMENT: A, A, A, E, E, G, M, M, N, T. Counting from the end: T, N, then M, so the third last letter is M.
MANAGEMENT has 10 letters, and the letter A appears three times in it.
What is the national mammal of the United States of America?
The American bison was declared the national mammal of the USA in 2016.
The bald eagle is the national bird and emblem of the USA, which many people loosely call its national animal.
Amjad and Ahmad together kept 20 balloons. Amjad kept three times as many as Ahmad. How many balloons did Ahmad keep?
Let Ahmad keep x balloons, so Amjad keeps 3x. Then x + 3x = 20, so 4x = 20 and x = 5.
Amjad therefore kept 15 balloons, and 15 is three times 5.
Which word is a synonym of anarchy?
Anarchy means a state of disorder due to the absence of authority, which is the same as lawlessness.
The opposite of anarchy is order or good government.
Who was the angel who brought the first wahi (revelation) to the Holy Prophet (PBUH) in the Cave of Hira?
Hazrat Jibrael (AS) came to the Prophet (PBUH) in the Cave of Hira and delivered the first verses of Surah Al-Alaq.
Hazrat Jibrael (AS) is also called Ruh-ul-Amin and brought the whole Quran over about 23 years.
One degree of an angle is equal to how many minutes?
A degree is divided into 60 minutes, and a minute into 60 seconds.
Choose the correct word to fill the blank: Why are you ___?
The verb 'are' is followed by an adjective that describes the subject, and 'angry' is the adjective.
'Angrily' is an adverb and is used to describe a verb, as in 'He spoke angrily'.
Which one is different from the rest: Ape, Chimpanzee, Monkey, Panda?
Ape, chimpanzee and monkey are all primates, while the panda is a bear.
A chimpanzee is itself a kind of ape.
Which Sahabi was appointed by the Holy Prophet (PBUH) as governor of Yemen?
The Holy Prophet (PBUH) sent Hazrat Muadh bin Jabal (RA) to Yemen as governor, judge and teacher of the people.
Before he left, the Prophet (PBUH) asked him how he would judge, and he replied that he would use the Quran, then the Sunnah, then his own reasoning.
Which of the following is another name of the Holy Quran?
Furqan, meaning the criterion that separates right from wrong, is one of the names of the Holy Quran.
Other names of the Quran are Al-Kitab, Al-Dhikr and Al-Noor; Zabur, Injeel and Tauraat are other revealed books.
What is the antonym of excrete?
To excrete is to get rid of waste matter from the body, so the opposite is to absorb or retain.
Kidneys excrete urea from the human body.
What is the antonym of prohibited?
Prohibited means not permitted, so its opposite is allowed.
Forbidden, banned and barred are synonyms of prohibited.
Which word is a synonym of applaud?
To applaud is to show approval, which means the same as to praise.
The opposite of applaud is to criticize or condemn.
What is the approximate total area of Pakistan?
Pakistan covers about 796,095 square kilometres, the 33rd largest country by area.
Balochistan is the largest province, covering about 44 percent of the country.
Around which body does the Earth revolve?
The Earth orbits the Sun, completing one revolution in about 365.25 days.
The Moon revolves around the Earth, not the Sun directly.
Which Article of the 1973 Constitution of Pakistan declares Islam as the State religion?
Article 2 states that Islam shall be the State religion of Pakistan.
Article 1 names the country the Islamic Republic of Pakistan.
In which part of Asia is India located?
India lies in South Asia, forming most of the Indian subcontinent.
SAARC was formed in 1985 by the countries of South Asia.
Aslam was 28 years old in 1945. How old will he be in 1965?
From 1945 to 1965 is 20 years, so his age is 28 + 20 = 48.
Age problems come down to adding the difference in years.
What was the code name of Pakistan's first nuclear tests of 28 May 1998?
Pakistan's tests of 28 May 1998 at Chagai in Balochistan were code-named Chagai-I.
India's 1974 test was Smiling Buddha and its 1998 tests were Shakti; Pakistan's second test on 30 May 1998 was Chagai-II.
What will be the third letter when the word AUGMENTED is arranged alphabetically?
Alphabetical order is A D E E G M N T U, so the third letter is E.
AUGMENTED has 9 letters, with E appearing twice.
Sahih Bukhari is regarded as the most authentic book of hadith after which book?
Muslims regard the Holy Quran as the most authentic book, followed in authenticity by Sahih Bukhari among the hadith books.
Imam Bukhari compiled his collection over about 16 years.
In the coordinate plane, the y-axis is the
The y-axis is the vertical number line of the plane, and the y-coordinate is called the ordinate.
The x-axis and y-axis meet at the origin (0, 0).
In the coordinate plane, the x-axis is the
The x-axis is the horizontal number line of the plane, and the x-coordinate is called the abscissa.
The two axes divide the plane into four quadrants.
Against whom was the War of Independence of 1857 (Jang-e-Azadi) fought by the people of the subcontinent?
The 1857 revolt was an uprising of Indian soldiers and people against British East India Company rule.
The British called it the Mutiny, while Muslims and Hindus of the subcontinent call it the War of Independence.
Who is the author of the famous book Hujjatullah-il-Baligha?
Hujjatullah-il-Baligha is a famous work on Islamic wisdom by Shah Waliullah Muhaddith Dehlvi.
Shah Waliullah also translated the Quran into Persian.
Ali and Ahmed have 25 balls in all. If Ali has 4 times as many as Ahmed, how many balls does Ahmed have?
Let Ahmed have x. Then x + 4x = 25, so 5x = 25 and x = 5.
Who is the Governor of Balochistan (as of 2026)?
Jaffar Khan Mandokhail is serving as Governor of Balochistan in 2026.
Sarfraz Bugti is the Chief Minister, not the Governor.
Who was the first woman to serve as Governor of the State Bank of Pakistan?
Dr Shamshad Akhtar was appointed Governor of the State Bank of Pakistan in January 2006, the first woman to hold the post.
She later served as Pakistan's caretaker finance minister in 2018.
Which barrage is commonly described as the biggest and the first barrage of Pakistan on the Indus?
Sukkur Barrage, opened in 1932, is the one Pakistani textbooks name as the first and biggest barrage on the Indus.
Sources differ on size; Guddu and Taunsa are other large barrages on the Indus.
On which document is the Constitution of Pakistan based?
The Objectives Resolution of 1949 laid down the guiding principles and was made a preamble and later a substantive part (Article 2A) of the Constitution.
It was moved by Liaquat Ali Khan in the Constituent Assembly.
Pakistan's economy is predominantly based on which sector?
Agriculture is the backbone of Pakistan's economy, supporting a large share of employment and exports like textiles from cotton.
Services now form the largest share of GDP, but agriculture remains the traditional base.
In which year was the First Battle of Panipat fought?
Babur defeated Ibrahim Lodhi at Panipat in 1526, which started the Mughal Empire in India.
The Second Battle of Panipat was fought in 1556 and the Third in 1761.
Where is the Bay of Riga located?
The Gulf (Bay) of Riga is an inlet of the Baltic Sea lying between Latvia and Estonia.
The city of Riga, the capital of Latvia, stands on this bay.
Where is the Bay of Siam located?
The Bay of Siam is an old name for the Gulf of Thailand, an arm of the South China Sea.
Siam was the former name of Thailand.
Choose the correct statement about air at higher altitude.
Air becomes lighter (thinner) as we go upward
Air becomes heavier as we go upward
Air density does not change with height
Atmospheric pressure and density decrease with height, so air becomes thinner and lighter as we go up.
This is why mountaineers use oxygen cylinders at great heights.
Where did the Quraish tribe belong?
The Quraish were the leading tribe of Makkah and custodians of the Kaaba.
The Prophet (PBUH) was born into the Banu Hashim clan of the Quraish.
To which religion did Rana Bhagwan Das belong?
Rana Bhagwandas was a Hindu who served as a judge of the Supreme Court and as acting Chief Justice of Pakistan.
He was the first non-Muslim to serve as acting Chief Justice of Pakistan.
Which Pakistani woman cricketer is the highest wicket-taker for Pakistan in women's ODIs and was the first Pakistani woman to take 100 ODI wickets?
Sana Mir reached 100 ODI wickets in February 2017 and finished with about 151 ODI wickets, the most for Pakistan women.
Nida Dar became the second Pakistani woman to reach 100 ODI wickets in April 2024.
Which type of brick was used in the buildings of the Indus Valley Civilization?
Cities like Mohenjo-daro and Harappa were built with uniform baked clay bricks, usually in a ratio of about 1:2:4.
Baked bricks made the drainage and the Great Bath waterproof and durable.
What name did the British give to the War of Independence of 1857?
The British called the events of 1857 the Sepoy Mutiny (or Indian Mutiny) because it began with Indian soldiers in the Company army.
Muslims and Indian nationalists call it the War of Independence.
Change the first word into a pronoun: Sana broke her pen.
Sana is a female name, so the pronoun that replaces it is She.
A pronoun is a word used in place of a noun.
In a bus of 30 passengers, 2/3 are male. How many females are there?
Females are 1/3 of 30, which also gives 10.
Who was the third caliph of Islam?
The order of the Rightly Guided Caliphs is Abu Bakr, Umar, Uthman and Ali. So the third was Hazrat Uthman (RA).
Hazrat Uthman (RA) is called Ghani and Zun-Noorain.
How many Rightly Guided (Pious) Caliphs of Islam were there?
The Khulafa-e-Rashideen were Hazrat Abu Bakr, Umar, Uthman and Ali (RA), four in total.
Their combined rule lasted about 30 years after the Prophet (PBUH).
The Panama Canal separates which two continents?
The Panama Canal cuts through the Isthmus of Panama, dividing North America from South America. It connects the Atlantic and Pacific Oceans.
What is the capital of the country Georgia?
Tbilisi is the capital of Georgia, a country in the Caucasus. Atlanta is the capital of the US state of Georgia.
Yerevan is the capital of Armenia.
What is the capital of Venezuela?
Caracas is the capital and largest city of Venezuela.
Bogota is the capital of Colombia.
If set A has 3 elements and set B has 4 elements, how many elements are in the Cartesian product A x B?
The number of elements in A x B is the product of the sizes: 3 x 4 = 12.
The number of elements of A x B equals that of B x A.
In which cave did the first revelation (wahi) come to the Holy Prophet (PBUH)?
The first revelation, the opening verses of Surah Al-Alaq, came in the Cave of Hira on Jabal-e-Noor near Makkah. Angel Jibreel brought it.
The Prophet (PBUH) later hid in the Cave of Thawr during the Hijrat.
In which Islamic month is Eid ul Adha celebrated?
Eid ul Adha is celebrated on 10 Dhul Hijjah, the twelfth Islamic month.
Hajj also takes place in Dhul Hijjah.
In which year was CENTO (Central Treaty Organization, formerly the Baghdad Pact) established?
The Baghdad Pact was signed in 1955 and was renamed CENTO in 1959 after Iraq withdrew.
Pakistan was a member of both CENTO and SEATO.
Through which point does the line x = 6y pass?
Putting x = 0 and y = 0 gives 0 = 0, so the line satisfies the equation at the origin. The same is true for y = 5x.
Any line of the form y = mx passes through the origin.
What was the code name of the first series of five Pakistani nuclear tests of 28 May 1998?
The five tests of 28 May 1998 were code-named Chagai-I, and the single test of 30 May 1998 was Chagai-II.
India's first nuclear test in 1974 was code-named Smiling Buddha.
Which device converts stored chemical energy into electrical energy?
A battery or electric cell uses chemical reactions to produce an electric current.
A generator converts mechanical energy to electrical energy, and a solar panel converts light energy.
Who was the first Indian Commander-in-Chief of the Indian Army (1949)?
General Kodandera Madappa Cariappa took over as Commander-in-Chief from the British officer Sir Francis Butcher on 15 January 1949.
Sources differ on the phrase first army chief, since the British general Rob Lockhart briefly led the army after 1947; most textbooks give Cariappa.
The Chauri Chaura incident of 1922 took place during which movement?
On 4 February 1922 a mob burned a police station at Chauri Chaura and killed policemen, so Gandhi suspended the Non-Cooperation Movement.
Chauri Chaura is in Uttar Pradesh, India.
What is the name of a chord that passes through the centre of a circle?
A chord through the centre touches the circle at two points and is the longest chord, called the diameter.
The diameter is twice the radius.
What is 5 o'clock in the afternoon in 24-hour time?
For afternoon hours add 12: 5 + 12 = 17, so 5 PM is 1700 hours.
Military time uses the 24-hour clock from 0000 to 2359.
What is the closest meaning of the word 'immense'?
Immense means extremely large or great.
Its opposite is tiny or minute.
Act of sticking together as a united whole
Cohesion is the state of sticking together or forming a united whole, as in a cohesive group.
The opposite of cohesion is disunity or disintegration.
What is the transpose of a column matrix?
Transposing a matrix swaps its rows and columns. A column matrix of order n x 1 becomes a matrix of order 1 x n, which is a row matrix.
The transpose of a row matrix is a column matrix.
A British commission sent to India in 1927 to review the Government of India Act 1919, with no Indian member
A commission for partition of Bengal
A Muslim League committee for Pakistan
A commission for dividing Punjab in 1947
The Simon Commission, led by Sir John Simon, arrived in India in 1928 to study constitutional reform. It had only British members, so Indian parties boycotted it.
It was announced in November 1927 and its slogan of protest was Simon Go Back.
Who wrote the book 'The Conquest of Happiness'?
The Conquest of Happiness (1930) was written by the British philosopher Bertrand Russell.
Russell won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1950.
Which companion of the Prophet (PBUH) is mentioned by name in the Quran?
Hazrat Zaid bin Haritha (RA) is named in Surah Al-Ahzab, the only companion mentioned by name in the Quran.
Abu Lahab, an enemy, is also named in Surah Al-Lahab.
In which city was the East India Company established?
The East India Company was formed in London and received its royal charter from Queen Elizabeth I.
Its first Indian trading post was set up at Surat in 1612.
In which year was the East India Company first established?
The English East India Company received its royal charter from Queen Elizabeth I on 31 December 1600.
The Company won control of Bengal after the Battle of Plassey in 1757.
Complete the sentence: If he had called me, I ___ come.
This is the third conditional (if + past perfect), which needs would have + past participle in the main clause.
Past unreal conditions use 'if + had + past participle', then 'would have + past participle'.
What kind of number is a - ib (where a and b are real and b is not zero)?
A number written in the form a + ib with real a and b is a complex number; a - ib is its conjugate, which is also complex.
A complex number has a real part and an imaginary part.
Composite means made up of several parts, and its opposite is simple, made of a single part.
In number theory the opposite of a composite number is a prime number.
Which are the two largest continents of the world by area?
Asia is the largest continent and Africa is the second largest by area.
Asia is also the most populous continent.
Which organization controls and develops Pakistan's water and electric power system?
WAPDA (Water and Power Development Authority) develops the country's water and hydropower resources.
IRSA, in contrast, distributes river water among the provinces.
Cosine is an even function, so cos(-x) = cos x.
Sine is an odd function: sin(-x) = -sin x.
What is sec x multiplied by cos x equal to?
Sec x = 1/cos x, so sec x . cos x = 1.
Cosec x is the reciprocal of sin x.
Where is the headquarters of the International Court of Justice located?
The ICJ sits in the Peace Palace in The Hague, Netherlands.
It is the principal judicial organ of the United Nations.
What is the opposite of the word crude?
Crude means raw or unrefined, so its opposite is refined, meaning processed or polished.
In manners, the opposite of crude is cultured or polite.
Who is the current President of the United States?
Donald Trump began his second term as the 47th President on 20 January 2025.
Joe Biden, the answer in 2022, was the 46th President from 2021 to 2025.
India built the Baglihar Dam on which river?
The Baglihar hydroelectric project is on the Chenab River in Jammu and Kashmir.
Pakistan raised objections under the Indus Waters Treaty and a neutral expert gave a decision in 2007.
What is the name of the angel in charge of Hell (Jahannam)?
The Quran (Surah Az-Zukhruf) mentions Malik as the keeper of Hell.
Ridwan is the angel who is the keeper of Paradise.
On which date is Pakistan Day celebrated?
Pakistan Day is celebrated on 23 March to mark the Lahore (Pakistan) Resolution of 1940.
Pakistan became a republic on 23 March 1956 when its first constitution came into force.
Between which two countries was the Tashkent Declaration of 1966 signed?
The Tashkent Declaration was signed by Pakistan and India to end the 1965 war.
The Soviet Union under Premier Kosygin mediated, and Indian PM Shastri died in Tashkent right after signing.
Which languages were declared official languages in the 1956 Constitution of Pakistan?
The 1956 Constitution made Urdu and Bengali the state languages of Pakistan.
The Bengali language movement of 1952 forced this recognition.
Where is the deepest hole (borehole) drilled by humans in the world?
The Kola Superdeep Borehole in Russia reached about 12,262 metres in 1989.
It is deeper than the Mariana Trench is deep, which is about 10,935 metres.
Which is the deepest known point of the Earth's surface?
The Challenger Deep in the Mariana Trench of the western Pacific is the deepest known point, at about 10,900 to 11,000 metres below sea level.
Mount Everest, the highest point, would be covered by more than 2 km of water if placed in the Challenger Deep.
Delight means great pleasure or joy; as a verb it means to please greatly.
A synonym of delight is joy, and an antonym is sorrow.
In which province of Pakistan is the Thar Desert located?
The Thar Desert, with Mithi and Umerkot, lies in eastern Sindh and extends into India.
It is one of the most densely populated deserts in the world.
Which of the following is a desert of Pakistan?
Cholistan in Punjab is a desert of Pakistan, along with Thar, Thal and Kharan.
Gobi is in Asia (Mongolia and China), and Sahara and Kalahari are in Africa.
In a diagonal matrix, if all the non-zero diagonal elements are equal, what is the matrix called?
A diagonal matrix with equal diagonal entries is called a scalar matrix.
A scalar matrix whose diagonal entries are all 1 is the identity matrix.
In which year (CE) did the mother of the Holy Prophet (SAW) pass away?
The Prophet (SAW) was born in 570 CE and his mother died when he was about six, around 577 CE.
The exact year is given slightly differently in some sources.
Approximately how many disbelievers (Quraish) came to fight the Muslims in the Battle of Badr?
The Makkan army at Badr was about 1000 strong, while the Muslims were about 313.
In the Battle of Uhad the Makkan army was about 3000 strong.
Which district of Pakistan has the largest population according to the census?
Lahore district had about 11.1 million people in 2017 and about 13.0 million in the 2023 census, the highest of any district.
Karachi is larger as a whole city, but it is divided into seven separate districts.
Dog is to bitch as horse is to what?
A bitch is the female dog; the female horse is a mare.
A male horse is called a stallion and a young horse a foal.
Which province of Pakistan was the first to issue driving licences to transgender persons (in 2018)?
The Khyber Pakhtunkhwa traffic police issued driving licences to transgender persons in March 2018, the first province to do so.
Punjab issued licences to 62 transgender drivers in June 2023.
According to a hadith, how many good deeds (nekis) are earned by reciting one letter of the Holy Quran?
The Prophet (PBUH) said a good deed is rewarded tenfold, so one letter of the Quran earns ten good deeds.
This hadith is narrated in Sunan al-Tirmidhi.
Which of the following countries is NOT a member of the Economic Cooperation Organization (ECO)?
ECO members are Pakistan, Iran, Turkey, Afghanistan, Azerbaijan, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan and Uzbekistan. Saudi Arabia is not among them.
ECO has ten members and its secretariat is in Tehran.
What is the meaning (synonym) of the word 'ecstasy'?
Ecstasy is a state of intense happiness or delight. Rapture is a close synonym.
The adjective form is ecstatic, meaning extremely happy.
Where was Abdul Sattar Edhi born?
Edhi was born in 1928 in Bantva in Gujarat, British India, and migrated to Pakistan after Partition.
His family belonged to the Memon community.
Who developed the first effective polio vaccine?
Jonas Salk developed the first effective inactivated polio vaccine, announced in 1955. Albert Sabin later developed the oral vaccine.
Pakistan and Afghanistan are the only countries where wild polio is still endemic.
For how many years is the Prime Minister of Pakistan elected?
The National Assembly has a term of five years and the Prime Minister, elected by it, serves for the term of the Assembly unless removed earlier.
The Constitution does not set a separate fixed term for the Prime Minister.
In whose government were the non-party based elections held in Pakistan in 1985?
General Zia-ul-Haq held non-party elections in February 1985. Muhammad Khan Junejo became Prime Minister after them.
The 1985 assemblies passed the Eighth Amendment.
Who was the Prime Minister of Pakistan when the first constitution was enforced in 1956?
The 1956 Constitution came into force on 23 March 1956 while Chaudhry Muhammad Ali was Prime Minister. He was also its main architect.
Iskander Mirza became the first President under it.
What is the antonym of the word 'embellish'?
To embellish is to make something more attractive by adding decoration. Its opposite is to disfigure or spoil.
Embellish can also mean to add exaggerated details to a story.
Enigmatic describes something puzzling and hard to understand, which is mysterious.
The noun enigma means a puzzle or riddle.
Who said that the life (character) of the Holy Prophet (PBUH) is the practical example of the Quran?
When asked about the character of the Holy Prophet (PBUH), Hazrat Ayesha (RA) replied that his character was the Quran. This means his life was the complete practical form of the Quran.
Hazrat Ayesha (RA) is among the narrators of the largest number of hadith.
Who started the Faraizi Movement in Bengal?
Haji Shariatullah started the Faraizi Movement in Bengal in the early 19th century to make Muslims follow the obligatory duties (faraiz) of Islam and give up un-Islamic customs.
After him, his son Dudu Miyan led the movement.
How many farz (obligatory acts) does Namaz have according to the Hanafi school?

Namaz has 13 farz: 6 outside the prayer (conditions such as cleanliness, covering the body, facing the Qibla, time and intention) and 7 inside it (such as takbeer, qiyam, qira'at, ruku, sajdah, qa'da akhira).
Wajibat of Namaz are different from farz, and leaving a farz makes the prayer invalid.
On which date of Ramadan was Makkah conquered (Fath-e-Makkah) in 8 AH?
Most Pakistani textbooks give 20 Ramadan 8 AH (January 630 CE) for the conquest of Makkah, when the Muslims entered the city peacefully.
Some sources give other dates in Ramadan such as 10 or 17.
What was the name of the father of Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah?
The father of Quaid-e-Azam was Jinnahbhai Poonja, a merchant in Karachi. His mother was Mithibai.
Quaid-e-Azam was born on 25 December 1876 in Karachi.
Who is the Chairman of the Federal Board of Revenue (FBR) of Pakistan, according to the latest available reports?
Rashid Mahmood Langrial was appointed FBR Chairman in August 2024 and the latest reports found show him still in office.
He succeeded Amjad Zubair Tiwana, who resigned in July 2024; the FBR chairmanship changes often, so check the latest news.
In which year was the Year of the Elephant (Aamul Feel) in which the Holy Prophet (PBUH) was born?
Abraha attacked the Kaaba with an elephant army in about 570 CE, and the Prophet (PBUH) was born in the same year.
Surah Al-Feel of the Quran describes this event.
A man walks a few steps towards the north, then turns right and walks, and then turns right again. In which direction is he now going?
Facing north, a right turn makes him face east; a second right turn makes him face south.
Two consecutive right turns always reverse the original direction.
In which year was the film Jinnah, on the life of Quaid-e-Azam, released?
The film Jinnah, starring Christopher Lee as Jinnah, was released in 1998.
It was directed by Jamil Dehlavi.
Who was the founder of the USSR (Soviet Union)?
Vladimir Lenin led the Bolshevik Revolution of 1917 and headed the new state when the USSR was formally created in 1922.
Joseph Stalin ruled the USSR after Lenin's death in 1924.
In 9/3 the numerator 9 is larger than the denominator 3, so it is an improper fraction. It simplifies to the whole number 3.
A proper fraction has a numerator smaller than its denominator, such as 5/7.
A plane uses 160 gallons of fuel to cover 330 nautical miles. About how many gallons will it use to cover 700 nautical miles?
Fuel per mile is 160 divided by 330, and 700 times 160 divided by 330 is 112000 divided by 330, which is about 339.4 gallons.
Fuel used is directly proportional to distance when the rate is constant.
What was the gift given to the Muslims on the night of Miraj?
On the night of Miraj, Allah made five daily prayers obligatory for the Muslims. The number was reduced from fifty to five.
Salah is often called the gift of Miraj.
The Gomal Pass connects Pakistan with which country?
The Gomal Pass lies on the western border of Pakistan near South Waziristan and DI Khan and leads into Afghanistan. It is an old trade route.
The Gomal River joins the Indus River in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.
Who was the first Governor of the North-West Frontier Province (now KPK) after the creation of Pakistan?
Sir George Cunningham was appointed Governor of NWFP in August 1947 at the creation of Pakistan.
Cunningham also served as governor before independence, in 1937-1946.
Who was the first Governor of Punjab after the creation of Pakistan?
Sir Francis Mudie was the first Governor of West Punjab in 1947.
He served until 1949 and was succeeded by Sir Abdur Rab Nishtar.
What was the name of the paternal grandfather of the Holy Prophet (PBUH)?
The Prophet's father was Abdullah, and Abdullah's father was Abdul Muttalib, the Prophet's paternal grandfather.
Abdul Muttalib was the son of Hashim and the one who rediscovered the Zamzam well.
In which province does the Green Line Bus Rapid Transit (BRT) system run?
The Green Line BRT runs in Karachi, which is the capital of Sindh province.
The Peshawar BRT (Zu Peshawar) is the equivalent system in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.
In which province of Pakistan is Gwadar located?
Gwadar is a port city on the Arabian Sea coast in the southwest of Balochistan.
Gwadar is the main port of the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor (CPEC).
At which place did the Holy Prophet (PBUH) deliver the sermon of Hajjatul Wida (Last Sermon)?
The Last Sermon was delivered on 9 Dhul Hijjah, 10 AH in the valley of Arafat.
It is regarded as a charter of human rights in Islam.
What is the HCF of 12 and 28?
12 = 2 x 2 x 3 and 28 = 2 x 2 x 7. The common part is 2 x 2 = 4.
Bait ul Mamoor is located in which heaven?
In the narration of the Miraj, the Prophet (PBUH) saw Bait ul Mamoor in the seventh heaven.

How many sides does a hexagon have?
The word hexagon comes from the Greek hex meaning six, so it has six sides.

Which is the highest mountain in the world?
Mount Everest, in the Himalayas on the Nepal-China border, is the highest mountain above sea level.

In which month of the Hijri calendar was the Treaty of Hudaibiya signed (6 AH)?

The complex number 1 + 0i is written (1, 0), and (a, b) times (1, 0) = (a, b) for every complex number.
Which prophet was tested by Allah with a long and severe illness and was known for his patience?
Hazrat Ayub (AS) was tested with loss of wealth, family and a long illness and kept patience, so his name is a proverb for sabr.

In which country did the first Industrial Revolution begin?

Surah Al-Maidah (5:32) says that whoever kills one innocent soul is as if he had killed all of mankind.

Where is Jabal Arafat (Jabal-e-Rahmat), the hill where pilgrims stand on 9 Dhul Hijjah?
Near Makkah, in the plain of Arafat

Change into passive voice: He said, "I have done my job."

Which one is different from the others: chimpanzee, ape, baboon, kangaroo, monkey?

The Karakoram Highway connects Pakistan with which country?
The Karakoram Highway runs from Hasan Abdal in Pakistan to Kashgar in China through the Khunjerab Pass.

Which is the hottest layer of the Earth's atmosphere?

What is the process by which water vapour is lost from the leaves of a plant?
Transpiration is the loss of water vapour through the stomata of leaves.

The order is M, N, O, so O follows N.
Which province was the first to issue driving licences to transgender persons in Pakistan (2018)?

Punjab police issued licences to transgender drivers in 2023.
Who said that the life of the Holy Prophet (PBUH) was the Quran in practice?
When asked about the Prophet's character, Hazrat Ayesha (RA) replied that his character was the Quran.

Which is the longest Surah of the Holy Quran?

Which is the longest freshwater lake in the world?

Which is the main river of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa?
The Kabul River flows from Afghanistan through Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and joins the Indus near Attock.
The Swat River is a tributary of the Kabul River.
What is the capital of Malaysia?
Kuala Lumpur is the capital and largest city of Malaysia.
Putrajaya is the administrative capital where government offices are located.
What is the approximate length of the Line of Control (LOC) between India and Pakistan?
The Line of Control runs for about 740 km through Kashmir.
The whole international border plus the LOC and Working Boundary is about 3,300 km.

What is the height of Mangla Dam (commonly quoted)?
Mangla Dam is about 147 metres (482 feet) high according to commonly cited figures.

What is the walk (running) between the hills of Safa and Marwah during Hajj and Umrah called?
Sa'i is the walking seven times between Safa and Marwah, following the footsteps of Hazrat Hajra.
Sa'i starts at Safa and ends at Marwah after seven trips.

The mean of identical numbers equals that number.

Tanzil comes from the Arabic root meaning to send down, and is used for the revelation of the Quran. The Quran itself describes itself as Tanzil.

Neil Armstrong of the Apollo 11 mission stepped on the Moon on 20 July 1969.

Number of rows by number of columns

The British East India Company and Nawab Siraj-ud-Daula of Bengal

The square root of 7 is an irrational number, about 2.6458.
How many roots does a quadratic equation have?
A quadratic equation has degree 2, and an equation of degree n has n roots. So it has 2 roots, which may be real or complex.
A quadratic equation has the form ax^2 + bx + c = 0 with a not equal to 0.
A matrix with only one row is called what?
A matrix of order 1 x n has a single row and is called a row matrix.
A matrix with only one column is called a column matrix.
In which battle were about 70 Sahaba martyred?
About 70 Sahaba were martyred in the Battle of Uhud in 3 Hijri.
Only 14 Muslims were martyred at Badr.
In which province of Pakistan is Sakhar (Sukkur) located?
Sukkur, also spelled Sakhar, is a city on the Indus River in Sindh.
In which year did Dr Abdus Salam win the Nobel Prize in Physics?
Dr Abdus Salam shared the 1979 Nobel Prize in Physics for the electroweak theory.
He was the first Pakistani and first Muslim from Pakistan to win a Nobel Prize.
What is the scalar (dot) product i . i of the unit vector i with itself?
The dot product of a unit vector with itself is the square of its magnitude, so i . i = 1 x 1 x cos 0 = 1.
The dot product of two different perpendicular unit vectors, such as i . j or i . k, is 0.
Which of the following countries is a full member of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) as of 2026?

Which fruit has its seeds on the outside of its body (on the surface of the skin)?
The tiny seed-like dots on a strawberry are actually separate fruits (achenes) on the outer surface, each containing a seed. The other fruits keep their seeds inside.
The fleshy red part of a strawberry is the swollen receptacle of the flower rather than a true fruit.
Who elects the President of Pakistan under the 1973 Constitution?
An Electoral College of the Senate, National Assembly and Provincial Assemblies
Under Article 41 of the 1973 Constitution the President is elected by an Electoral College made up of members of the Senate, the National Assembly and the four Provincial Assemblies.

What is the measure of an angle inscribed in a semicircle?
By Thales' theorem, an angle inscribed in a semicircle subtends the diameter and is always a right angle, 90 degrees.
The central angle on a diameter is 180 degrees, which is exactly double the inscribed angle.
Who demanded the separation of Sindh from the Bombay Presidency in the Muslim proposals of the 1920s?
Jinnah included the separation of Sindh from Bombay in the Delhi Muslim Proposals of 1927 and again in his Fourteen Points of 1929.
Sindh was actually separated from the Bombay Presidency in 1936 and became a separate province.
Complete the series: A C F J O ?
The gaps between letters increase by 1 each time: +2, +3, +4, +5, so the next gap is +6. O is the 15th letter and 15 + 6 = 21, which is U.
A is the 1st letter and Z is the 26th letter of the English alphabet.
Complete the series: B E J Q ?
The gaps are +3, +5, +7 (odd numbers), so the next gap is +9. Q is the 17th letter and 17 + 9 = 26, which is Z.
The gaps in this series are consecutive odd numbers starting from 3.

A treaty with the Jews of Madinah

Where did the Holy Prophet (PBUH) deliver the Last Sermon?
In the valley of Uranah on the plain of Arafat
During the Farewell Hajj the Holy Prophet (PBUH) addressed more than one hundred thousand Muslims on the 9th of Dhul Hijjah in the valley of Uranah at Arafat.
Part of the sermon was also given at Mina on the days after Arafat.
In which province of Pakistan is the city of Sibi located?
Sibi is a city in the province of Balochistan and is famous for its annual Sibi Mela and its very hot summers.
Sibi is the headquarters of Sibi Division in Balochistan.
What was the real (original) name of Hazrat Abu Bakr Siddique (RA)?
His name was Abdullah, son of Abu Quhafa, and he was given the title Siddique (the truthful) and Atiq.
Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA) was the first Khalifa of Islam and ruled from 11 AH to 13 AH.
Which prophet (AS) was tested by Allah with a long and severe illness and showed great patience?
Hazrat Ayub (AS) lost his health and wealth in a long trial and remained patient, so his patience became proverbial.

Choose the correct preposition: She shouted ____ him.
The verb shout takes at when it means to speak angrily to someone, so the correct sentence is She shouted at him.
Shout to someone means to call out so that the person can hear you, with no anger.

'Siraat' is an Arabic word meaning a path or way. In Surah Al-Fatiha, Siraat-e-Mustaqeem means the straight path.

The sister is now 3 x 5 = 15 years old. Adil needs 15 - 5 = 10 more years, so the sister will be 15 + 10 = 25.

In which country did the Black Lives Matter slogan and movement first start?

Muhammad Yousuf won the IBSF World Amateur Snooker Championship for Pakistan in 1994.

Who sold the Kashmir valley and to whom?
The British East India Company to Gulab Singh Dogra
By the Treaty of Amritsar (1846) the British East India Company sold Kashmir to Gulab Singh, the Dogra ruler of Jammu.
Gulab Singh became the first Maharaja of Jammu and Kashmir.
What is the trivial solution of a homogeneous system of linear equations in three unknowns x, y and z?
In a homogeneous system every right-hand side is 0, so putting every unknown equal to 0 always satisfies it. This is called the trivial solution (0, 0, 0).

The SUPARCO of Pakistan is an organisation that works in which field?
SUPARCO stands for Space and Upper Atmosphere Research Commission. It is Pakistan's national space agency.
SUPARCO was founded in 1961 and launched Pakistan's first satellite Badr-1 in 1990.
Ahsan Ramzan, who became the youngest world champion in 2022, is a player of which sport?

Tiananmen Square is situated in which city?
Tiananmen Square lies in the centre of Beijing, the capital of China. It is named after the Gate of Heavenly Peace.
It is one of the largest public squares in the world.

Pakistan issued its first postage stamps on 9 July 1948. They were a set of four stamps showing the Pakistani flag and national symbols.
Before that, Indian stamps overprinted with the word Pakistan were used in 1947.
In which city was the first television station of Pakistan set up?
Pakistan Television started its first broadcast from Lahore on 26 November 1964. It was a pilot station.
Karachi and Dhaka stations followed in 1966.
Marvi, the famous folk tale, belongs to which province of Pakistan?

Marvi was a village girl of Tharparkar who refused the offers of the ruler Umar Soomro.

After which event did Hazrat Abu Sufyan (RA) accept Islam?
Abu Sufyan accepted Islam at the time of the Conquest of Makkah in Ramadan 8 AH.

Abu Sufyan embraced Islam on the occasion of the Conquest of Makkah, which took place in 8 AH.
Some candidates remember 6 AH, but the Conquest of Makkah was in 8 AH.
In which province of Pakistan is the city of Sukkur located?
Sukkur is a major city on the bank of the Indus River in Sindh.
The Sukkur Barrage on the Indus, completed in 1932, irrigates large areas of Sindh.
Which surah is known as Arus-ul-Quran (the Bride of the Quran)?
Surah Ar-Rahman is called the Bride of the Quran because of its beauty and its repeated refrain.
Surah Yaseen is called the heart of the Quran.
How many surahs of the Holy Quran are named after prophets, according to the commonly given list?
The commonly counted ones are Yunus, Hud, Yusuf, Ibrahim, Nuh and Muhammad, giving six.
Counts differ between sources depending on which names are included.
Which word is closest in meaning (a synonym) to "evacuate"?
To evacuate is to leave or empty a place, which is to vacate it.
Evacuation is commonly used for disasters.
Which word is closest in meaning (a synonym) to "evidence"?
Evidence is the facts or signs that show something is true, which is proof.
Which word is closest in meaning (a synonym) to "flourish"?
To flourish is to grow well and prosper, which is to thrive.
Which word is closest in meaning (a synonym) to "malicious"?
Malicious means intending to harm, so spiteful is closest.
Which word is closest in meaning (a synonym) to "negotiate"?
To negotiate is to discuss terms in order to reach agreement, which is to bargain.
Which word is closest in meaning (a synonym) to "replenish"?
To replenish is to fill up again, which is to refill.
Which word is closest in meaning (a synonym) to "savage"?
Savage means fierce and cruel, so brutal is closest.

Who is the President of Syria as of October 2026?

Bashar al-Assad was president from 2000 until December 2024, and the post of prime minister was abolished in March 2025.
What is the other name of the Ghazwa of Tabuk?
Tabuk is also called Ghazwat al-Usrah, the Army of Hardship, because of the heat, distance and shortage of supplies.
It is the last expedition led by the Prophet (SAW) himself.
In 622 AD, the Holy Prophet (SAW) migrated from Makkah to which place?
The Hijrat of 622 AD was from Makkah to Yathrib, later called Madina.
The Islamic Hijri calendar starts from this migration.
Talha is moving towards the north and then turns right. In which direction is he facing now?
Facing north, a right turn points him towards the east.
A left turn from north would point him to the west.
What is the synonym of the word 'tame' (or 'tamed')?
To tame means to make an animal gentle and used to humans, so tame or tamed means domesticated.

The sister is 20 when Ali is 10, so she is 10 years older. When Ali is 20, she is 20 + 10 = 30.
The age difference between two people always stays the same.
What is one third of one tenth of 120?
One tenth of 120 is 12 and one third of 12 is 4.
The order of taking fractions does not change the result: 120 x 1/3 x 1/10 is also 4.
What is the term of office of the President of Pakistan?
Under the 1973 Constitution the President holds office for five years.
A person cannot hold the office of President for more than two consecutive terms.
In set theory, what does the letter Z denote?
Z stands for the set of integers, that is, all positive and negative whole numbers and zero (from the German word Zahlen).
N is natural numbers, Q is rational numbers and R is real numbers.
Which pronoun is used for a thing?
'It' is the singular pronoun used for things and animals; he and she are for persons.

Tipu Sultan was born as Sultan Fateh Ali Khan Tipu, son of Haider Ali of Mysore.

Zun-Noon is the title of which prophet?
Zun-Noon means the one of the fish and is the title of Hazrat Yunus (AS).
He was swallowed by a fish and prayed Laa ilaha illa anta subhanaka.

12 days is 1 week plus 5 days, and 5 days after Friday is Wednesday.
The week has 7 days, so only the remainder after dividing by 7 matters.

The 2nd is Friday, so the 3rd is Saturday and the 4th is Sunday. The day after tomorrow means the 4th.
Day after tomorrow means two days after today.

Xinjiang borders Gilgit-Baltistan in the north of Pakistan across the Karakoram.
The Khunjerab Pass on the Karakoram Highway connects Pakistan with Xinjiang.

Rectangle, circle and triangle are closed plane figures, while an angle is not a closed shape.
A circle is the only one without straight sides.
Who lives and works in the White House in Washington, D.C.?
The White House is the official residence and workplace of the President of the United States.
The White House has been the residence of every US President since John Adams in 1800.
Al-Lat and Al-Uzza were names of what in pre-Islamic Arabia?
Al-Lat, Al-Uzza and Manat were the three chief idols worshipped by the Arabs before Islam.
Al-Lat was worshipped at Taif and Al-Uzza near Makkah; Manat was worshipped near Madinah.

Where is the headquarters of the World Trade Organization (WTO)?
The WTO has its headquarters in Geneva, Switzerland.
The WTO was established on 1 January 1995, replacing GATT.

The 15th is 14 days after the 1st, which is exactly two weeks, so it is also a Friday.

What is sin(180 - x) equal to?
Angles 180 - x and x lie on the same horizontal level of the unit circle, so they have the same sine: sin(180 - x) = sin x.
In the same way, cos(180 - x) = -cos x.
Who was the Prime Minister of the United Kingdom at the outbreak of the Second World War in 1939?

Martial law (military government under Yahya Khan)

How many seats are reserved for non-Muslim minorities in the National Assembly of Pakistan under the 1973 Constitution?
Article 51 of the Constitution reserves ten seats in the National Assembly for non-Muslims.

Tarbela Dam on the Indus was completed later, in 1974.
