Which constitution was in force in Pakistan before the 1973 Constitution?
The 1962 Constitution, given by Ayub Khan, remained until it was abrogated in 1969 by Yahya Khan, apart from a brief interim period.
An Interim Constitution was in force in 1972 before the 1973 Constitution.
SUPARCO is the national organization of Pakistan for which field?
SUPARCO stands for Space and Upper Atmosphere Research Commission, Pakistan's national space agency.
According to the 1973 Constitution, sovereignty belongs to whom?
The Preamble and Objectives Resolution state that sovereignty over the entire universe belongs to Almighty Allah alone, exercised by the people as a sacred trust.
The authority is exercised through chosen representatives within limits set by Allah.
In which place was Benazir Bhutto buried?
Benazir Bhutto was buried in the family mausoleum at Garhi Khuda Bakhsh near Larkana, Sindh, beside her father.
She was assassinated in Rawalpindi on 27 December 2007.
What was the name of Benazir Bhutto's mother?
Begum Nusrat Bhutto, of Iranian-Kurdish origin, was the wife of Zulfikar Ali Bhutto and mother of Benazir.
She was also known as Mader-e-Jamhooriat (Mother of Democracy).
Between whom was the brotherhood (Mukhawat) established after the migration to Madinah?
The Prophet (PBUH) created brotherhood between the Muhajirin who came from Makkah and the Ansar, the helpers of Madinah.
It helped settle the Muhajirin economically in Madinah.
Near which town is the Diamer Bhasha Dam being built?
Diamer Bhasha Dam is on the Indus River about 40 km downstream of Chilas on the border of Gilgit-Baltistan and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.
It is planned as a very large dam for water storage and electricity.
What is the meaning of biased?
Prejudiced in favour of one side
A biased person unfairly favours or opposes someone or something.
A legislature chosen by the army
Bicameral means two chambers; the word camera means chamber.
Pakistan's Parliament has the National Assembly and the Senate.
Which was the first bicameral legislature of Pakistan, consisting of a National Assembly and a Senate?
The 1956 and 1962 Constitutions provided a single House (unicameral legislature). The 1973 Constitution created Parliament with two Houses, the National Assembly and the Senate.
The Bogra Formula of 1953 had proposed a two-house legislature, but it was never adopted; some sources differ on how the first bicameral body is described.
Where is the Black Sea located?
Between southeastern Europe and western Asia
The Black Sea lies between southeastern Europe and western Asia, bordered by Turkey, Bulgaria, Romania, Ukraine, Russia and Georgia.
It connects to the Mediterranean through the Bosphorus and the Dardanelles straits.
In which year did Muhammad Ali Bogra become Prime Minister of Pakistan?
Governor-General Ghulam Muhammad dismissed Khawaja Nazimuddin in April 1953 and appointed Muhammad Ali Bogra, then ambassador to the USA, as Prime Minister.
Bogra remained Prime Minister until August 1955 and was succeeded by Chaudhry Muhammad Ali.
On which date was the Bogra Formula presented to the Constituent Assembly of Pakistan?
Prime Minister Muhammad Ali Bogra presented his constitutional formula on 7 October 1953. It proposed two houses with equal provincial representation in the upper house.
The Constituent Assembly was dissolved by Ghulam Muhammad in October 1954 before the formula became a constitution.
On which date was the Pakistan-China boundary agreement signed?
Pakistan and China signed the boundary agreement on 2 March 1963 and settled the border of Gilgit-Baltistan with Xinjiang.
The Karakoram Highway linking the two countries was later built and opened to traffic in 1978.
Who bowled the fastest recorded delivery in cricket history at 161.3 km per hour?
Shoaib Akhtar bowled a delivery of 161.3 km per hour against England in the 2003 World Cup, which is still the official record.
He is known as the Rawalpindi Express.
A boy travels towards the north, then turns left and travels some distance, then turns right. In which direction is he facing now?
Facing north, a left turn makes him face west. A right turn from west makes him face north again.
Left and right turns change direction by 90 degrees each, so a left followed by a right cancel out.
In a class the number of girls is 7 more than the number of boys and the total is 33. How many boys are there?
Let boys be x, so girls are x + 7 and 2x + 7 = 33, giving x = 13. Girls are therefore 20.
Who abrogated the 1962 Constitution of Pakistan in March 1969?
When Ayub Khan resigned in March 1969, General Yahya Khan imposed martial law and abrogated the 1962 Constitution.
Iskander Mirza abrogated the 1956 Constitution in 1958.
Which reforms of 1909 introduced separate electorates for Muslims in British India?
The Indian Councils Act 1909, known as the Minto-Morley Reforms, granted separate electorates to Muslims.
The Simla Deputation of 1906 had demanded separate electorates from Lord Minto.
On which river did India build the Baglihar dam?
The Baglihar hydroelectric dam is built by India on the Chenab river in Jammu and Kashmir. The Chenab flows on into Pakistan.
Under the Indus Waters Treaty of 1960 the Chenab is one of the three western rivers allotted to Pakistan.
A train travels at 120 km/h. How much distance does it cover in 30 minutes?
30 minutes is half an hour, so distance = 120 x 1/2 = 60 km.
Distance equals speed multiplied by time.
In a bus of 24 people, 3/4 are male. What percentage are female?
Males are 3/4 of 24 = 18, so females are 24 - 18 = 6. Percentage = 6/24 x 100 = 25 percent.
The female share is 1 - 3/4 = 1/4, which is 25 percent.
Fill in the blank: We have business classes ______ night.
The preposition 'at' is used with night in the phrase 'at night'.
We say in the morning, in the evening, but at night.
Which country shares a sea border with Pakistan but no land border?
Pakistan has a maritime boundary with Oman in the Arabian Sea but no common land border. India and Iran share both land and sea boundaries, while Afghanistan is landlocked.
Pakistan's land neighbours are India, China, Afghanistan and Iran.
From which country did Pakistan acquire the J-10C fighter aircraft?
The J-10C is a Chinese fighter built by Chengdu Aircraft Corporation. Pakistan Air Force inducted it from China.
Pakistan also operates the JF-17 Thunder, which it co-developed with China.
How many days are there in a common (non-leap) calendar year?
A common year has 12 months totalling 365 days. A leap year has 366 days.
A leap year comes every four years and adds 29 February.
What is the complex number 4 - 2i called?
A number of the form a + bi with i the square root of minus 1 is a complex number. Here a = 4 and b = -2.
Approximately how many prophets came to the world in total, according to popular Islamic tradition?
A popular narration says that about 124,000 prophets were sent. The number is not given in the Quran.
Sources differ on the exact number, and 313 is commonly given for the Rasuls (messengers).
Who was the ruler of Sindh when Muhammad bin Qasim invaded it in 711 AD?
Raja Dahir of the Brahman dynasty ruled Sindh from Aror. Muhammad bin Qasim defeated him in 712 AD.
The Sindh campaign took place under Umayyad governor Hajjaj bin Yusuf.
Muhammad bin Qasim conquered Sindh during the rule of which dynasty?
Muhammad bin Qasim conquered Sindh in 711-712 AD during the reign of the Umayyad caliph Walid bin Abdul Malik. The Mughals came centuries later.
Hajjaj bin Yusuf was the Umayyad governor of Iraq who sent him.
Zakat becomes obligatory on a minimum of how many camels?
The nisab for camels is five. One goat is due on 5 to 9 camels.
Zakat on gold has a nisab of 7.5 tola, and on silver 52.5 tola.
Which canal separates Asia from Africa?
The Suez Canal in Egypt separates Africa from the Sinai Peninsula in Asia. It links the Mediterranean Sea and the Red Sea.
What is the capital of Argentina?
Buenos Aires is the capital and largest city of Argentina.
Montevideo is the capital of Uruguay.
What is the capital of Bahrain?
Manama is the capital of Bahrain, an island country in the Persian Gulf.
Doha is the capital of Qatar.
What is the capital of Cuba?
Havana is the capital and largest city of Cuba.
Kingston is the capital of Jamaica.
What is the capital of Denmark?
Copenhagen is the capital and largest city of Denmark.
Oslo is the capital of Norway.
What is the capital of India?
New Delhi is the capital of India.
Capital moved from Calcutta to Delhi in 1911.
What is the capital of Thailand?
Bangkok is the capital and largest city of Thailand.
Hanoi is the capital of Vietnam.
On which date was the Indian pilot Abhinandan Varthaman captured in Pakistan?
Wing Commander Abhinandan's aircraft was shot down on 27 February 2019, a day after the Balakot air strike. He was returned to India on 1 March 2019.
The Pakistan Air Force shot down two Indian aircraft that day.
On which date is International Women's Day celebrated?
International Women's Day is observed every year on 8 March.
International Labour Day falls on 1 May.
According to the 2023 census of Pakistan, what is the approximate total population?
The 7th Population and Housing Census 2023, the first digital census, recorded about 241.49 million people. This was approved by the Council of Common Interests.
The 2017 census had counted about 207.7 million, and some publications show slightly different later figures.
What is the line passing through the centre of a circle and touching the circle at both ends called?
A chord that passes through the centre is called a diameter. It is the longest chord of the circle.
Where is the largest railway workshop of Pakistan located?
The Mughalpura Railway Workshops in Lahore are the largest railway workshops in Pakistan.
Sources may name other railway facilities differently.
How many centimetres are there in one metre?
The prefix centi means one hundredth, so 1 metre equals 100 centimetres.
In which district of Balochistan did Pakistan conduct its nuclear tests in May 1998?
Pakistan carried out its nuclear tests in the Ras Koh Hills of Chagai district, Balochistan, on 28 and 30 May 1998.
Pakistan observes 28 May every year as Youm-e-Takbeer.
Who is the Chairman of the Senate of Pakistan as of October 2026?
Syed Yousaf Raza Gilani of the PPP was elected Chairman of the Senate and sworn in on 9 April 2024.
Sadiq Sanjrani was Senate chairman from 2018 to 2024.
Who is the Secretary General of the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation (OIC) as of October 2026?
Mauritania's Ismail Ould Cheikh Ahmed was elected OIC Secretary General on 27 August 2026 in Jeddah, succeeding Hissein Brahim Taha of Chad.
Hissein Brahim Taha held the post from 2021, which was the answer in 2022.
In mathematics, a quantity whose value can change is called a
A variable is a symbol that can take different values, unlike a constant whose value is fixed.
In the expression 3x + 5, x is the variable and 3 is the coefficient.
Who was the first Pakistani Commander-in-Chief of the Pakistan Army?
Ayub Khan became the first Pakistani C-in-C in January 1951, after British generals Messervy and Gracey.
Ayub Khan later became President of Pakistan after the 1958 coup.
According to Islamic teaching, what is recited in the ear of a newborn baby?
It is Sunnah to recite the Azan in the baby's right ear soon after birth.
Iqamah is recited in the left ear according to many scholars.
Which of the following is a Chinese COVID-19 vaccine?
Sinopharm is made in China; the other three were developed in the USA, Germany and the UK.
Sinovac and CanSino are other Chinese vaccines used in Pakistan.
Choose the correct word: If he had called me, I ____ come.
A third conditional sentence (if + past perfect) takes would have + past participle in the main clause.
The third conditional describes unreal situations in the past.
Choose the correct word: Who did you take this book ____?
The sentence means from whom the book was taken, so the preposition from is correct.
Formally the sentence would be: From whom did you take this book?
What was Abdur Rahman Chughtai famous for?
Abdur Rahman Chughtai (1894-1975) was a celebrated painter and artist whose style was inspired by Mughal and Islamic art.
His album Muraqqa-e-Chughtai is among his best known works.
In which US state is the Grand Canyon located?
The Grand Canyon, carved by the Colorado River, is in northern Arizona.
It is about 446 km long and up to 1.8 km deep.
Which city is called the City of Lights in Pakistan?
Karachi earned the name City of Lights for its lively nightlife and was once known for being awake at all hours.
Paris is the City of Lights worldwide.
In which period did the American Civil War take place?
The American Civil War between the Union and the Confederacy was fought from 1861 to 1865.
It ended slavery in the USA with the 13th Amendment in 1865.
Who led the Union side in the American Civil War?
Abraham Lincoln was President of the Union (the Northern states) during the war.
Jefferson Davis led the Confederacy and Robert E. Lee was its top general.
Mohenjo-daro, a famous site of the Indus Valley Civilization, is located in which province of Pakistan?
Mohenjo-daro lies in Larkana district of Sindh on the bank of the Indus.
Harappa, the other major city, is in Punjab.
Who were the first people to reach the summit of Mount Everest in 1953?
Edmund Hillary of New Zealand and Sherpa Tenzing Norgay reached the summit on 29 May 1953.
Mallory and Irvine vanished near the summit in 1924 and their success is unproven.
What is the closest meaning of the word 'precious'?
Precious means of great value or highly prized.
Gold and diamonds are called precious metals and stones.
What is the closest meaning of the word 'breach'?
To breach something is to break or violate it, such as a rule or a contract.
A breach can also mean a gap made in a wall.
Which line is the de facto boundary between India and China?
The India-China frontier is known as the Line of Actual Control (LAC).
The McMahon Line is the 1914 boundary in the east that China does not accept.
Coercive means forcing someone to act by pressure or threat, so its opposite is voluntary, done by free choice.
The noun form is coercion, meaning the use of force or threats to make someone do something.
Which word is a synonym of 'coercive'?
Coercive means using force or pressure to make someone obey, which is close in meaning to compulsory.
In a matrix of order 5 x 4, how many elements are there in each column?
The order 5 x 4 means 5 rows and 4 columns. Each column runs down through all the rows, so it has 5 elements.
The total number of elements in a 5 x 4 matrix is 20.
Which letter and number come next in the series: Z1, X3, V5, T7, ?
The letters move back by 2 each time (Z, X, V, T, R) and the numbers increase by 2 (1, 3, 5, 7, 9). So the next term is R9.
Letter series that skip every other letter are common in verbal tests.
To command means to give an authoritative instruction, which is the same as to order.
Command also means control over a unit, as in the command of an army.
The Nehru Report of 1928 was prepared in response to which commission?
The Simon Commission of 1927 had no Indian member, and Lord Birkenhead challenged Indians to frame a constitution. The Nehru Report was the Indian reply.
Quaid-e-Azam later put forward his Fourteen Points in 1929 in reply to the Nehru Report.
What is common in the series 4, 8, 12, 16?
4 = 4 x 1, 8 = 4 x 2, 12 = 4 x 3 and 16 = 4 x 4, so every term is a multiple of 4 with a common difference of 4.
A series with a constant difference is called an arithmetic progression.
The Partition of Bengal in 1905 gave benefits to which community?
It created the Muslim-majority province of Eastern Bengal and Assam, giving Muslims better chances in education, jobs and politics.
Hindu agitation led the British to annul the partition in 1911.
900 employees work in a company and 480 of them are men. What is the percentage of women?
The percentage of men is 53.33%, and the two percentages add up to 100.
In which year did the East India Company annex the Punjab?
After the Second Anglo-Sikh War, the Punjab was annexed to the Company's territories in 1849.
Maharaja Ranjit Singh had ruled the Punjab until his death in 1839.
Who compiled the hadith collection Musnad Ahmad?
Musnad Ahmad was compiled by Imam Ahmad bin Hanbal, founder of the Hanbali school of fiqh.
It contains tens of thousands of hadith arranged by narrator.
What is the real part of the complex number 6 + 7i?
In a + bi the real part is a, so for 6 + 7i the real part is 6 and the imaginary part is 7.
The modulus of 6 + 7i is the square root of 85.
What is the largest composite number from 1 to 99?
97 is prime, 98 = 2 x 49 and 99 = 9 x 11 has factors other than 1 and itself. So 99 is the largest composite number.
A composite number has more than two factors.
On what date was the Indian National Congress established?
The first session of the Indian National Congress was held in Bombay on 28 December 1885.
Its first president was W. C. Bonnerjee.
Which country shares the longest land border with Pakistan?
Pakistan-India border is about 3,100 to 3,300 km long, longer than the Afghan border of about 2,600 km. China and Iran borders are much shorter.
Some Pakistani textbooks name Afghanistan (Durand Line) as the longest border, so sources differ.
Which caliph received the surrender of Jerusalem (Bait-ul-Muqaddas) in 637 AD?
Jerusalem was besieged by Muslim armies under Abu Ubaidah and Amr bin al-As and its people surrendered to Caliph Umar (RA) in person.
Khalid bin Waleed (RA) conquered Damascus region, not Jerusalem.
How many articles does the Constitution of Pakistan (1973) contain?
The 1973 Constitution contains 280 articles divided into 12 parts and 7 schedules.
The Constitution was passed on 10 April 1973 and enforced on 14 August 1973.
How many members did the first Constituent Assembly of Pakistan originally have?
The first Constituent Assembly formed in 1947 had 69 members.
Its membership was later raised to 79 after the addition of more members.
What is the official name of Pakistan according to the Constitution of 1973?
Article 1 of the 1973 Constitution states that the country is the Islamic Republic of Pakistan.
Under the 1962 Constitution the name was just the Republic of Pakistan.
Which ruler introduced the Constitution of 1962 in Pakistan?
The 1962 Constitution was given by President Field Marshal Ayub Khan and set up a presidential system.
It was enforced on 8 June 1962 and abrogated in 1969 by Yahya Khan.
In which year did the construction of Tarbela Dam begin?
The contract was awarded in May 1968 and main construction ran from 1968 to 1976.
Tarbela Dam is built on the Indus River and is the largest earth-filled dam in the world.
In which year was Rawal Dam built (completed)?
Rawal Dam on the Korang River in Islamabad is listed as completed in 1962.
Some sources give 1962 as the start of construction, so sources differ.
Who performs the duties of the President of Pakistan when the President is absent or unable to act?
Article 49 of the Constitution says the Chairman of the Senate acts as President when the office is vacant or the President is absent.
If the Chairman is unavailable, the Speaker of the National Assembly acts as President.
Radians = degrees x pi/180 = 60 x pi/180 = pi/3.
Convert to passive voice: He told me about the accident.
I was told about the accident by him.
I am told about the accident by him.
The accident was told by him to me about.
I had told about the accident by him.
The past simple active becomes was/were plus past participle in passive, with the object I becoming the subject.
Passive voice puts the receiver of the action at the start of the sentence.
Which device converts mechanical energy into electrical energy?
A generator (dynamo) turns a coil in a magnetic field and produces electric current from mechanical motion.
An electric motor does the opposite and converts electrical energy into mechanical energy.
In which year was the Economic Cooperation Organization (ECO) established?
ECO was established in 1985 by Pakistan, Iran and Turkey as the successor of RCD.
RCD (Regional Cooperation for Development) was formed in 1964.
Space and Upper Atmosphere Research Commission
Satellite and Upper Atmosphere Research Corporation
Space Utilization and Planetary Research Commission
Science and Upper Atmosphere Research Council
SUPARCO is Pakistan's national space agency, called the Space and Upper Atmosphere Research Commission.
Which is the hottest layer of the Earth?
Temperature increases with depth, so the inner core is the hottest layer at around 5,000 to 6,000 degrees Celsius.
The inner core is solid due to the immense pressure even though it is so hot.
The Wakhan Corridor connects Pakistan to which province of Afghanistan?
The Wakhan Corridor is a narrow strip in Badakhshan province of north-eastern Afghanistan.
What is cosec x multiplied by tan x equal to?
Cosec x . tan x = (1/sin x)(sin x/cos x) = 1/cos x = sec x.
Tan x equals sin x divided by cos x.
Between which two countries is the longest international border in the world?
The Canada-USA border is about 8,900 km long including the Alaska border, the longest in the world.
It is also the longest undefended border.
A train covers 120 km in 1 hour 40 minutes. How much distance will it cover in 15 minutes?
1 hour 40 minutes is 100 minutes, so the speed is 120 / 100 = 1.2 km per minute. In 15 minutes the train covers 1.2 x 15 = 18 km.
At this speed the train runs at 72 km/h.
A train covers 120 km in one hour. How much distance will it cover in 12 minutes?
12 minutes is 1/5 of an hour. So the distance is 120 / 5 = 24 km.
Speed in km per minute is distance in km/h divided by 60, here 2 km per minute.
A train covers 90 km in 1 hour. How much time will it take to cover 120 km?
Time = distance / speed = 120 / 90 = 4/3 hours. 4/3 hours is 1 hour 20 minutes.
The same train covers 1.5 km every minute.
If a car covers 20 km in an hour, what distance does it cover in 30 minutes?
30 minutes is half an hour. So the distance is 20 / 2 = 10 km.
Distance equals speed multiplied by time.
If a car covers 90 km in one hour and 40 minutes, in how many minutes will it cover 1 km?
1 hour 40 minutes is 100 minutes for 90 km. So 1 km takes 100 / 90 = 10/9 minutes.
Which country developed the Sinopharm vaccine against Covid-19?
Sinopharm is a state-owned Chinese pharmaceutical company, and its BBIBP-CorV vaccine was developed in China.
Pakistan used the Chinese Sinopharm and CanSino vaccines in its Covid-19 vaccination drive.
Which of the following British reforms introduced separate electorates for the Muslims of the subcontinent?
The Indian Councils Act of 1909, known as the Minto-Morley Reforms, granted Muslims separate electorates, which was a key demand of the Simla Deputation of 1906.
The Nehru Report of 1928 rejected separate electorates, while the Cripps Mission came in 1942.
Which is the major rabi (winter) crop of Pakistan?
Wheat is sown in October to December and harvested in April to May, which makes it the main rabi crop.
Cotton, rice and sugarcane are kharif (summer) crops.
On which date is World Red Cross and Red Crescent Day celebrated?
It is observed on 8 May, the birthday of Henry Dunant, the founder of the Red Cross.
Henry Dunant won the first Nobel Peace Prize in 1901.
After the 2026 tournament, which country or countries will host the next FIFA World Cup in 2030?
FIFA awarded the 2030 World Cup to Spain, Portugal and Morocco, with opening matches in Uruguay, Argentina and Paraguay to mark the centenary.
The 2026 World Cup was hosted jointly by the United States, Canada and Mexico, and Qatar hosted in 2022.
What is the currency of Belgium (Brussels) and Finland?
Both Belgium and Finland are members of the Eurozone and use the euro.
Belgium used the Belgian franc before adopting the euro in 2002.
What is the currency of Uganda?
Uganda's national currency is the Ugandan shilling.
The capital of Uganda is Kampala.
Which is the most traded currency in the world?
The US dollar is on one side of the majority of global foreign exchange trades and is the main reserve currency.
The euro is the second most traded currency.
What is the name of China's currency?
China's official currency is the renminbi, whose main unit is the yuan.
The word renminbi means the people's currency.
Who is the current Director General of the Intelligence Bureau (IB) of Pakistan?
Fuad Asadullah Khan has led the IB since 2022 and in May 2026 the Prime Minister approved a four-year extension for him.
He was the first officer from the intelligence cadre to head the IB.
Who is the current Chancellor of Germany?
Friedrich Merz of the CDU became Chancellor in May 2025 and was still in office in October 2026.
His predecessor was Olaf Scholz (2021 to 2025), and before him Angela Merkel served from 2005 to 2021.
If a circle is divided into 360 equal parts, what is each part called?
A full circle measures 360 degrees, so each of 360 equal parts is one degree.
A quadrant is a quarter of a circle, or 90 degrees.
Which country announced the cutting of funding to the World Health Organization in 2020 and later withdrew from it?
In 2020 President Trump halted US funding to the WHO, and in 2025 the United States started its withdrawal.
The United States had been the largest single donor to the WHO.
In which country is the Khanpur (Kahnpur) Dam located?
Khanpur Dam is on the Haro River near Haripur in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan.
It supplies drinking water to Islamabad and Rawalpindi.
Hazrat Asma (R.A), known as Dhat un-Nitaqayn, was the daughter of which Sahabi?
Asma bint Abu Bakr was the elder sister of Hazrat Aisha (R.A) and helped the Prophet (PBUH) during the Hijrah.
She was the mother of Abdullah ibn Zubair (R.A).
Hazrat Umm Kulthum (R.A), who was married to Hazrat Uthman (R.A), was the daughter of whom?
Umm Kulthum was a daughter of the Prophet (PBUH) and married Hazrat Uthman after the death of her sister Ruqayyah.
This is why Hazrat Uthman is called Dhun-Nurayn, the possessor of two lights.
Which of the following was a daughter of Hazrat Ali (R.A) and Hazrat Fatima (R.A)?
Hazrat Zainab bint Ali was a daughter of Hazrat Ali and Hazrat Fatima and sister of Hasan and Husain.
Their other daughter was Umm Kulthum bint Ali.
How many days are there in a leap year?
A leap year has an extra day, 29 February, so it has 365 + 1 = 366 days.
A leap year comes every four years, for example 2024 and 2028.
Who acts as the President of Pakistan in his absence?
Under Article 49 of the Constitution, the Chairman of the Senate acts as President when the office is vacant or the President is absent.
If the Chairman is not available, the Speaker of the National Assembly acts as President.
At what age did the Holy Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) pass away?
According to the most accepted account, the Prophet (PBUH) passed away in 11 AH at the age of 63 years.
He is buried in Madinah in the room of Hazrat Aisha (R.A).
When did the Al-Khalid main battle tank enter service with the Pakistan Army?
The Al-Khalid (MBT-2000), developed by Pakistan with Chinese help, entered service in 2001.
Some sources mention 2004 for its formal presentation, and the upgraded Al-Khalid-I was inducted in July 2020.
What is the definition of a noun?
A word that describes an action
A word that names a person, place, thing or idea
A word that describes a noun
A word that joins two sentences
A noun is a naming word: it names a person, place, animal, thing or idea.
A verb shows action, an adjective describes a noun, and a conjunction joins words or clauses.
A matrix with equal number of rows and columns
A matrix with only one row
A matrix with all elements zero
A matrix with only one column
A square matrix has the same number of rows as columns, for example 3 by 3.
Only square matrices have determinants and can have inverses.
What is the radian measure of 60 degrees?
Radians = degrees x pi/180 = 60 x pi/180 = pi/3.
In which year did Allama Iqbal deliver his famous Allahabad Address (Khutba)?
Allama Iqbal gave his presidential address at the Muslim League session in Allahabad in December 1930, proposing a Muslim state in north-west India.
The Lahore Resolution followed ten years later, in 1940.
In which Hijri year was the Last Sermon (Khutba Hujjat ul Wida) delivered?
The Prophet (SAW) performed his only Hajj, the Farewell Pilgrimage, in 10 AH (632 CE).
He passed away a few months later, in 11 AH.
Which word is a synonym of 'demise'?
Demise means death or the end of something.
In which body were the Basic Democrats of Ayub Khan's system mainly represented?
Electoral college for President and assemblies
Basic Democrats, elected from union councils, formed the electoral college that elected the President and members of the assemblies.
The system was announced in 1959 and used in the 1965 presidential election.
How many Basic Democrats were there in Ayub Khan's system (40,000 in each wing)?
Ayub Khan's Basic Democracies had 80,000 members, 40,000 in East Pakistan and 40,000 in West Pakistan.
The number was later raised to 120,000, but 80,000 was the original figure.
What is the derivative of tan x with respect to x?
d/dx (tan x) = d/dx (sin x / cos x) = (cos^2 x + sin^2 x) / cos^2 x = sec^2 x.
The derivative of cot x is minus cosec squared x.
Pakistan's friendship with which neighbouring country is described as higher than the mountains and deeper than the oceans?
Pakistani leaders describe the Pakistan-China friendship as higher than the Himalayas and deeper than the oceans.
The Karakoram Highway and CPEC link the two countries.
In which province of Pakistan is the Cholistan Desert located?
The Cholistan Desert lies in southern Punjab, near Bahawalpur.
It is locally called Rohi and is an extension of the Thar Desert.
In which province of Pakistan is the Thal Desert located?
The Thal Desert lies in Punjab between the Jhelum and Indus rivers, covering districts such as Bhakkar, Layyah and Khushab.
It is now largely irrigated by the Thal Canal.
Which lake is known as the world's largest permanent desert lake?
Lake Turkana in northern Kenya lies in a desert region and is the largest permanent desert lake, nicknamed the Jade Sea.
It is a very alkaline lake in the Great Rift Valley.
What is the determinant of a diagonal matrix?
For a diagonal matrix all off-diagonal entries are zero, so the determinant is the product of the diagonal elements.
The sum of diagonal elements is called the trace.
Who is known as the youngest Microsoft Certified Professional, and from which country did she come?
Arfa Karim Randhawa of Faisalabad, Pakistan, became a Microsoft Certified Professional at age 9 in 2004.
She died in January 2012 at age 16, and a software technology park in Lahore is named after her.
A square matrix whose off-diagonal elements are all zero
A matrix with all elements equal
A matrix with one row only
A matrix whose determinant is always 1
A diagonal matrix is a square matrix in which every element outside the main diagonal is zero.
Scalar and identity matrices are special diagonal matrices.
If the side of a square is a, what is the length of its diagonal?
By Pythagoras, diagonal = square root of (a^2 + a^2) = a times root 2.
The diagonals of a square are equal and bisect each other at right angles.
What is the diameter of a circle whose radius is 28?
What is the radius of a circle with diameter 52 cm?
Area of this circle is pi x 26 x 26.
Arrange the letters of the word MANAGEMENT in alphabetical order. Which letter is third from the last?
The letters in order are A, A, E, E, G, M, M, N, N, T. From the end: T, N, then N, so the third last is N.
The word MANAGEMENT has ten letters.
Which word comes first in the dictionary?
Compare the third letter: Addidas has d, which comes before i in Adiabatic, Adjust (j) and Adit (i).
Dictionary order compares letters from left to right.
On which date did the singer Lata Mangeshkar die?
Lata Mangeshkar, the Indian playback singer, died in Mumbai on 6 February 2022.
Approximately how many disbelievers (Quraish) took part in the Battle of Uhad?
The Quraish marched to Uhad in 3 AH with about 3000 men, against about 700 Muslims at the start.
At Badr the Quraish army was about 1000 strong.
Where was democracy first practised in the world?
Democracy began in the ancient Greek city-state of Athens around the 5th century BC.
The word democracy comes from the Greek words demos (people) and kratos (rule).
Who developed the first successful polio vaccine?
Jonas Salk developed the inactivated polio vaccine, announced in 1955.
Albert Sabin later developed the oral polio vaccine.
The voice of which animal is described in the Holy Quran as the worst of voices?
Surah Luqman says the harshest of voices is surely the voice of the donkey.
The advice is given by Hazrat Luqman to his son in Surah Luqman.
Which President of Pakistan abrogated the 1956 Constitution in October 1958?
President Iskander Mirza abrogated the 1956 Constitution on 7 October 1958 and imposed martial law.
Ayub Khan, the army chief, became Chief Martial Law Administrator and soon removed Mirza.
What is the opposite of the word diversity?
Diversity means variety; its opposite is uniformity, meaning sameness.
Diversity is a synonym of variety.
Viceroy Lord Curzon partitioned Bengal in 1905, creating the Muslim-majority province of Eastern Bengal and Assam.
The partition was annulled in 1911 under Lord Hardinge.
Which document paved the way for the constitution of Pakistan?
The Objective Resolution of 1949 laid down the guiding principles for the constitutions of Pakistan and became their preamble.
It was moved by Liaquat Ali Khan in the Constituent Assembly on 12 March 1949.
If one dozen pencils cost Rs 60, what is the cost of 5 pencils?
One pencil costs 60 / 12 = Rs 5, so 5 pencils cost 5 x 5 = Rs 25.
If one dozen pencils cost Rs 27, what is the price of 4 pencils?
Four pencils are one third of a dozen, so the cost is 27 / 3 = Rs 9.
What is the national dress of Pakistan?
Shalwar Kameez is worn across all provinces and is recognised as the national dress of Pakistan.
Sherwani is the national dress for formal wear of men and is linked with Quaid-e-Azam.
What is the special dress of Hajj called?
Pilgrims wear the Ihram, two unstitched white sheets for men, while performing Hajj and Umrah.
Ihram also names the sacred state that a pilgrim enters.
For how many days did the 1965 Pakistan-India war last?
The war began on 6 September 1965 and the ceasefire came on 23 September 1965, a total of 17 days.
The Tashkent Declaration of January 1966 followed the war.
What is the cutting of hair by a pilgrim at the end of Hajj called?
Halq means shaving the head, and qasr means trimming the hair; one of them is done to leave the state of Ihram.
Women only trim a fingertip length of hair.
Who was the Prime Minister of India when the Indus Waters Treaty was signed in 1960?
Jawaharlal Nehru signed the treaty with Pakistan's President Ayub Khan at Karachi on 19 September 1960.
The World Bank mediated the treaty.
What is the measure in degrees of each angle (corner) of a square?
A square has four equal angles and they sum to 360 degrees, so each is 360 / 4 = 90 degrees.
A rectangle also has four right angles.
ECO stands for Economic Cooperation Organization, a regional group of Asian countries.
It succeeded the Regional Cooperation for Development (RCD) of 1964.
Abdul Sattar Edhi, the famous humanitarian known as the Angel of Mercy, belonged to which country?
Edhi spent his life in Pakistan and founded the Edhi Foundation in Karachi. He is regarded as one of the greatest humanitarians of Pakistan.
Edhi died in Karachi on 8 July 2016.
Which of these international days is observed by the United Nations in January (on 24 January)?
International Day for the Eradication of Poverty
The International Day of Education is observed on 24 January. World Refugee Day is 20 June and the Day for the Eradication of Poverty is 17 October.
Mother's Day is not a UN day and falls in May in most countries.
If one egg takes 2 minutes to boil, how many minutes will 5 eggs take when boiled together in the same pot?
Eggs boil at the same time in the same pot, so the time does not depend on the number of eggs. All 5 eggs take 2 minutes.
This is a classic logic puzzle where the obvious multiplication is wrong.
Akbar is older than Ahmad and Umair is older than Akbar. Who is the eldest?
Umair is older than Akbar, and Akbar is older than Ahmad. So the order is Umair, Akbar, Ahmad and Umair is the eldest.
Chain the comparisons to rank all persons.
If Akbar is elder than Ahmad and Adnan is elder than Akbar, then who is the eldest?
Adnan is elder than Akbar, and Akbar is elder than Ahmad. So Adnan is the eldest.
The youngest in this chain is Ahmad.
In which pact were separate electorates for Muslims granted?
Under the Lucknow Pact of 1916 the Congress accepted the Muslim League's demand for separate electorates for Muslims.
Separate electorates were first given in the Morley-Minto Reforms of 1909.
What is a set that has no element called?
A set with no element is called the null set or empty set and is written as a circle with a slash or as curly brackets with nothing inside.
The empty set is a subset of every set.
What is a set with exactly one element called?
A set containing only one element, such as the set containing 5 alone, is called a singleton set.
A singleton set has exactly two subsets.
If every element of set A is also an element of set B, then A is called what of B?
When all elements of A belong to B, A is a subset of B, written A is contained in B.
B is then called a superset of A.
Which one is different from the rest: cow, snake, elephant, monkey?
Cow, elephant and monkey are mammals, while a snake is a reptile.
Mammals are warm-blooded and feed milk to their young.
What is the meaning of the word 'embellish'?
To make more attractive by adding decoration
Embellish means to decorate or beautify something, or to add extra details to a story.
Adorn and ornament are synonyms of embellish.
When was the partition of Bengal enforced by Lord Curzon?
Lord Curzon divided Bengal into East Bengal and Assam and West Bengal, and the partition took effect on 16 October 1905.
On which date did the Indian Independence Act 1947 come into effect, creating Pakistan and India?
The Act was passed by the British Parliament on 18 July 1947 and the two dominions came into being on 15 August 1947 at midnight.
Which of the following are the vowels of the English alphabet?
The five vowel letters of English are A, E, I, O and U.
The English alphabet has 26 letters, so 21 are consonants.
If RAT is coded as TAR (letters reversed), then what is FAT equal to?
RAT becomes TAR by reversing the order of letters. Reversing FAT gives TAF.
Reversal codes are the simplest letter codes.
In trigonometry, what is tan x equal to?
cos x divided by sin x
sin x divided by cos x
Tangent is the ratio of sine to cosine, so tan x equals sin x divided by cos x.
Cot x is the reciprocal of tan x.
What is cosecant x equal to?
sin x divided by cos x
Cosecant is the reciprocal of sine, so cosec x = 1 / sin x.
Sec x = 1 / cos x and cot x = 1 / tan x.
Simplifying gives x - 7 = 0, which has highest power 1 of x, so it is linear and gives x = 7.
A linear equation in one variable has exactly one root.
In whose era was the Battle of Yamama fought?
The Battle of Yamama was fought in 11-12 AH against the false prophet Musaylima during the caliphate of Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA).
Many Huffaz died there, which led to the first compilation of the Quran.
Who headed the committee for the collection of the Holy Quran in the era of Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA)?
Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA) appointed Zaid bin Thabit, the Prophet's scribe of revelation, to collect the Quran into one volume.
Zaid also led the committee in the era of Hazrat Usman (RA).
The Holy Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) belongs to the descendants of which prophet?
The Prophet (PBUH) descended from Hazrat Ismail (AS), son of Hazrat Ibrahim (AS), through the Quraysh.
Hazrat Essa (AS) had no father and no direct descendants.
How many end points does a ray have?
A ray starts at one fixed point and extends endlessly in one direction, so it has one end point.
A line segment has two end points and a line has none.
How many enemy soldiers marched against the Muslims in the Battle of Uhud?
The Quraysh army at Uhud numbered about 3000 soldiers, while the Muslims were about 700.
The Quraysh were led by Abu Sufyan.
Which uncle of Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) was among his bitter enemies?
Abu Lahab (Abdul Uzza) strongly opposed the Prophet (PBUH) and a Surah of the Quran is named after him. Abu Jahal was not his uncle.
Which country connects Asia and Europe?
Turkey lies partly in Asia (Anatolia) and partly in Europe (Thrace), separated by the Bosphorus strait.
Istanbul is the only major city located on two continents.
Which event did the Holy Prophet (PBUH) take part in after the Harb-e-Fijar?
After the Harb-e-Fijar, the Holy Prophet (PBUH) took part in Hilf-ul-Fudul, a pact formed in Makkah to help the oppressed and protect travellers and the weak. He was a young man at the time.
The Holy Prophet (PBUH) later said that he would still accept such a pact even in Islam.
On what date did Pakistan conduct its first nuclear tests?

Pakistan carried out its first nuclear tests in the Chagai hills, Balochistan, on 28 May 1998 (five tests, Chagai-I), followed by one more on 30 May 1998. This was a reply to India's tests earlier that month.
28 May is observed in Pakistan as Youm-e-Takbeer.
What is the measure of each external angle of a regular hexagon?
The sum of the external angles of any polygon is 360 degrees. A hexagon has 6 sides, so each external angle is 360 divided by 6 = 60 degrees.
Each internal angle of a regular hexagon is 120 degrees.
What is the measure of each external angle of a regular octagon?
The sum of the external angles of any polygon is 360 degrees. An octagon has 8 sides, so each external angle is 360 divided by 8 = 45 degrees.
Each internal angle of a regular octagon is 135 degrees.
What is meant by Laissez-faire in economics?
Minimum government interference in the economy
Laissez-faire is a French term meaning let do. It is the policy that the government should interfere as little as possible in economic affairs and leave markets free.
Adam Smith is the economist most associated with ideas of free markets.
Which word comes first in the dictionary: False, Fallow, Faithful, Fallable, Falcon?
All words begin with Fa. The third letters are i (Faithful), l (the rest), so Faithful comes first. Then Falcon, Fallable, Fallow and False follow.
Dictionary order compares letters one by one from the left.
Hazrat Ali (RA) belonged to which family (clan) of Quraish?
Hazrat Ali (RA) was the son of Abu Talib, who was a son of Abdul Muttalib of Banu Hashim. He was thus a cousin of the Holy Prophet (PBUH).
The Holy Prophet (PBUH) also belonged to Banu Hashim.
The family tree of the Holy Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) connects to which prophet?
The lineage of the Holy Prophet (PBUH) goes through Adnan back to Hazrat Ismail (AS), the son of Hazrat Ibrahim (AS).
Hazrat Ismail (AS) settled in Makkah with his mother Hazrat Hajra.
For what industry is Gaddani in Balochistan famous?
Gaddani, on the coast of Balochistan near Karachi, has one of the largest ship breaking yards in the world, where old ships are dismantled.
For which product is Sialkot famous?
Sialkot is world famous for sports goods, such as footballs, and also for surgical instruments and leather goods.
Footballs made in Sialkot have been used in FIFA World Cups.
For what is Ziyarat in Balochistan famous?
Ziyarat is a hill town famous for the Quaid-e-Azam Residency, where Quaid-e-Azam spent his last days in 1948, and for one of the largest juniper forests in the world.
The Residency was damaged by a terrorist attack in 2013 and later rebuilt.
How many Nobel Prizes in Physics has Pakistan received so far?
Dr Abdus Salam received the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1979, shared with Glashow and Weinberg. No other Pakistani has won in Physics.
Dr Abdus Salam was the first Pakistani Nobel laureate and Malala Yousafzai won the Peace Prize in 2014.
A car travels at 120 km/h and another car travels twice as fast. How far will the second car travel in 30 minutes?
The second car's speed is 2 x 120 = 240 km/h. In 30 minutes (half an hour) it travels 240 x 1/2 = 120 km.
Son is to father as nephew is to what?
A son is the child of his father, and a nephew is the child of the brother or sister of an uncle or aunt, so the relation is nephew to uncle.
The female counterpart of a nephew is a niece.
What was the name of the father of the Holy Prophet Muhammad (PBUH)?
The father of the Holy Prophet (PBUH) was Hazrat Abdullah bin Abdul Muttalib, who died before the Prophet was born.
His mother was Hazrat Amina bint Wahab.
Surah Al-Fatiha is also called by which name?
Surah Al-Fatiha is also called Umm-ul-Kitab (Mother of the Book) and Umm-ul-Quran because it sums up the message of the Quran.
It is also called Sab'a Mathani and is recited in every rakat of Namaz.
For which crime was Fatimah bint Aswad (a woman of Banu Makhzum) punished in the time of the Holy Prophet (PBUH)?
Fatimah bint Aswad of Banu Makhzum was found guilty of theft, and the Holy Prophet (PBUH) ordered the punishment for theft. He refused to let rank or family influence the decision.
He said that nations before them were destroyed because they punished the poor but spared the rich.
Which day is observed in Pakistan on 5th February every year?
Pakistan observes 5 February as Kashmir Solidarity Day to express support for the people of Indian-administered Kashmir.
Pakistan Day is on 23 March and Defence Day on 6 September.
Which woman is mentioned by name in the Quran?
Hazrat Maryam (AS), the mother of Prophet Isa (AS), is the only woman named in the Quran.
A complete Surah of the Quran, Surah Maryam, is named after her.
How many Pakistanis have received the Nobel Prize in Physics?
Only Dr Abdus Salam has won the Nobel Prize in Physics, in 1979.
Malala Yousafzai is the other Pakistani Nobel laureate, winning the Peace Prize in 2014.
SUPARCO, the national agency of Pakistan, belongs to which field?
SUPARCO stands for Space and Upper Atmosphere Research Commission and deals with space technology.
Who was the first Field Marshal of Pakistan?
Muhammad Ayub Khan promoted himself to the rank of Field Marshal in 1959.
Asim Munir was promoted to Field Marshal in May 2025, making him the second.
Subtract x from both sides: 2x - 9 = 7, so 2x = 16 and x = 8.
Subtract 2x from both sides: x - 9 = 7, so x = 16.
Cross multiplying gives 14x = 56, which also gives x = 4.
What is the mean of 1, 3, 5 and 6?
The mean is the sum of values divided by the number of values.
Which letter comes after M in the English alphabet?
The alphabet runs L, M, N, so N follows M.
Which letter comes after O in the English alphabet?
The alphabet runs N, O, P, so P follows O.
O is the 15th letter and P the 16th.
Arrange the letters 'IYTC' to form a meaningful word.
Rearranging I, Y, T, C gives the word CITY.
An anagram uses all the given letters exactly once.
On what date was the United Nations (UNO) formally established?
The UN Charter came into force on 24 October 1945 after ratification by the main founding states.
The Charter was signed on 26 June 1945 at San Francisco, and 24 October is celebrated as UN Day.
Which is the largest fort of Pakistan?
Ranikot Fort in Sindh has walls about 26 km long and is often called the largest fort in the world.
It is also known as the Great Wall of Sindh.
Between whom was the Ghazwa (Battle) of Badr fought?
The Muslims of Madinah and the Quraish of Makkah
The Muslims and the Jews of Khyber
The Muslims and the Byzantine army
The Muslims and the tribe of Thaqif at Taif
Badr was fought in 2 AH between the small Muslim army led by the Holy Prophet (PBUH) and the much larger army of the Quraish of Makkah.
Badr is called Yaum-ul-Furqan, the day that separated right from wrong.
Near which city is the mountain where the Battle of Uhud was fought?
The Battle of Uhud was fought at the foot of Mount Uhud, a few kilometres north of Madinah.
The battle took place in 3 AH between the Muslims and the Quraish of Makkah.
Which fraction comes next in the series: 3/5, 5/8, 8/12, 12/17, ?
Numerators are 3, 5, 8, 12, 17 with differences 2, 3, 4, 5, so the next is 17. Each denominator equals the next numerator, and the denominators 5, 8, 12, 17 continue with 17+6 = 23.
Each fraction's numerator equals the previous fraction's denominator.
What is the currency of France?
France uses the euro, which replaced the French franc in 2002.
The euro is shared by most countries of the European Union eurozone.
Which party formed the government in the North-West Frontier Province (now KPK) just before the creation of Pakistan in 1947?
After the 1946 elections the Congress under Dr Khan Sahib formed the ministry in the NWFP, which stayed in office until it was dismissed in August 1947.
The people of the NWFP voted for Pakistan in the referendum of July 1947.
If the first day of a month is Friday, which day will the 17th be?
The 15th is 14 days (two full weeks) after the 1st, so it is also a Friday. The 17th is two days later, a Sunday.
A week has 7 days, so dates 7 apart fall on the same weekday.
Change the narration (direct speech) of: He bade farewell to his friends.
He said to his friends that good-bye.
He told his friends, "Farewell to you."
To bid farewell means to say good-bye, so in direct speech it becomes: He said to his friends, "Good-bye."
Similar idioms: bade welcome becomes said, "Welcome", and wished becomes said, "Good luck."
What is the full form of PIA?
PIA stands for Pakistan International Airlines, the national flag carrier of Pakistan.
PIA began as Orient Airways in 1946 and took its present name in 1955.
In which city were the Olympic Games named Tokyo 2020 held?
The 2020 Summer Olympics were awarded to Tokyo, Japan. Because of COVID-19 they were postponed and held in Tokyo from July to August 2021.
How many doors (gates) does the Holy Kaaba have?
The Kaaba has a single door, on its north-east wall, about two metres above ground level.
The door is made of gold-plated material and is opened only on special occasions.
Who served as both Governor General and Prime Minister of Pakistan?
Khawaja Nazimuddin was Governor General from 1948 to 1951 and then Prime Minister from 1951 to 1953.
He became Governor General after the death of Quaid-e-Azam.
Robert E. Lee was a famous general of which war?
Robert E. Lee commanded the Confederate army of Northern Virginia in the American Civil War (1861-1865). His main opponent on the Union side was Ulysses S. Grant.
Lee surrendered to Grant at Appomattox Court House in April 1865.
Who is the President of Germany?
Frank-Walter Steinmeier has been the Federal President of Germany since March 2017 and was re-elected in 2022. His second term ends in March 2027.
The President is the head of state, while the Chancellor (currently Friedrich Merz) is the head of government.
In which Ghazwa was the Holy Prophet (PBUH) wounded?
In the Battle of Uhad (3 AH) the Prophet (PBUH) was wounded in the face and his blessed tooth was broken.
The Muslim archers left their post on the hill during Uhad, which let the Quraish attack from behind.
A brother is 5 years old and his sister is three times his age. What will be the sister's age when the brother is 12?
The sister is 3 x 5 = 15 years old now. The brother becomes 12 after 7 years, so the sister will be 15 + 7 = 22.
The age difference between two people always stays the same (here 10 years).
What is jute commonly known as?
Jute is called the golden fibre because of its shiny golden-brown colour and its high value as a cash crop.
Bangladesh and India are the largest producers of jute.
In which province of Pakistan is Gorakh Hill located?
Gorakh Hill is a hill station in the Kirthar range in Dadu district of Sindh.
It stands at about 5,600 feet and is one of the highest points in Sindh.
Who was the maternal grandfather of the Holy Prophet (PBUH)?
The Prophet's mother was Hazrat Amina bint Wahb, so her father Wahb bin Abd Manaf was his maternal grandfather.
Wahb belonged to the Banu Zuhra clan of Quraish.
The sign greater than or equal to is used in which type of mathematical statement?
The sign for greater than or equal to compares two quantities without saying that they are exactly equal, so it forms an inequality.
The sign for less than or equal to is also used in inequalities.
To which language group does the Sindhi language belong, among the given options?
Sindhi is an Indo-Aryan language that developed from Sanskrit and Prakrit. Of the given options, Sanskrit is the ancestral language group.
Sindhi is the official language of Sindh province and is written in a Perso-Arabic script.
What is the first group of the periodic table called?
Group 1 contains lithium, sodium, potassium, rubidium, caesium and francium, which are called alkali metals.
Hydrogen sits at the top of Group 1 but is not an alkali metal.
Choose the correct word: They ___ seeds in flowers.
The subject They is plural, so the simple present plural verb grow is needed.
The verb grows is used with singular subjects such as he, she or it.
The old fort of Gwadar/Chabahar region lies on the coast of the Gulf of which?
Gwadar and Chabahar lie on the coast near the Gulf of Oman, at the mouth of the Persian Gulf.
Pakistan bought Gwadar from Oman in 1958.
Which hadith is called Muttafaq Alaih?
A hadith narrated by both Imam Bukhari and Imam Muslim
A hadith narrated by only one companion
A hadith narrated by Imam Tirmidhi
Muttafaq Alaih (agreed upon) is a hadith recorded in both Sahih Bukhari and Sahih Muslim.
Such hadith are considered to be of the highest authenticity.
To whom did Hazrat Umar (RA) hand over the Quran copy that was compiled in the time of Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA)?
The compiled copy of the Quran was kept with Hazrat Umar (RA) and, after his death, with his daughter Hazrat Hafsa (RA).
Hazrat Usman (RA) later borrowed this copy to prepare standard copies of the Quran.
Who received the Nishan-e-Haider for bravery in the Kargil War of 1999?
Captain Karnal Sher Khan Shaheed was awarded the Nishan-e-Haider for his bravery in Kargil.
Havaldar Lalak Jan Shaheed also received the Nishan-e-Haider for Kargil.
What is the straight line that divides a circle into two equal halves called?
A chord passing through the centre of a circle is the diameter and it cuts the circle into two equal semicircles.
The diameter equals twice the radius.
Who is the author of the novel The Pursuit of Happiness (2001)?
The novel The Pursuit of Happiness was written by the author Douglas Kennedy.
Do not confuse it with The Conquest of Happiness by Bertrand Russell.
What is the HCF of 12 and 16?
12 = 2 x 2 x 3 and 16 = 2 x 2 x 2 x 2. The common factors are 2 x 2, so the HCF is 4.
Where is the headquarters of the International Labour Organization (ILO) located?
The ILO, a specialised agency of the United Nations, has its headquarters in Geneva, Switzerland.
The ILO was founded in 1919 and became a UN agency in 1946.
Where is the headquarters of the African Union located?
The African Union has its headquarters in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia.
The African Union replaced the Organisation of African Unity in 2002.
How many gates (doors) does Jannah have?
According to the hadith, Jannah has eight gates, one of which is called Ar-Rayyan.
Golan Heights are occupied by which country?
Israel captured the Golan Heights from Syria in the 1967 war and later annexed it.
The Golan Heights are internationally recognised as Syrian territory.
According to the Quran, who will be in the lowest depths of the Fire?
Surah An-Nisa says the hypocrites will be in the lowest depths of the Fire.
Hypocrites outwardly claimed faith while hiding disbelief.
With the help of which country did Pakistan carry out the Saindak project?
The Saindak copper-gold project in Balochistan was developed with Chinese help by the Metallurgical Corporation of China.
Saindak is in Chagai district, Balochistan.
Which is the highest mountain range in the world?
The Himalayas contain Mount Everest and most of the world's highest peaks.
The Andes are the longest continental mountain range.
For how many years did the Prophet (PBUH) preach Islam in Makkah before the Hijrat to Madina?
The Prophet (PBUH) received his first revelation at 40 and migrated at 53, so he preached in Makkah for about 13 years.
He then lived about 10 years in Madina.
On which hills is the city of Islamabad situated?
Islamabad lies at the foot of the Margalla Hills, part of the Himalayan foothills.
Faisal Mosque is at the foot of the Margalla Hills.
Ali is 5 years old and his sister is 3 times his age. How old will his sister be when Ali is 10 years old?
The sister is 3 x 5 = 15, so she is 10 years older than Ali. When Ali is 10 she will be 20.
The age difference between two people stays the same over time.
Ali is 5 years old and his sister is 3 times his age. How old is his sister?
She is 10 years older than Ali.
Ali is 5 years old and his sister is 3 times his age. When Ali is 11 years old, how old will his sister be?
The sister is 15, so she is 10 years older. When Ali is 11 she will be 11 + 10 = 21.
The age difference stays 10 years forever.
How many disbelievers of Quraish were killed in the Battle of Badr?
About 70 Quraish were killed and 70 captured at Badr.
Which Act of 1909 first introduced separate electorates for Muslims in British India?
The Indian Councils Act of 1909 (Morley-Minto Reforms) gave Muslims separate electorates.
Quaid-e-Azam later accepted separate electorates in the Lucknow Pact of 1916.
Who was the first woman to head an elected democratic government in Pakistan?
Benazir Bhutto became Prime Minister in 1988 after elections.
She was the first woman to lead a Muslim-majority country's government.
On which date of Rabi ul Awwal is the birthday of the Holy Prophet (PBUH) commonly observed?
Most Sunni Muslims observe the birth of the Prophet (PBUH) on 12 Rabi ul Awwal.
Shia scholars commonly observe it on 17 Rabi ul Awwal.
Fill in the blank: The children ___ the honey on bread.
The plural subject children takes the plural verb eat.
Choose the correct word: Nadia's father ___ honey.
Father is singular and the sentence is active present, so the verb is buys.
A singular third person subject takes a verb ending in s in the simple present.
Boy is to girl as horse is to what?
A girl is the female of a boy; the female of a horse is a mare.
A young horse is a foal.
A man travels 90 km in 1 hour at a constant speed. In how many minutes will he cover 1 km?
90 km takes 60 minutes, so 1 km takes 60 divided by 90 = 2/3 minute, which is 40 seconds.
Speed 90 km per hour equals 1.5 km per minute.
Infections in the human body are caused by which of the following?
Germs (pathogens such as bacteria and viruses)
Infections occur when disease-causing germs such as bacteria, viruses, fungi or parasites enter the body and multiply.
Antigens are substances that trigger the immune system, while antibodies are made to fight them.
What was the old name of Hyderabad (Sindh)?
Hyderabad in Sindh was built on the site of the old fort town called Neerunkot (Nerunkot), which was ruled by the Kalhora dynasty later.
Mian Ghulam Shah Kalhora founded the modern city of Hyderabad in 1768.
If the eccentricity e of a conic is greater than 1, the conic is a:
A conic has e = 0 for a circle, e less than 1 for an ellipse, e = 1 for a parabola and e greater than 1 for a hyperbola.
A circle is the special case of an ellipse with zero eccentricity.
Hazrat Ibrahim (AS) is known for his confrontation with which tyrant ruler?
Hazrat Ibrahim (AS) challenged the idol worship and the claim of divinity of King Namrood, who had him thrown into a fire that Allah made cool.
Pharaoh was the opponent of Hazrat Musa (AS).
What was the relation of Hazrat Ibrahim (AS) to Hazrat Yaqub (AS)?
Hazrat Ibrahim (AS) was father of Ishaq (AS), who was the father of Yaqub (AS), so Ibrahim was the grandfather of Yaqub.
Yaqub (AS) is also called Israel and his twelve sons were the tribes of Bani Israel.
About what percentage of the world's ice is found in Antarctica?
Antarctica holds about 90 percent of all the ice on Earth, and about 70 percent of the world's fresh water.
Greenland holds most of the remaining ice.
What is the first source of Islamic law (Shariah)?
The Quran is the primary source of Islamic law, followed by the Sunnah (Hadith), Ijma (consensus) and Qiyas (analogy).
Ijtehad is the effort of scholars to derive rulings from these sources.
What are the real part and the imaginary part of the complex number -3 + 4i?
In a + bi, a is the real part and b is the imaginary part. Here a = -3 and b = 4.
i is defined by i squared = -1.
What is the imaginary part of the complex number 7 - 2i?
Write 7 - 2i as 7 + (-2)i. The imaginary part is the coefficient of i, which is -2.
For which sport is Imam-ul-Haq famous?
Imam-ul-Haq is a left-handed Pakistani cricketer who plays as an opening batsman for the national team.
He is the nephew of former Pakistan captain Inzamam-ul-Haq.
In which year was the International Monetary Fund (IMF) established?
The IMF was formally established in December 1945 after the Bretton Woods conference of July 1944, and began operations in 1947.
Some sources say 1944 because the agreement was drawn up at Bretton Woods that year.
Where is the headquarters of the International Monetary Fund (IMF)?
The IMF has its headquarters in Washington DC, United States, close to the World Bank.
The UN headquarters is in New York and the WTO is in Geneva.
Which is an important river of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KPK)?
The Kabul River flows from Afghanistan through Peshawar and joins the Indus near Attock. Swat river is also a major river of the province.
The Hub River lies on the border of Sindh and Balochistan.
When was the third martial law imposed in Pakistan?
General Zia-ul-Haq imposed martial law on 5 July 1977 by removing the government of Zulfikar Ali Bhutto.
The earlier martial laws were in 1958 (Ayub Khan) and 1969 (Yahya Khan); General Musharraf took power in 1999 without declaring martial law.
Who introduced the Constitution of 1962 in Pakistan?
President Field Marshal Ayub Khan introduced the 1962 constitution, which set up a presidential system with Basic Democracies.
A 1999 conflict between Pakistan and India in the Kargil sector of Kashmir
The 1965 war in the Rann of Kutch
In 1999 fighting took place in the Kargil district of Kashmir after infiltration across the Line of Control, ending in July 1999.
The Kargil conflict took place during the premiership of Nawaz Sharif.
In a village the population was 16000 in the year 2000. If the population becomes 5 times every year, what was the population in 1998?
Each year the population is multiplied by 5. So 1999 was 16000 / 5 = 3200, and 1998 was 3200 / 5 = 640.
Going back in time means dividing by the growth factor.
On what date did India get independence?
India became independent from British rule on 15 August 1947, one day after Pakistan.
India celebrates Republic Day on 26 January because its constitution came into force in 1950.
In which years did Israel and Singapore get independence respectively?
Israel declared independence on 14 May 1948, and Singapore became independent from Malaysia on 9 August 1965.
Which law was adopted as the interim constitution of Pakistan after independence in 1947?
Pakistan adopted the Government of India Act 1935, with amendments, as its interim constitution until the 1956 constitution came into force.
The Objectives Resolution was passed in March 1949.
Who is the Prime Minister of India (as of October 2026)?
Narendra Modi has been Prime Minister of India since 2014 and began his third term in June 2024.
The Indian PM is the head of government while the President is the head of state.
What is the sum of the interior angles of a triangle?
In Euclidean geometry the three interior angles of any triangle always add up to 180 degrees.
The interior angles of a quadrilateral add up to 360 degrees.
What is the integral of sin x with respect to x?
The derivative of cos x is -sin x, so the derivative of -cos x is sin x. Hence the integral of sin x is -cos x + C.
The integral of cos x is sin x + C.
What is the integral of tan x with respect to x?
Write tan x as sin x over cos x and put u = cos x; the integral becomes -ln |cos x| + C, which equals ln |sec x| + C.
The derivative of tan x is sec squared x.
What is the antonym of interim?
Interim means temporary, so its opposite is permanent.
Provisional and temporary are synonyms of interim.
How far does Pakistan's territorial sea extend from its baseline?
Pakistan's Territorial Waters and Maritime Zones Act of 1976 fixed the territorial sea at 12 nautical miles, in line with international law.
Pakistan's Exclusive Economic Zone extends up to 200 nautical miles.
On which date in 1933 was the name Pakistan first put forward by Choudhry Rahmat Ali in the pamphlet Now or Never?
Choudhry Rahmat Ali issued the pamphlet Now or Never on 28 January 1933 and proposed the name Pakistan in it.
The Lahore Resolution came later, on 23 March 1940.
Which of the following is the multiplicative inverse form of the 2 by 2 matrix with entries a, b in the first row and c, d in the second row?
Matrix with d, -b in the first row and -c, a in the second row, multiplied by 1/(ad - bc)
Matrix with a, c and b, d, multiplied by 1/(ad - bc)
Matrix with d, b and c, a, multiplied by (ad - bc)
For a 2 by 2 matrix, swap a and d, change the signs of b and c, and divide by the determinant ad - bc.
The inverse exists only when the determinant is not zero.
The inverse of a square matrix exists only if what condition holds?
The inverse equals the adjoint divided by the determinant, so the determinant must not be zero; such a matrix is called non-singular.
A matrix with zero determinant is called singular.
What is the additive inverse of the ordered pair (-a, -b)?
The additive inverse is the pair that gives (0, 0) when added. (-a, -b) + (a, b) = (0, 0), so the answer is (a, b).
The additive identity of ordered pairs is (0, 0).
What is the capital of Iran?
Tehran is the capital and largest city of Iran.
Iran lies to the west of Pakistan.
9/2 is a ratio of two integers, so it is rational, and every rational number is also a real number.
As a decimal, 9/2 equals 4.5, which terminates.
Hazrat Ismail (AS) is known by which title?
Hazrat Ismail (AS) is called Zabihullah, the one offered for sacrifice, in the story of Hazrat Ibrahim's (AS) dream.
Which battle was fought by the Muslims after the Battle of Badr, as the second major battle of Islam?
Badr was fought in 2 AH and the Battle of Uhud followed in Shawwal 3 AH.
Uhud is a mountain near Madinah.
Which is the 7th month of the Islamic (Hijri) calendar?
