If the 2nd day of a month is Monday, what day will the 9th be?
The 9th is 7 days after the 2nd. After a full week the day repeats, so it is Monday.
Any two dates 7 days apart fall on the same weekday.
Which is the highest mountain in the world above sea level?
Mount Everest is about 8,849 m high, the highest peak above sea level.
K2 on the Pakistan-China border is the second highest.
In which year did Lord Mountbatten arrive in India as the last Viceroy?
Lord Mountbatten arrived in India in March 1947 to oversee the transfer of power. He announced the Partition plan on 3 June 1947.
He later became the first Governor General of independent India.
A train moves at 120 km/h. What distance does it cover in 120 minutes?
120 minutes is 2 hours. Distance = 120 x 2 = 240 km.
Convert minutes to hours by dividing by 60.
A train is moving at a speed of 60 km/h. How much distance does it cover in 10 minutes?
10 minutes is 1/6 hour. Distance = 60 x 1/6 = 10 km.
At 60 km/h a train covers 1 km each minute.
In which year was Islamabad officially made the capital of Pakistan, replacing Rawalpindi as interim capital?
Karachi was first capital, then Rawalpindi served as interim capital while Islamabad was built. Islamabad officially became the capital in 1967.
Sources differ on the exact year, since the decision was taken in 1959-60 and the shift happened in stages.
Who moved the Objective Resolution in the Constituent Assembly of Pakistan in 1949?
Prime Minister Liaquat Ali Khan moved the Objective Resolution, and it was passed on 12 March 1949.
It later became the preamble of the 1973 Constitution.
Which of the following is one of the Ashra Mubashra?
Hazrat Talha bin Ubaidullah (RA) is among the ten Companions given the glad tidings of Paradise. The others listed are not in the group.
The ten include Abu Bakr, Umar, Usman, Ali, Zubair, Talha, Abdur Rahman bin Auf, Saad bin Abi Waqqas, Saeed bin Zaid and Abu Ubaidah.
What is the relation between multiplication and division?
Division undoes multiplication, so they are inverse operations. For example, 6 x 4 = 24 and 24 / 4 = 6.
Addition and subtraction are also inverse operations.
Where is Baitul Muqaddas (Al-Aqsa Mosque) located?
Baitul Muqaddas is in Jerusalem, in Palestine. It was the first Qibla of the Muslims.
The Qibla was changed to the Kaaba in the 2nd year of Hijra.
What is the title of Hazrat Musa (AS)?
Hazrat Musa (AS) is called Kalimullah because Allah spoke to him directly.
Khalilullah is Ibrahim, Safiullah is Adam and Ruhullah is Isa.
Who was the mother of the Holy Prophet Muhammad (PBUH)?
The Holy Prophet's mother was Hazrat Amina bint Wahb. Halima Sadia was his wet nurse.
Hazrat Amina passed away when he was about 6 years old.
Which one is different from the following: actor, director, music, producer?
Actor, director and producer are all people who work on a film, while music is a thing, not a person.
Odd-one-out questions are solved by finding the item of a different category.
How old was the Holy Prophet (SAW) when his grandfather Abdul Muttalib died?
Abdul Muttalib took care of the Prophet (SAW) after his mother Hazrat Amina died, and passed away when the Prophet was about 8 years old.
After that the Prophet (SAW) was raised by his uncle Abu Talib.
Who was the Habshi (Abyssinian) king Najashi, who gave shelter to the early Muslim migrants?
Najashi was the title of the Abyssinian king, whose real name was Ashama bin Abjar.
When he died in 9 AH, the Prophet (SAW) offered his funeral prayer in absentia.
An optional prayer offered after sunrise
A prayer offered during an eclipse
Ishraq is an optional (nafl) prayer offered about 15 to 20 minutes after sunrise, after the Fajr prayer.
Namaz-e-Istisqa is the prayer for rain.
Which prophet was sent to Namrood?
Namrood was the tyrant king of Babylon, and Hazrat Ibrahim (AS) preached against him and his idol worship.
Namrood had Hazrat Ibrahim (AS) thrown into a fire, which Allah made cool and safe.
Where is the National Museum of Pakistan located?
The National Museum of Pakistan is in Karachi, in the Burnes Garden area.
The Lahore Museum is a separate and older museum.
How many member countries does NATO have at present?
NATO has 32 members, after Finland joined in 2023 and Sweden in 2024.
NATO was founded in 1949 with 12 members.
A helicopter needs 50 gallons of fuel to cover 320 km. How many gallons are needed to cover 400 km?
Fuel per km is 50 divided by 320 = 0.15625 gallons, so 400 km needs 400 x 0.15625 = 62.5 gallons.
Equivalently, 400 is 1.25 times 320, so the fuel is 1.25 x 50 = 62.5.
Is sin x positive or negative in the first quadrant?
In the first quadrant the y-coordinate is positive and sin x equals y divided by r, so it is positive.
In the first quadrant all six trigonometric ratios are positive.
The line x = 3 is ______ to the X axis.
The line x = 3 is a vertical line, and a vertical line meets the horizontal X axis at a right angle.
The line x = 3 is parallel to the Y axis.
Fill in the blank: Mrs. Rehan is not pleased ___ the new servant.
The adjective pleased is followed by the preposition with when it refers to a person. So the correct sentence is: not pleased with the new servant.
Other common adjective and preposition pairs are angry with, good at and afraid of.
What is a bill called after it has been passed by Parliament and approved by the President of Pakistan?
A bill passed by both houses and assented to by the President becomes an Act of Parliament, which is law. An ordinance is a temporary law issued by the President when Parliament is not in session.
Under Article 75 of the Constitution the President has ten days to assent to a bill or return it.
What comes next in the series: 3A, 5C, 7E, ?
The numbers increase by 2 (3, 5, 7, 9) and the letters skip one letter each time (A, C, E, G). So the next term is 9G.
The letters A, C, E, G are the 1st, 3rd, 5th and 7th letters of the alphabet.
What comes next in the series: 3x+4, 4x+2, ?
The coefficient of x increases by 1 each time (3, 4, 5) and the constant decreases by 2 (4, 2, 0). So the next term is 5x+0 = 5x.
Such a pattern is two arithmetic progressions running together.
What comes next in the series: B2, C3, D4, E5, F?
Each letter moves one step forward and each number increases by 1. F pairs with 6, so the next term is F6.
B is the 2nd letter, C the 3rd, and so on, so each letter pairs with its own position number.
What comes next in the series: 3W, 6X, 9Z, ?
The numbers increase by 3 (3, 6, 9, 12). The letters move forward by 1, then 2, then 3: W to X to Z to C (after Z the alphabet starts again). So the next term is 12C.
In such letter series, the alphabet is treated as a circle, so Z is followed by A.
These are the squares 1x1, 2x2, 3x3, 4x4. The next is 5x5 = 25.
The gaps between squares are the odd numbers 3, 5, 7, 9.
The terms in odd positions go 155, 165 and the terms in even positions go 65, 75, each rising by 10. So the next term is 165 + 10 = 175.
This is an alternating series made of two separate series.
Each number is 2 more than the one before it. So 8 + 2 = 10.
These are the first even natural numbers.
Each number is 3 more than the one before. So 12 + 3 = 15.
Each number is 3 more than the one before. So 9 + 3 = 12.
Each number is 5 more than the one before. So 15 + 5 = 20.
The differences are 3, 6, 12, 24, each double the last. The next difference is 48, so 21 - 48 = -27.
The same series appears as 66, 63, 57, 45, 21 where the next term after 45 is 21.
Sardar Abdur Rab Nishtar served as the Governor of which province of Pakistan?
Sardar Abdur Rab Nishtar, a leader of the Pakistan Movement, was Governor of Punjab from 1949 to 1951.
Nishtar Medical University in Multan is named after him.
In which Hijri year was Zakat made obligatory?
According to the commonly taught view, Zakat became obligatory in the second year of Hijri, around the time Ramadan fasting was ordained. Some scholars give slightly different years.
Sources differ a little on the exact year of Zakat.
How many soldiers did the Quraysh army have at the Battle of Uhud?
The Makkan army led by Abu Sufyan had about 3000 soldiers against around 700 Muslims at the start of the battle (about 1000 left with Abdullah bin Ubayy).
The Quraysh army had 200 horsemen and Khalid bin Walid led their cavalry.
School is a noun. Which pronoun can be used in its place?
A school is a singular, non-living thing, so the pronoun it is used for it.
The plural pronoun for schools is they.
What is the word used in place of a noun called?
A pronoun is used in place of a noun to avoid repeating it, such as he, she, it and they.
Words like he, she and it are personal pronouns.
What is the total number of nuclear-armed countries in the world today?
Nine countries have nuclear weapons: the USA, Russia, the UK, France, China, India, Pakistan, Israel (undeclared) and North Korea.
Pakistan is the only Muslim country with nuclear weapons.
On which date did Pakistan become a nuclear power by conducting nuclear tests?
Pakistan carried out its tests in the Chagai Hills on 28 May 1998, responding to India's tests of 11 and 13 May 1998.
According to the commonly accepted belief, how many Prophets (Anbiya) were sent by Allah?
A well-known narration gives the number of Prophets as 124,000. The exact number is known only to Allah.
The Quran names 25 Prophets. Sources differ about the number of Rasools, commonly given as 313.
13, 15, 17 and 19 are what type of numbers?
Each of these numbers leaves a remainder of 1 when divided by 2, so they are odd numbers.
The only even prime number is 2.
If a set has two elements, how many elements are in its power set?
The power set of a set with n elements has 2 to the power n elements. For n = 2 this is 4: the empty set, two single-element subsets, and the set itself.
A set with 3 elements has a power set of 8 elements.
Which languages were declared official languages of Pakistan by the 1962 constitution?
The 1962 constitution recognised Urdu and Bengali as the national languages of Pakistan.
The 1956 constitution had also named Urdu and Bengali as state languages.
Which is generally regarded as the oldest city of Pakistan according to Pakistani textbooks?
Peshawar is commonly described as the oldest living city of Pakistan, inhabited for over 2,500 years.
Sources differ, as Multan is also claimed to be among the oldest cities in South Asia.
For whom are the Special Olympics held?
The Special Olympics are sports competitions for people with intellectual disabilities.
The Paralympic Games are held for athletes with physical disabilities.
In which country were the first Olympic Games, ancient and modern, held?
The ancient Games were held at Olympia in Greece and the first modern Games took place at Athens, Greece, in 1896.
The Olympic Games were revived by Baron Pierre de Coubertin.
What is the capital of Oman?
Muscat is the capital and largest city of Oman.
Oman is ruled by a Sultan and is located on the south-eastern coast of the Arabian Peninsula.
What is a matrix with only one row called?
A matrix having only one row is called a row matrix; its order is 1 x n.
A matrix with only one column is called a column matrix.
Change into passive voice: Open the door.
An imperative sentence is changed into the passive using Let + object + be + past participle, giving Let the door be opened.
Imperative sentences express commands, requests or advice.
What does Allama Iqbal Open University mainly promote?
Allama Iqbal Open University in Islamabad provides distance and open education to students who cannot attend regular institutions.
It was established in 1974 as the People's Open University and renamed in 1977.
Fill in the blank: She opened the door ____.
A word describing how an action is done must be an adverb, so slowly is correct.
Most adverbs of manner are formed by adding ly to an adjective.
In which year was the Mangla Dam completed and opened?
Mangla Dam on the Jhelum River was completed in 1967 under the Indus Waters Treaty works.
The dam was raised in 2009 to increase its storage capacity.
What is the opposite of contiguous?
Contiguous means sharing a border or touching, so its opposite is separated or detached.
Contiguous comes from the Latin contingere, meaning to touch.
What is the border between Indian Punjab and Pakistani Punjab called?
The boundary between India and Pakistan in Punjab was drawn by the Radcliffe Commission in 1947 and is called the Radcliffe Line.
The Wagah border crossing near Lahore lies on this line.
Subtraction is carried out from left to right.
What is the order of a square matrix having n rows?
A square matrix has equal rows and columns, so its order is n x n.
A 3 x 3 matrix is a square matrix of order 3.
What are the coordinates of the origin on a Cartesian graph?
The origin is the point where the x-axis and y-axis cross, so both its x and y values are zero.
The two axes divide the plane into four quadrants that meet at the origin.
Who built the Quba Mosque, the first mosque in Islam?
The Prophet (PBUH) laid the foundation of the Quba Mosque near Madinah on his Hijrah, and the Companions helped build it.
The Quran (Surah At-Tawbah) refers to a mosque founded on piety from the first day, which scholars identify as Quba.
What is another name of the Battle of Ahzab?
The Battle of Ahzab (the Confederates) in 5 AH is also called the Battle of Khandaq because the Muslims dug a trench around Madinah on the advice of Hazrat Salman Farsi (RA).
The Quraysh and their allied tribes besieged Madinah for about a month and then withdrew.
In which period was the first war between Pakistan and India over Kashmir fought?
The first Indo-Pak war over Kashmir began in October 1947 after tribal and Pakistani forces entered the state and India sent troops. It ended with a UN-brokered ceasefire on 1 January 1949.
The ceasefire line later became the Line of Control after the Simla Agreement of 1972.
The Dawn newspaper is owned by which family-run group?
Dawn is published by Dawn Media Group, which is controlled by the Haroon family (with the Saigol family). The Haroon family bought majority shares in 1946.
Dawn was founded by Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah in Delhi in 1941.
Who signed the Simla Agreement of 1972 on behalf of India?
The Indian Prime Minister at that time, Indira Gandhi, signed the Simla Agreement on 2 July 1972.
Zulfikar Ali Bhutto signed for Pakistan.
What was the Gandhi-Irwin Pact of 1931?
An agreement that ended the Civil Disobedience Movement and let Gandhi attend the Second Round Table Conference
A pact between Congress and the Muslim League
The Gandhi-Irwin Pact was signed on 5 March 1931 between Mahatma Gandhi and the Viceroy Lord Irwin. Congress suspended civil disobedience and the government released political prisoners.
Gandhi then attended the Second Round Table Conference in London in 1931.
By what name is the boundary line between Pakistan and India known?
The international border between Pakistan and India was drawn in 1947 by the Radcliffe Boundary Commission, headed by Sir Cyril Radcliffe.
The Durand Line is the Pakistan-Afghanistan border.
Which area of Pakistan is called the Switzerland of Pakistan?
Swat valley is known as the Switzerland of Pakistan for its mountains, rivers and green scenery.
Faisalabad, by contrast, is known as the Manchester of Pakistan.
Under the 1973 Constitution of Pakistan, which institution is supreme?
The 1973 Constitution set up a parliamentary system in which the Parliament is the supreme law-making body and the Prime Minister heads the government.
In practice the Constitution itself is supreme, and Parliament must act within it.
What is the parliament of Israel called?
The Israeli parliament is called the Knesset and it has 120 members.
Lord Curzon was the Viceroy of India from 1899 to 1905 and he carried out the partition of Bengal.
The Muslim League was founded in 1906, soon after the partition.
On what date was the Indian Independence Act passed by the British Parliament?
The Indian Independence Act received royal assent on 18 July 1947 and created the two dominions of Pakistan and India.
The 3 June 1947 plan was announced by Lord Mountbatten before the Act.
In a bus of 30 passengers, 2/3 are men and the rest are girls. What is the percentage of girls?
Men = 2/3 x 30 = 20, so girls = 30 - 20 = 10. Percentage of girls = 10/30 x 100 = 33.33%.
Who has the power to promulgate an ordinance in Pakistan?
Under Article 89 of the Constitution, the President may promulgate an ordinance when the National Assembly is not in session (or the Senate, if only it is sitting) and immediate action is needed.
An ordinance lapses after 120 days unless extended once by a resolution of the Assembly.
What is the Kunyat (kuniyyat) of the Holy Prophet Muhammad (PBUH)?
The Prophet (PBUH) was called Abu al-Qasim after his eldest son Qasim.
Abu Turab was the kunyat of Hazrat Ali (RA), and Abu Hafs of Hazrat Umar (RA).
What is the perimeter of a circle called?
The distance around a circle is called its circumference, equal to 2 x pi x radius.
The diameter is twice the radius.
What is the period of the function sin x?
The sine function repeats its values after every 2 pi radians (360 degrees), so sin(x + 2 pi) = sin x.
The period of tan x is pi.
A. R. Cornelius, a famous Chief Justice of Pakistan, belonged to which religion?
Justice Alvin Robert Cornelius was a Christian and served as Chief Justice of Pakistan from 1960 to 1968.
He was the fourth Chief Justice of Pakistan.
Aleem Dar is a famous personality in which field?
Aleem Dar is a Pakistani international cricket umpire, who won the ICC Umpire of the Year award three times.
He officiated in more than 130 Test matches.
If 5 persons write 5 papers in 5 days, how many papers will 1 person write in 5 days?
Each person writes 1 paper in 5 days (5 persons write 5 papers in 5 days). So 1 person writes 1 paper in 5 days.
In 25 days, 1 person would write 5 papers.
Which pass connects Peshawar with Afghanistan?
The Khyber Pass, with the Torkham crossing, connects Peshawar with Afghanistan.
The Bolan Pass connects Quetta with Afghanistan and the Khunjerab Pass links Pakistan with China.
Which pillar of Islam is related to the event of Meraj?
Five daily prayers were made obligatory during the Meraj (Night Journey).
Originally 50 prayers were prescribed and were reduced to five.
On which date did the Pakistan Air Force capture the Indian pilot Wing Commander Abhinandan?
Abhinandan's MiG-21 was shot down on 27 February 2019 and he was taken into custody.
He was handed over to India on 1 March 2019 at Wagah.
Badr, where the first major battle of Islam was fought, is the name of what?
A plain with wells near Madinah
Badr is a plain valley with wells about 150 km from Madinah where the Battle of Badr took place in 2 AH.
Mount Uhud, in contrast, is a mountain near Madinah.
Which is the brightest planet in the sky?
Venus is the brightest planet as seen from Earth because it is close and its thick clouds reflect much sunlight.
It is often called the morning or evening star.
Inzamam-ul-Haq is a famous player of which game?
Inzamam-ul-Haq is a former Pakistan cricket captain and batter.
He was a member of the 1992 World Cup winning Pakistan team.
What is the land of the pure people (Sarzamin-e-Pak) a name for?
The name Pakistan means land of the pure, from Urdu pak (pure) and stan (land).
The name was coined by Chaudhry Rahmat Ali in 1933.
Which Pakistani women cricketer was the first to take 100 wickets in women's ODIs?
Sana Mir, former captain of Pakistan women's team, was the first Pakistani woman to reach 100 ODI wickets.
Sana Mir finished her career with over 150 ODI wickets.
Khushal Khan Khattak is a famous poet of which language?
Khushal Khan Khattak (1613-1689) was a warrior-poet who wrote in Pashto.
He is regarded as the national poet of the Pashtuns.
Baba Fariduddin Ganj Shakar is regarded as the first major poet of which language?
Baba Farid (1173-1266) of Pakpattan is considered the first major poet of the Punjabi language.
Some of his verses are included in the Guru Granth Sahib.
Which of the following points lies on the line y = 6x?
For (2, 12): 6 times 2 = 12, so it satisfies y = 6x. The others do not.
The line y = 6x has slope 6 and passes through the origin.
In which year was the film Jinnah, based on the life of Quaid-e-Azam, released?
The film Jinnah, directed by Jamil Dehlavi and starring Christopher Lee, was released in 1998.
Christopher Lee played the role of Muhammad Ali Jinnah in the film.
What is the population of Punjab province according to the 2023 census?
The 2023 census counted about 127.7 million people in Punjab, the most populous province.
Punjab holds roughly half of Pakistan's population.
Which of the following is a major port of Sri Lanka?
Colombo is the largest and busiest port of Sri Lanka.
Hambantota is another important port of Sri Lanka.
When did Pakistan issue its first postage stamps?
Pakistan's first set of postage stamps was issued on 9 July 1948.
Before that, British Indian stamps overprinted with the word Pakistan were used in 1947.
What is the value of x to the power 0 (for x not equal to 0)?
Any non-zero number raised to the power 0 equals 1, because x to the power n divided by x to the power n equals x to the power 0, which equals 1.
The expression 0 to the power 0 is treated as undefined or indeterminate in many contexts.
Which countries hold veto power in the UN Security Council?
The five permanent members of the Security Council (P5) have veto power: USA, UK, France, Russia and China.
A single veto from any permanent member blocks a substantive resolution.
Which regional organization was the predecessor of the Economic Cooperation Organization (ECO)?
RCD, formed in 1964 by Pakistan, Iran and Turkey, was revived and expanded as ECO in 1985.
Pakistan, Iran and Turkey were the founding members of both RCD and ECO.
How many compiled copies of the Quran were prepared in the time of Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA)?
Under Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA) the Quran was collected into one single compiled copy, kept with him and then with Hazrat Umar and Hazrat Hafsa (RA).
Copies were multiplied and sent to different regions later, during the time of Hazrat Uthman (RA).
Which is the present constitution of Pakistan?
Pakistan is currently governed by the Constitution of 1973, which came into force on 14 August 1973.
It has been amended many times, including the 18th Amendment in 2010.
Who acts as President of Pakistan when the President is absent or unable to work?
Under Article 49 of the Constitution, the Chairman of the Senate acts as President, and if he is unavailable, the Speaker of the National Assembly does.
The Chairman of the Senate is elected by the members of the Senate.
If the price of 3 eggs is 4 rupees, what is the price of 18 eggs?
18 eggs is 6 times 3 eggs, so the price is 6 times 4 = 24 rupees.
This is a direct proportion problem solved by the unitary method.
In which year was the Al-Khalid main battle tank put into production in Pakistan?
The Al-Khalid (MBT-2000) was developed with China and Ukraine, and serial production at Heavy Industries Taxila began in 2001.
The Al-Khalid is also known as MBT-2000 and was developed jointly with China's Norinco.
Which fighter jet is produced by Pakistan (jointly with China)?
The JF-17 Thunder is a light multirole fighter made at Pakistan Aeronautical Complex, Kamra, with China's Chengdu Aircraft Corporation.
The JF-17 is also called the FC-1 Xiaolong in China.
Which country is the largest producer of tobacco in the world?
China grows the most tobacco leaf in the world, followed by countries such as India and Brazil.
China is also the largest consumer of cigarettes.
Which country produces the most olives in the world?
Spain is the largest producer of olives and olive oil, mainly from the region of Andalusia.
Spain produces roughly half of the world's olive oil in a good year.
What is the value of i x i, where i is the imaginary unit?
The imaginary unit is defined by i squared equals -1, so i x i = -1.
Higher powers repeat in a cycle: i cubed is -i and i to the fourth power is 1.
What is the antonym of the word prohibit?
To prohibit means to forbid something, so its opposite is to permit or allow it.
Prohibit comes from the Latin prohibere, meaning to hold back.
Which word is a synonym of prohibit?
Prohibit means to officially stop something from being done, which is the same as forbid.
Ban and bar are other synonyms of prohibit.
Which country started the Saindak copper-gold project in Balochistan?
The Saindak project in Chagai district was developed with a Chinese company, the Metallurgical Corporation of China (MCC), which has operated it under lease.
Saindak is Pakistan's first major copper and gold mining project.
Which type of government is provided by the 1973 Constitution of Pakistan?
The 1973 Constitution set up a parliamentary system in which the Prime Minister heads the government and the President is head of state.
The 18th Amendment (2010) restored the full parliamentary character of the Constitution.
Kharan is a district of which province of Pakistan?
Kharan is a district and town in the west of Balochistan province.
The Kharan Desert, where Pakistan tested nuclear devices in 1998 near Chagai, lies in this region of Balochistan.
Which is the largest province of Pakistan by area?
Balochistan covers about 347,000 square kilometres, around 44 percent of Pakistan.
Punjab is the largest province by population.
How many seats does the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Provincial Assembly have?
After the 25th Amendment merged FATA into KP in 2018, the assembly grew from 124 to 145 seats (115 general, 26 women, 4 non-Muslim).
Before the merger the assembly had 124 seats.
Under the 1973 Constitution, what is the term of the National Assembly and the provincial assemblies?
The National Assembly and the provincial assemblies are each elected for five years unless dissolved earlier.
The Senate, by contrast, is a permanent house with members serving six-year terms.
Which word is a synonym of provoke?
To provoke means to stir up a strong reaction, which is the same as to incite.
Instigate and arouse are other synonyms of provoke.
Which were the official languages of Pakistan under the 1956 Constitution?
The 1956 Constitution made Urdu and Bengali the state languages of Pakistan.
The 1956 Constitution also allowed English for official purposes for a transition period.
What was the age of Dr Abdul Qadeer Khan at the time of Pakistan's first nuclear tests in May 1998?
Born on 1 April 1936, he was 62 years old on 28 May 1998.
The tests were carried out at Chagai in Balochistan.
From whom did Muhammad bin Qasim conquer Sindh?
Muhammad bin Qasim defeated Raja Dahir, the Hindu ruler of Sindh, in 711-712 AD.
Raja Dahir was defeated near Raor.
Muhammad bin Qasim conquered Sindh during the rule of which caliphate?
He was sent by Hajjaj bin Yusuf, governor of Iraq, during the Umayyad Caliphate of Walid bin Abdul Malik.
The Abbasid Caliphate began later, in 750 AD.
Which prophet was sent to the people of Aad (Qaum-e-Hood)?
Hazrat Hud (AS) was sent to the people of Aad, who lived in Ahqaf in southern Arabia.
Surah Hud of the Quran is named after him.
Derawar Fort is a large fort in the Cholistan Desert near Ahmedpur East in Bahawalpur district, Punjab.
The fort was built by Rajput Bhatti rulers and is now on Pakistan's tentative UNESCO list.
What is a quantity that can change or take different values called?
A quantity whose value can change is called a variable, such as x in the equation x + 2 = 5. A quantity whose value never changes is a constant.
In algebra, letters such as x, y and z are commonly used to represent variables.
Where was Masjid Quba, the first mosque in Islam, built?
Masjid Quba was built in the village of Quba on the outskirts of Madinah. The Holy Prophet (PBUH) laid its foundation when he arrived there during the Hijrat.
Masjid Quba is regarded as the first mosque built in Islam.
The Khojak Pass connects Quetta with which Afghan city?
The Khojak Pass in Balochistan lies on the route from Quetta to Chaman and on to Kandahar in Afghanistan. The Khojak Tunnel runs beneath it.
The Bolan Pass links Quetta with Sibi and the plains of Sindh and Punjab.
For how many years did the Quraish of Makkah socially and economically boycott the Holy Prophet (PBUH) and Banu Hashim?
The Quraish boycotted Banu Hashim and Banu Muttalib for about three years, and the family stayed in Shib Abi Talib. The boycott ended in the tenth year of prophethood.
Hazrat Abu Talib and Hazrat Khadija (RA) both died soon after the boycott ended.
Who is said to have been the first to memorise the whole Quran (hifz)?
The Quran was revealed to the Holy Prophet (PBUH), who memorised it as it came and recited it to Hazrat Jibril (AS). He is therefore regarded as the first hafiz.
Among the companions, sources name several early huffaz, so this answer refers to the first hafiz overall.
What is a circle with zero radius called?
If the radius is zero, all points of the circle coincide with the centre, so it is a single point called a point circle.
A circle with radius 1 is called a unit circle.
From whom did Raja Gulab Singh buy Kashmir in 1846?
After the First Anglo-Sikh War, the British East India Company sold Kashmir to Gulab Singh of Jammu for 75 lakh rupees. This was done through the Treaty of Amritsar.
Gulab Singh founded the Dogra dynasty that ruled Jammu and Kashmir until 1947.
Through which treaty did Raja Gulab Singh purchase Kashmir?
Gulab Singh bought Kashmir from the British under the Treaty of Amritsar, signed on 16 March 1846. The price was 75 lakh rupees.
The Treaty of Lahore was signed a few days earlier, in March 1846, between the British and the Sikhs.
Which mountain range connects Pakistan with China through the Karakoram Highway?
The Karakoram Highway crosses the Karakoram range and reaches China through the Khunjerab Pass. So the Karakoram range links Pakistan with China.
The Khunjerab Pass, at about 4693 metres, is among the highest paved border crossings in the world.
If my age is 10 years and my brother's age is 2 times my age, what will be the ratio of my age to my brother's age after 10 years?
My brother is 2 x 10 = 20 years old now. After 10 years I will be 20 and he will be 30, so the ratio is 20 : 30 = 2 : 3.
The ratio of ages moves closer to 1 : 1 as both people grow older.
Regional Cooperation for Development (RCD) was an organisation of which three countries?
RCD was formed in 1964 by Pakistan, Iran and Turkey to promote economic, technical and cultural cooperation.
RCD was later renamed ECO, which expanded in 1992 to include Central Asian states and Afghanistan.
Change into active voice: The book is being read by her.
The passive form is being read becomes the active is reading, and the agent her becomes the subject she. The tense stays present continuous.
In active voice the doer of the action is the subject of the sentence.
Change into passive voice: We are reading a book.
A book was being read by us.
A book is read by us.
A book is being read by us.
A book has been read by us.
Present continuous passive uses is or are being plus the past participle. The object a book becomes the subject and we becomes by us.
Passive voice puts the focus on the action or receiver rather than the doer.
What is the value of the real number -(4! + 6)?
What is the real part of the complex number 7 - 2i?
In a + bi form with a = 7 and b = -2, the real part is 7.
Real numbers are complex numbers whose imaginary part is zero.
Rearrange the letters V I S R E L to make a word. What is the second last letter of that word?
The letters form the word SILVER. Its letters are S, I, L, V, E, R so the second last letter is E.
Silver has the chemical symbol Ag from the Latin argentum.
How many Pakistani Nobel Prize winners have won in the field of physics?
Only Dr Abdus Salam won the Nobel Prize in Physics, in 1979 for the electroweak theory. Malala Yousafzai won the Peace Prize in 2014.
Abdus Salam shared the 1979 physics prize with Sheldon Glashow and Steven Weinberg.
Who is the President of India (as of 2026)?
Droupadi Murmu became the 15th President of India on 25 July 2022 and still holds the office. Narendra Modi is the Prime Minister.
Her predecessor was Ram Nath Kovind, who served from 2017 to 2022.
Which of the following is one of the eight categories of zakat recipients (masarif) mentioned in Surah At-Tawbah?
Surah At-Tawbah (verse 60) lists the fakir, miskin, zakat collectors, those whose hearts are to be reconciled, slaves, debtors, fi sabilillah and travellers. Debtors (Al-Gharimin) are one of them.
Zakat cannot be given to the Prophet's family (Bani Hashim) according to the majority view.
What is dead reckoning in navigation?
Sailing only at night using the stars
Estimating current position from a known starting point, speed, time and direction
Measuring the depth of the sea
Dead reckoning calculates the present position by using a previously known position and adding the distance travelled on a known course. It does not need external signals.
Before GPS, ships and aircraft relied heavily on dead reckoning.
In which year did China recognize Pakistan?
The People's Republic of China was proclaimed in 1949 and Pakistan recognized it in 1950, among the first countries to do so. Diplomatic relations began on 21 May 1951.
Pakistan was among the first Muslim countries to recognize the People's Republic of China.
Where is the Red Sea located?
The Red Sea lies between northeast Africa (Egypt, Sudan, Eritrea) and the Arabian Peninsula (Saudi Arabia, Yemen). It connects to the Mediterranean through the Suez Canal.
The Red Sea joins the Indian Ocean through the Bab-el-Mandeb strait.
Who said that the character of the Holy Prophet (PBUH) was the Quran?
When asked about the Prophet's character, Hazrat Ayesha (RA) replied that his character was the Quran. This shows he lived by its teachings.
Hazrat Ayesha (RA) is also known as Umm-ul-Momineen and narrated over 2000 hadith.
In which region of the world is Pakistan located?
Pakistan lies in South Asia, bordered by Iran, Afghanistan, China and India. The Arabian Sea is to the south.
Pakistan is a member of SAARC, the regional body of South Asia.
In the reign of which caliph was the Battle of Yamama fought?
The Battle of Yamama was fought in 632 CE against the false prophet Musaylima in the caliphate of Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA). Many Huffaz of the Quran were martyred.
This loss led to the first compilation of the Quran in one book.
In which province of Pakistan is the Reko Diq mine located?
Reko Diq is in Chagai district of Balochistan. It holds one of the world's largest copper and gold deposits.
Saindak, also in Chagai, is another copper and gold project.
What was the relation of Hazrat Ali (RA) to the Holy Prophet (PBUH)?
Hazrat Ali (RA) was the son of Abu Talib, the Prophet's uncle, so he was a cousin. He married the Prophet's daughter Hazrat Fatima (RA).
Hazrat Ali (RA) was the fourth Rightly Guided Caliph.
According to the Quran, which religion is accepted by Allah?
The Quran states that the religion with Allah is Islam (Surah Al-Imran 3:19). It also says no other religion will be accepted from anyone.
The Quran was completed with the verse declaring Islam as the chosen religion (Surah Al-Maidah 5:3).
What is the antonym of reluctant?
Reluctant means unwilling, so its opposite is willing or eager. The other options are synonyms.
Eager and keen are also antonyms of reluctant.
For how many days did the Holy Prophet (PBUH) stay in the Cave of Thawr (Ghar-e-Saur) during the Hijrat?
During the migration to Madinah the Prophet (PBUH) and Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA) hid in the Cave of Thawr for three days. They then continued to Madinah.
The cave is near Makkah, south of the city.
According to the 1962 Constitution of Pakistan, what was the minimum age to be a member of the National Assembly?
The 1962 Constitution required a member of the National Assembly to be at least 25 years old.
Sources differ slightly on some qualification details; the minimum age of the President under the 1962 Constitution is commonly given as 35 years.
According to the 1973 Constitution, what is the minimum age required to be elected President of Pakistan?
Article 41 of the 1973 Constitution requires the President to be a Muslim, qualified to be a member of the National Assembly, and not less than 45 years old.
The President is elected by an electoral college of the Senate, National Assembly and provincial assemblies for a five-year term.
How many seats were reserved for women in the National Assembly under the 1956 Constitution of Pakistan?
The 1956 Constitution provided a National Assembly of 300 general seats plus 10 seats reserved for women for ten years.
Under the 1973 Constitution today, 60 National Assembly seats are reserved for women.
How many seats are reserved for women in the Punjab Assembly?
The Punjab Assembly has 371 seats: 297 general seats, 66 seats for women and 8 for non-Muslims.
Punjab has the largest provincial assembly in Pakistan.
In which city did the Quraish tribe reside?
The Quraish were the ruling tribe of Makkah and guardians of the Kaaba.
The Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) belonged to the Banu Hashim clan of the Quraish.
At which place in Lahore was the Lahore Resolution presented in 1940?
The session of the All India Muslim League was held at Minto Park, now Iqbal Park, where Minar-e-Pakistan stands.
Minar-e-Pakistan was built to commemorate the resolution.
On which date was the China-Pakistan boundary agreement signed?
Pakistan and China signed the boundary agreement on 2 March 1963, settling the border of the Northern Areas with Xinjiang.
Pakistan and China established diplomatic relations on 21 May 1951.
Which gas is mainly responsible for global warming?
Carbon dioxide, released by burning fossil fuels, traps heat in the atmosphere as a greenhouse gas.
Methane is another important greenhouse gas.
What is SUPARCO responsible for in Pakistan?
SUPARCO is the Space and Upper Atmosphere Research Commission, Pakistan's national space agency.
SUPARCO was established in 1961 and launched Badr-1, Pakistan's first satellite, in 1990.
What is the meaning of retaliation?
Retaliation means paying back an injury or wrong with a similar action, that is, revenge.
What is the antonym of retaliation?
Retaliation means revenge, so its opposite is forgiveness or pardon.
Revenge, vengeance and reprisal are synonyms of retaliation.
In how many years was the Holy Quran revealed?
The Quran was revealed gradually over about 23 years: about 13 years in Makkah and about 10 years in Madina.
Revelation began in 610 CE in the cave of Hira.
Which Surah is generally regarded as the last complete Surah to be revealed?
Surah An-Nasr is generally regarded as the last complete Surah revealed to the Prophet (PBUH).
Sources differ; some name Surah At-Tawbah as the last Surah revealed.
If the letters of the word BEAUTY are written in reverse order, which is the last letter?
BEAUTY reversed is YTUAEB, so the last letter is B.
The first letter of the reversed word is Y.
According to the Hadith Qudsi on fasting, who will Himself give the reward of fasting?
In the Hadith Qudsi Allah says: Fasting is for Me and I shall reward it Myself.
Fasting is the third pillar of Islam in some counts and the fourth in the commonly taught Pakistani order.
In which direction does the sun rise?
The Earth rotates from west to east, so the sun appears to rise in the east.
The sun sets in the west.
In which war did the general Robert E. Lee fight?
Robert E. Lee commanded the Confederate army of Northern Virginia in the American Civil War of 1861 to 1865.
He surrendered to Ulysses S. Grant at Appomattox in 1865.
There are 30 males and females in a room and 2/3 of them are males. What is the percentage of females?
Males are 2/3 of 30 = 20, so females are 30 - 20 = 10. Percentage of females = 10/30 x 100 = 33.33%.
Fractions can be converted to percentages by multiplying by 100, so 1/3 is 33.33%.
In the absence of the President of Pakistan, who acts as the President?

Under Article 49 of the Constitution, the Chairman of the Senate acts as President when the office is vacant or the President is absent. If he is also unavailable, the Speaker of the National Assembly acts.
The acting President can serve until a new President is elected or the President returns.
What is the running between Safa and Marwa during Hajj and Umrah called?
The walking or running seven times between the hills of Safa and Marwa is called Sa'i. It commemorates Hazrat Hajra's search for water for Ismail (AS).
Tawaf is the circling of the Kaaba.
Which is the fastest running animal in the world?
The cheetah can run at about 100 to 120 km per hour in short bursts, which is the fastest of all land animals.
The peregrine falcon is the fastest animal overall when diving.
Who has scored the most runs in Test cricket?
Sachin Tendulkar of India scored 15,921 runs in 200 Tests, and no one has passed this total as of October 2026.
Joe Root of England is second, having passed 14,000 Test runs in 2026.
What is the capital of Russia?
Moscow is the capital and largest city of Russia.
Saint Petersburg was the capital of the Russian Empire until 1918.
Saleem is 3 years old and his sister is three times as old as him. How old will his sister be when Saleem is 12?
The sister is 3 x 3 = 9 years old now, so she is 6 years older than Saleem. When he is 12, she will be 12 + 6 = 18.
The age difference between two people always stays the same.
Sana was three times as old as her brother when he was 5 years old. How old is Sana when her brother is 12?
Sana was 3 x 5 = 15, so she is 10 years older than her brother. When he is 12, she is 12 + 10 = 22.
The age gap between siblings never changes.
What is the synonym of foe?
Foe means an enemy or opponent.
The antonym of foe is friend or ally.
Ali is 3 years old and his sister Sara is 3 times his age. How old will Sara be when Ali is 8 years old?
When Ali is 3, Sara is 3 x 3 = 9, so Sara is 6 years older than Ali. The age gap stays the same, so when Ali is 8, Sara is 8 + 6 = 14.
The difference between two people's ages never changes with time.
Ali is 3 years old and his sister Sara is 3 times his age. How old will Sara be when Ali is 15 years old?
When Ali is 3, Sara is 9, so she is 6 years older. When Ali is 15, Sara is 15 + 6 = 21.
The age gap of 6 years stays fixed for life.
How many seats does the Provincial Assembly of Sindh have in total?
The Sindh Assembly has 168 seats: 130 general seats, 29 reserved for women and 9 reserved for non-Muslims.
The Punjab Assembly is the largest provincial assembly with 371 seats.
How many general seats does Khyber Pakhtunkhwa have in the National Assembly of Pakistan after the 2023 delimitation?
After the merger of FATA and the 2023 delimitation, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa has 45 general seats in the National Assembly.
Before the merger of FATA the province had 35 general seats, while Punjab now has 141 general seats.
In which city is the secretariat of the Economic Cooperation Organization (ECO) located?
The ECO Secretariat is located in Tehran, Iran.
ECO was founded in 1985 by Pakistan, Iran and Turkey, and it grew to ten members in 1992 and after.
What is the antonym (opposite) of the word selfless?
Selfless means putting others before oneself, so its opposite is selfish, meaning concerned only with oneself.
Unselfish and altruistic are synonyms of selfless.
Which prophet was sent by Allah to Pharaoh (Firaun)?
Hazrat Musa (AS), along with his brother Hazrat Harun (AS), was sent to Firaun, the ruler of Egypt.
Hazrat Musa (AS) led the Bani Israel out of Egypt, crossing the sea.
Which prophet was sent to the tyrant king Namrud (Nimrod)?
Hazrat Ibrahim (AS) challenged Namrud, who claimed divinity, and was thrown into a fire that Allah made cool and safe.
Hazrat Ibrahim (AS) is known as Khalilullah, the friend of Allah.
Under which Act was Sindh separated from the Bombay Presidency in 1936?
The Government of India Act 1935 created Sindh as a separate province, which came into effect on 1 April 1936.
The demand for separating Sindh from Bombay was part of the Quaid-e-Azam's Fourteen Points of 1929.
How many vowels are there in this sequence: A Q W S T R H J C B D Y K L O?
The only vowels in the sequence are A and O, so the count is 2. Y is treated as a consonant here.
The English vowels are A, E, I, O and U.
How many vowels are there in the sequence: a d i u l k m e?
The vowels in the sequence are a, i, u and e, which makes 4.
The English alphabet has five vowels and twenty-one consonants.
The numbers go up by 1 each time and the letters go backwards through the alphabet (z, y, x, w). So the next term is 4w.
Z is the 26th letter and W is the 23rd letter of the alphabet.
Complete the series: a, c, f, ?
The gaps increase by 1: a to c is +2, c to f is +3, so the next is +4. F is the 6th letter and 6 + 4 = 10, which is j.
J is the 10th letter of the English alphabet.
What is the next term in the series: A1, C3, D4, G7, ?
The number is the position of the letter in the alphabet, and the numbers 1, 3, 4, 7 each equal the sum of the two before (3 + 4 = 7). The next number is 4 + 7 = 11, which is K.
The numbers 1, 3, 4, 7, 11 are known as the Lucas numbers.
The Khalid main battle tank of Pakistan entered service in which year?
The Al-Khalid (MBT-2000), developed by Pakistan with Chinese help, entered service with the Pakistan Army around 2001.
The Al-Khalid tank is named after the great Muslim general Hazrat Khalid bin Waleed (RA).
Fill in the blank: ____ sun sets in the west.
There is only one sun, so the definite article the is used before it.
The definite article is also used with unique things such as the moon, the earth and the sky.
Which pillar of Islam was made obligatory on the night of Mairaj (Meraj)?
The five daily prayers were ordered by Allah during the night journey (Mairaj) of the Holy Prophet (PBUH). At first fifty prayers were prescribed, and this was reduced to five.
Mairaj is dated by tradition to 27 Rajab.
In which year was the Shimla Agreement between Pakistan and India signed?
The Shimla Agreement was signed on 2 July 1972 by Zulfikar Ali Bhutto and Indira Gandhi.
It converted the ceasefire line of Kashmir into the Line of Control.
Under the Constitution of Pakistan, what is the official name of the Parliament of Pakistan?
Article 50 of the Constitution says the Parliament consists of the President and the two Houses, the National Assembly and the Senate, and it is called Majlis-e-Shoora (Parliament).
The two houses of the Majlis-e-Shoora are the National Assembly and the Senate.
In which direction of Pakistan does the port city of Gwadar lie?
Gwadar lies on the Arabian Sea coast in the south-west corner of Pakistan in the province of Balochistan.
Pakistan purchased Gwadar from the Sultan of Oman in 1958.
Which type of triangle has all three sides of different lengths?
A scalene triangle has no two sides equal, while an isosceles triangle has two equal sides and an equilateral triangle has three equal sides.
The angles of a scalene triangle are also all different.
According to the Holy Quran, which religion is accepted by Allah Almighty as the true religion?
Surah Al-Imran (3:19) says that the religion in the sight of Allah is Islam.
Surah Al-Imran is the 3rd surah of the Quran and has 200 verses.
On what date did Pakistan and India sign the Lahore Declaration?
The Lahore Declaration was signed by Nawaz Sharif and Atal Bihari Vajpayee on 21 February 1999 at Lahore.
Vajpayee travelled to Lahore on the inaugural Delhi-Lahore bus service.

Cosec, sec and cot are the reciprocals of sin, cos and tan.

Cosine is an even function, so cos(-y) = cos y.
Which tense is normally used with the words 'since' and 'for' (for example, 'I have lived here since 2010')?

'Since' and 'for' show how long an action or state has continued up to now, which is expressed by the present perfect (or present perfect continuous) tense. Example: She has worked here for five years.
'Since' is used with a point in time and 'for' with a length of time.
In which year did Sir Syed Ahmad Khan die?
Sir Syed Ahmad Khan died at Aligarh on 27 March 1898.
He was born in 1817, so he lived about 80 years.
Which province of Pakistan is the largest by area?
Balochistan covers about 347,000 square kilometres, nearly 44 percent of Pakistan.
Punjab is the largest province by population.
About how many soldiers did the Quraish army have in the Battle of Badr?
The Quraish army at Badr (2 AH) numbered about 1000 men, against about 313 Muslims.
At Uhud the Quraish had about 3000 soldiers.
About how many soldiers were in the Muslim army at the Battle of Uhud when the fighting began?
The Muslims set out with about 1000, but around 300 hypocrites led by Abdullah bin Ubayy returned, leaving about 700 men.
The Battle of Uhud took place in 3 AH (625 CE).
Which type of brackets is used to write a solution set?
Sets, including solution sets, are written inside curly brackets, for example {2, 3}.
Round and square brackets are used for intervals.
Solve the proportion 2 : x :: 14 : 28. What is x?
In a proportion the product of extremes equals the product of means: 2 x 28 = x x 14. So 56 = 14x and x = 4.
A proportion a : b :: c : d means a/b = c/d.
Solve the proportion 8 : 4 :: X : 16. What is X?
Subtract 2x from both sides: x - 9 = 7. Add 9: x = 16.
Add x and 9 to both sides: 4x = 18, so x = 18/4 = 9/2 = 4.5.
Who was the son of Hazrat Sarah (AS), the wife of Hazrat Ibrahim (AS)?
Hazrat Sarah was the mother of Hazrat Ishaq (AS), born when she was very old.
Hazrat Ismail (AS) was the son of Hazrat Hajra.
The sound of which animal is mentioned in the Quran as the most unpleasant of sounds?
Surah Luqman (31:19) says the harshest of sounds is surely the braying of the donkey.
This verse is part of Luqman's advice to his son to lower his voice.
When was the Soviet Union (USSR) established?
The USSR was formally created on 30 December 1922 by the union of Russian, Ukrainian, Belarusian and Transcaucasian republics.
Iqbal's famous 1930 speech at the annual session of the All India Muslim League is known as which address?
Allama Iqbal delivered his Presidential Address at Allahabad in December 1930. In it he proposed a separate Muslim state in north-west India.
The Allahabad Address is considered the intellectual root of the Pakistan idea.
What is the last sermon of the Holy Prophet (SAW) called?
The Prophet (SAW) delivered his final sermon during the Farewell Hajj at Arafat. It is called Khutbah Hajjat-ul-Wida.
The Farewell Hajj took place in 10 AH.
A car runs at 60 km/hr and a train runs at twice the speed of the car. What is the speed of the train?
Train speed = 2 x 60 = 120 km/hr. Speed does not change with the time taken, so it is still 120 km/hr after 30 minutes.
In 30 minutes this train would cover 60 km.
What does OPAC stand for in library science?
OPAC means Online Public Access Catalogue. It is a computerised database that lets users search a library's holdings.
It replaced the traditional card catalogue.
Fill in the blank: She arrived ___ the station.
We use the preposition at with a specific point or place such as a station. So the sentence is: She arrived at the station.
We use arrive in for large places such as cities and countries.
After which battle did the Quraysh stop their attacks on Madina, as the Prophet (SAW) said they would no longer attack?
After the failed siege of Madina in the Battle of Khandaq (Ahzab) in 5 AH, the Prophet (SAW) said that the Quraysh would not attack again and the Muslims would march against them.
The Battle of Khandaq was won mainly by the trench dug on the advice of Salman Farsi (RA).
The graphical representation of which type of equation is a straight line?
A linear equation such as y = mx + c has degree one in its variables. Its graph is always a straight line.
A quadratic equation gives a parabola.
Which word is closest in meaning to 'strange'?
Strange means unusual or unexpected, and odd has the same meaning. The other options mean the opposite.
Other synonyms of strange are peculiar and queer.
How many Muslim soldiers marched in the army for the Ghazwa of Tabuk?
The Prophet (SAW) led about 30,000 Muslim fighters to Tabuk in 9 AH. It was the largest Muslim army up to that time.
The campaign is also called the Army of Hardship (Jaish-ul-Usrah).
What is the central subject of the Holy Quran?
The Quran is a book of guidance addressed to mankind. Its main subject is man and his success in this world and the Hereafter.
The Quran has 114 surahs and 30 paras.
Subversion means an attempt to weaken or overthrow an established authority from within. Undermining carries the same sense.
Which prophet is famous in Islamic tradition for suffering the longest illness with patience?
Hazrat Ayub (AS) suffered a long illness and loss of wealth and remained patient. He is the symbol of sabr.
The Quran mentions his prayer in Surah Al-Anbiya and Surah Sad.
Who was the first Pakistani to reach the summit of K2?
Ashraf Aman reached the summit of K2 in 1977 as part of a Japanese-led expedition.
Nazir Sabir was the first Pakistani to climb Mount Everest, in 2000, and sources differ slightly on the exact K2 summit date in August 1977.
If the 2nd day of a month is Sunday, what day is the 16th of that month?
From the 2nd to the 16th is 14 days, which is exactly two weeks. So the 16th falls on the same day as the 2nd, Sunday.
Dates that differ by a multiple of 7 always fall on the same weekday.
What is the meaning of the name of Surah Al-Ankabut?
Ankabut means spider, and the surah is named after the spider's web used as an example in it.
Al-Ankabut is the 29th surah of the Quran.
Which two surahs are known as Muawwazatain?
Surah Al-Falaq and Surah An-Nas are called Muawwidhatayn because they seek refuge in Allah.
They are the last two surahs of the Quran, 113 and 114.
What is the capital of Sweden?
Stockholm is the capital and largest city of Sweden.
Sweden is a Scandinavian country in northern Europe.
Which word is closest in meaning (a synonym) to "abate"?
To abate means to become less intense, which is to subside.
Which word is closest in meaning (a synonym) to "acquiesce"?
To acquiesce is to accept or go along with something without protest, so comply is closest.
Which word is closest in meaning (a synonym) to "acquisition"?
An acquisition is something gained or bought, close to purchase.
Companies use the word for takeovers.
Which word is closest in meaning (a synonym) to "awful"?
Awful means very bad, same as terrible.
The word originally meant inspiring awe.
Which word is closest in meaning (a synonym) to "brute"?
A brute is a savage or cruel creature, so beast is closest.
Which word is closest in meaning (a synonym) to "exceptional"?
Exceptional means unusually good or rare, like extraordinary.
Which word is closest in meaning (a synonym) to "irksome"?
Irksome means causing irritation, so annoying is closest.
Which word is closest in meaning (a synonym) to "magistrate"?
A magistrate is a civil officer who acts as a judge in lower courts.
In Pakistan, judicial magistrates hear minor criminal cases.
Which word is closest in meaning (a synonym) to "puzzled"?
Puzzled means confused, the same as perplexed.
Which word is closest in meaning (a synonym) to "voyage"?
A voyage is a long journey, especially by sea.
Bon voyage means have a good trip.
Which word is closest in meaning (a synonym) to "wield"?
To wield is to hold and use something such as a tool or power, so handle is closest.
One can wield a sword or wield influence.
Approximately how many Muslim soldiers took part in the Ghazwa (Battle) of Tabuk?
The Prophet (SAW) led about 30,000 Muslims to Tabuk, the largest Muslim army up to that time.
It took place in 9 AH and no fighting actually occurred.
What is the capital of Tajikistan?
Dushanbe is the capital and largest city of Tajikistan.
Tajikistan borders Afghanistan, China, Kyrgyzstan and Uzbekistan.
A man travels towards the north and then turns to his left. In which direction is he now facing?
Facing north, a left turn points to the west.
A right turn from north would point to the east.
Ali moves towards the north, then turns left, and after moving turns right. In which direction is he now facing?
North then left gives west, and a right turn from west gives north.
Two opposite turns cancel each other out.
If 1 km takes 100 minutes, how many km can be covered in 12 minutes at the same rate?
Rate is 1/100 km per minute, so in 12 minutes the distance is 12 x 1/100 = 0.12 km.
Distance equals speed multiplied by time.
Which of the following was NOT among the Ashra Mubashra (the ten Companions given glad tidings of Paradise)?
Hazrat Talha is one of the ten given the glad tidings of Paradise, while Hazrat Zaid bin Haritha (RA) is not on that list.
The ten include the four Rightly Guided Caliphs, Talha, Zubair, Abdur Rahman bin Auf, Saad bin Abi Waqqas, Saeed bin Zaid and Abu Ubaidah bin Jarrah.
Which is the tallest building in Pakistan?
Bahria Icon Tower in Karachi is generally listed as Pakistan's tallest building, though its stated height varies by source (about 273 to 300 metres).
Habib Bank Plaza was long considered the tallest before the Icon Tower was built.
Tarbela Dam is located in which district and province of Pakistan?
Tarbela Dam is built on the River Indus near Tarbela in Haripur district of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.
It is the largest earth-filled dam in the world.
How many farz (obligatory acts) does Tayammum have according to the Hanafi school?
The three farz of Tayammum are making the intention, striking the hands on clean earth and wiping the face, and wiping both arms up to the elbows.
Tayammum is performed when water is not available or cannot be used.
On which date is International Tea Day observed?
The United Nations designated 21 May as International Tea Day, first observed in 2020.
Earlier, tea-producing countries had celebrated an International Tea Day on 15 December.
A soldier's mother ____ her emotions as he left for the front. Choose the correct word.
The phrasal verb 'bottled up' means kept feelings hidden, and 'teared' is not the right form in this sense.
'Bottle up' is the phrasal verb; the past tense is 'bottled up'.
What is 20% of one tenth of 90?
One tenth of 90 is 9, and 20% of 9 is 1.8.
20% is the same as one fifth.
Multiplying by one tenth moves the decimal point one place left.
What is one third of one tenth of 9?
One tenth of 9 is 0.9 and one third of 0.9 is 0.3.
Which prophet was tested by Allah with a long illness and is known for his patience?
Hazrat Ayyub (AS) suffered a long illness and loss of wealth yet stayed patient, so he is a symbol of sabr.
The Quran mentions his story in Surah Al-Anbiya and Surah Sad.
What is cosec theta equal to?
Cosecant is the reciprocal of sine, so cosec theta = 1 / sin theta.
Sec theta is 1 / cos theta and cot theta is 1 / tan theta.
In a right-angled triangle, sin theta is equal to which ratio?
Sine of an angle is the length of the opposite side (perpendicular) divided by the hypotenuse.
Cos theta is base / hypotenuse and tan theta is perpendicular / base.
Which is the third surah of the Holy Quran?
The order is Al-Fatiha, Al-Baqarah, Al-Imran, so the third surah is Al-Imran.
A number whose three times is 6 has 2 added to it. What is the result?
If 3 times the number is 6, the number is 2. Adding 2 gives 2 + 2 = 4.
The candidate answer 2 is only the number itself, not the final result.
Through which point does the line y = 6x pass?
Putting x = 0 gives y = 0, so the line passes through the origin (0, 0).
A line of the form y = mx always passes through the origin.
Watch is to time as barometer is to what?
A watch measures time and a barometer measures atmospheric pressure.
A thermometer measures temperature and an anemometer measures wind speed.
What was the approximate age of the Holy Prophet (PBUH) at the time of the Fujjar war?
The Fujjar war was fought in the sacred months and the young Prophet (PBUH) took part by handing arrows to his uncles at about the age of 15 years.
Some narrations give an age between 14 and 20 years, so sources differ slightly; 15 is the common textbook answer.
Tipu Sultan was killed defending Seringapatam against the British in the Fourth Anglo-Mysore War on 4 May 1799.
The Treaty of Seringapatam in 1792 ended the Third Anglo-Mysore War.
Which title is used for Hazrat Abu Bakr Siddiq (RA)?
Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA) is known by the title Attiq, meaning freed from the fire of Hell, besides Siddiq.
Farooq is the title of Hazrat Umar (RA) and Murtaza of Hazrat Ali (RA).
Habibullah (beloved of Allah) is the title of whom?
Habibullah is a famous title of the Holy Prophet Muhammad (PBUH).
If today is Friday, what day will it be after 14 days?
14 days is exactly 2 weeks, so the day is the same: Friday.
Any multiple of 7 days brings the same weekday.
If today is Monday, what day will it be after 5 days?
Counting 5 days after Monday gives Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday, Saturday.
Saturday and Sunday form the weekend.
What is the line that touches a circle at exactly one point called?
A tangent touches the circle at exactly one point, while a secant cuts it at two points.
A tangent is perpendicular to the radius at the point of contact.
How many tournaments make up the Grand Slam in tennis?
The four Grand Slam tennis tournaments are the Australian Open, French Open, Wimbledon and US Open.
Wimbledon is the oldest of the four.
Aslam walks towards the north, then turns left and then turns right. In which direction is he facing now?
Facing north, a left turn makes him face west and a right turn then brings him back to face north.
Left and right turns cancel each other out.
Which province of Pakistan first issued driving licences to transgender persons (in 2018)?
Khyber Pakhtunkhwa traffic police formally issued driving licences to transgender persons in March 2018.
Islamabad issued a licence to Laila Ali in November 2018; sources differ on what counts as first.
What is the transpose of a row matrix called?
Transposing swaps rows and columns, so a 1 by n row matrix becomes an n by 1 column matrix.
The transpose of a square matrix is also a square matrix.
What was the Treaty of Amritsar (1846) about?
Sale of Kashmir by the British to Gulab Singh
End of the First Anglo-Sikh War handing Punjab to the Mughals
Under the Treaty of Amritsar the British sold Kashmir to Gulab Singh Dogra for 7.5 million rupees.
It followed the First Anglo-Sikh War and created the princely state of Jammu and Kashmir.
In which Hijri year was Hazrat Usman (RA) martyred?
Hazrat Usman (RA), the third caliph, was besieged in his house and martyred in Dhul Hijjah 35 AH (656 CE).
He was succeeded as caliph by Hazrat Ali (RA).
If 8 : 4 :: X : 16, what is the value of X?
8 : 4 is the ratio 2 : 1, so X : 16 must also be 2 : 1. Hence X = 16 x 2 = 32.
In a proportion a : b :: c : d, the product of the extremes equals the product of the means (a x d = b x c).
If x = (1/3) y and y = 9, what is the value of x?
Multiplying by 1/3 is the same as dividing by 3.
If Y = 4x - 2 and x = 2, what is the value of Y?
Multiplication is done before subtraction in the order of operations.
If y = 2x - 1 and x = 2, what is the value of y?
Substitution means replacing a variable by its given value.
What comes next in the series Z1, Y2, X3, ...?
The letters move backwards through the alphabet (Z, Y, X, W) while the numbers go up by 1 (1, 2, 3, 4). So the next term is W4.
Letter pairs like this often combine a reverse alphabet with an increasing number.
On what date was the Treaty of Versailles signed?
The Treaty of Versailles was signed on 28 June 1919 in the Hall of Mirrors at the Palace of Versailles.
It came into force on 10 January 1920, the same day the League of Nations first met.
What was the Treaty of Versailles?
A peace treaty ending World War I with Germany
A treaty ending World War II
An alliance between Britain and France
A treaty founding the United Nations
The Treaty of Versailles was the peace settlement between Germany and the Allied Powers after World War I.
It forced Germany to accept war guilt, pay reparations and lose territory.
According to the commonly accepted count, how many verses (ayat) does the Holy Quran have?
The Hafs count most widely followed gives 6236 verses across 114 surahs.
Counts differ slightly between recitation traditions; 6666 is a popular but not the standard figure.
Fill in the blank: He was very grateful that he ----- my computer promptly.
The sentence is in the past tense (was grateful), so the past tense repaired is correct.
Tense should stay consistent between the clauses of a sentence.
Who was the last Viceroy of British India?
Lord Mountbatten served as the last Viceroy from March to August 1947 and then became the first Governor-General of independent India.
In which year did Prime Minister Liaquat Ali Khan make his official visit to the United States?
Liaquat Ali Khan visited the USA in May 1950 at the invitation of President Truman.
This visit is seen as the start of close Pakistan-US relations.
Which party won the most seats and votes in the 1970 general elections of Pakistan?
The Awami League led by Sheikh Mujibur Rahman won 160 of the 300 general seats in the National Assembly, almost all in East Pakistan.
The PPP of Z. A. Bhutto came second, winning 81 seats, all in West Pakistan.
How many vowels are in the letter string AEDIPOUDLEC (Aedipoudlec)?
The vowels are A, E, I, O, U, E, which makes 6.
The English vowels are A, E, I, O and U.
How many vowels are in AZPQTVSJFIU?
The vowels are A, I and U, giving 3.
The English vowels are A, E, I, O and U.
How many vowels are in AdebccTEvIxyz?
The vowels are A, e, E and I, giving 4.
Capital and small letters count equally.
Wakhan Corridor border meets which country, separating Pakistan from it?
The narrow Wakhan Corridor of Afghanistan separates Pakistan from Tajikistan.
It also touches China at its eastern end.
Ali was walking towards north. He turned left, walked on, then turned right and again turned left. In which direction is he now facing?
Facing north, a left turn gives west; a right turn from west gives north; a left turn from north gives west again.
A left turn is a quarter turn anticlockwise and a right turn is a quarter turn clockwise.
What is the walking between the hills of Safa and Marwa called in Hajj and Umrah?
Sai is the seven-fold walking between Safa and Marwa, in remembrance of Hazrat Hajra (RA) searching for water for Ismail (AS).
The Zamzam spring emerged during that event.
Which country does India import the largest share of its weapons from, according to SIPRI data?
SIPRI data show Russia as India's largest arms supplier for 2020-24, with about 36 percent of India's imports. France is second.
Russia's share of Indian imports has fallen sharply from about 72 percent in 2010-14.
Choose the correct form of the sentence: Amna will have repair her bike by next week.
Amna will have repaired her bike by next week.
Amna will has repaired her bike by next week.
Amna will have repairing her bike by next week.
Amna will had repair her bike by next week.
The future perfect tense is formed with will have plus the past participle, so repair must become repaired.
The future perfect tense shows an action that will be completed before a stated time in the future.
If 10 men can dig a well in 5 days, how many days will 5 men take to dig it?
Total work = 10 x 5 = 50 man-days. With 5 men, days = 50 / 5 = 10 days.
Fewer workers need proportionally more time, which is called inverse proportion.
In which country is the White House located?
The White House stands at 1600 Pennsylvania Avenue in Washington, D.C., United States.
Construction of the White House began in 1792 and it was first occupied by President John Adams in 1800.
Which country is traditionally called the Land of the White Elephant?
Thailand (formerly Siam) is known by this name because white elephants were sacred and symbols of royal power there.
Sources differ slightly, as Myanmar and Laos have also been linked to white elephants, but Thailand is the textbook answer.
Which woman cricketer was the first Pakistani woman to take 100 ODI wickets?
Sana Mir reached 100 ODI wickets in February 2017 during the Women's World Cup Qualifier match against Bangladesh in Colombo.
Sana Mir finished her career with 151 ODI wickets and was inducted into the ICC Hall of Fame.
If the base of a triangle is 3 cm and its height is 6 cm, what is its area?
Area of a triangle = 1/2 x base x height = 1/2 x 3 x 6 = 9 square cm.
The question calls the second length width, but a triangle's area formula uses the height perpendicular to the base.
Which wife of the Holy Prophet (PBUH), when asked about his character, said that his character was the Quran?
Hazrat Ayesha (RA) replied that the character of the Prophet (PBUH) was the Quran, meaning he lived by it completely.
Hazrat Ayesha (RA) was the daughter of Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA) and narrated over 2000 hadiths.
Who won the seventh edition of the Pakistan Super League (PSL 7) in 2022?
Lahore Qalandars beat Multan Sultans by 42 runs in the final at Gaddafi Stadium, Lahore, on 27 February 2022.
It was the first PSL title for Lahore Qalandars, who also won PSL 8 in 2023.
Which team won the 2021 ICC Men's T20 World Cup?
Australia beat New Zealand by 8 wickets in the final in Dubai in November 2021 to win their first T20 World Cup.
Pakistan won the 2009 ICC T20 World Cup, and it reached the 2021 semi-final.
When are the articles a and an used?
A and an are indefinite articles used before singular countable nouns; a is used before a consonant sound and an before a vowel sound.
The article the is the definite article and can be used with singular, plural and uncountable nouns.
What is the main work of SUPARCO, Pakistan's national space agency?
SUPARCO stands for Space and Upper Atmosphere Research Commission, which runs Pakistan's space and satellite programme.
SUPARCO was established in 1961 and launched Pakistan's first rocket, Rehbar-I, in 1962.
What is the work of the angels Munkar and Nakir, according to Islamic belief?
Blowing the trumpet on the Day of Judgement
Questioning a person in the grave
Munkar and Nakir are the two angels who question a person in the grave about his Lord, his religion and his Prophet.
The angels who record deeds are Kiraman Katibin, who sit on each person's shoulders.
In which year did the Holy Prophet Hazrat Muhammad (PBUH) pass away?
The Holy Prophet (PBUH) passed away on 12 Rabi-ul-Awwal, 11 AH, which corresponds to June 632 CE, in Madina.
He was about 63 years old, and he was buried in the room of Hazrat Ayesha (RA).
If one man writes one paper in 5 minutes, how long does one man take to write one paper?
The question already states that he takes 5 minutes for one paper, so the answer is 5 minutes.
At this rate, he would write 12 papers in one hour.
Which famous book was written by Data Ganj Bakhsh (Hazrat Ali Hujwiri)?
Data Ganj Bakhsh wrote Kashf-ul-Mahjoob, one of the oldest Persian works on Sufism.
What does WWW stand for in internet addresses?
WWW stands for World Wide Web, the system of linked pages accessed over the internet.
The World Wide Web was invented by Tim Berners-Lee in 1989.
90% of 91 = 0.9 x 91 = 81.9. Equivalently, 10% of 91 is 9.1, and 91 minus 9.1 = 81.9.
Taking 90% of a number is the same as subtracting 10% of it.
90% of 99 = 0.9 x 99 = 89.1. Equivalently, 10% of 99 is 9.9, and 99 minus 9.9 = 89.1.
90% of 100 is 90, so 90% of 99 is 0.9 less than 90.
In set theory, what is n(A-B) equal to?
A-B contains the elements of A that are not in B. These are all elements of A except those common to both, so n(A-B) = n(A) - n(A intersection B).
The union formula is n(A union B) = n(A) + n(B) - n(A intersection B).
